South Carolina Science Academic Standards

65FF3450DFE70131A4A068A86D17958E.description: Infer explanations concerning the age of the universe and the age of Earth on the basis of scientific evidence.

65FED820DFE70131A49F68A86D17958E.description: Match dating methods (including index fossils, ordering of rock layers, and radiometric dating) with the most appropriate application for estimating geologic time.

65FE7930DFE70131A49E68A86D17958E.description: Summarize how fossil evidence reflects the changes in environmental conditions on Earth over time.

65FE1CA0DFE70131A49D68A86D17958E.description: Recall the divisions of the geologic time scale and illustrate the changes (in complexity and/or diversity) of organisms that have existed across these time units.

65FDADF0DFE70131A49C68A86D17958E.description: Summarize the conditions of Earth that enable the planet to support life.

65FD44B0DFE70131A49B68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the dynamic relationship between Earth's conditions over geologic time and the diversity of its organisms.

65FC7F00DFE70131A49968A86D17958E.description: Analyze environments to determine possible sources of water pollution (including industrial waste, agriculture, domestic waste, and transportation devices).

65FC2060DFE70131A49868A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of the transfer of solar energy and geothermal energy on the oceans of Earth (including the circulation of ocean currents and chemosynthesis).

65FBB340DFE70131A49768A86D17958E.description: Summarize the advantages and disadvantages of devices used to control and prevent coastal erosion and flooding.

65FB1D50DFE70131A49668A86D17958E.description: Explain the results of the interaction of the shore with waves and currents.

65FABAB0DFE70131A49568A86D17958E.description: Compare the physical and chemical properties of seawater and freshwater.

65FA5030DFE70131A49468A86D17958E.description: Explain how karst topography develops as a result of groundwater processes.

65F9E030DFE70131A49368A86D17958E.description: Illustrate the characteristics of the succession of river systems.

65F983A0DFE70131A49268A86D17958E.description: Summarize the location, movement, and energy transfers involved in the movement of water on Earth's surface (including lakes, surface-water drainage basins [watersheds], freshwater wetlands, and groundwater zones).

65F92840DFE70131A49168A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of Earth's freshwater and ocean systems.

65F85770DFE70131A48F68A86D17958E.description: Predict weather conditions and storms (including thunderstorms, hurricanes, and tornados) on the basis of the relationship among the movement of air masses, high and low pressure systems, and frontal boundaries.

65F7E280DFE70131A48E68A86D17958E.description: Summarize the evidence for the likely impact of human activities on the atmosphere (including ozone holes, greenhouse gases, acid rain, and photochemical smog).

65F78990DFE70131A48D68A86D17958E.description: Summarize possible causes of and evidence for past and present global climate changes.

65F73110DFE70131A48C68A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship between the rotation of Earth and the pattern of wind belts.

65F6D550DFE70131A48B68A86D17958E.description: Attribute global climate patterns to geographic influences (including latitude, topography, elevation, and proximity to water).

65F67420DFE70131A48A68A86D17958E.description: Summarize the cause and effects of convection within Earth's atmosphere.

65F617F0DFE70131A48968A86D17958E.description: Summarize the changes in Earth's atmosphere over geologic time (including the importance of photosynthesizing organisms to the atmosphere).

65F59E50DFE70131A48868A86D17958E.description: Summarize the thermal structures, the gaseous composition, and the location of the layers of Earth's atmosphere.

65F52A10DFE70131A48768A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the dynamics of Earth's atmosphere.

65F46880DFE70131A48568A86D17958E.description: Summarize the formation of ores and fossil fuels and the impact on the environment that the use of these fuels has had.

65F41090DFE70131A48468A86D17958E.description: Classify minerals and rocks on the basis of their physical and chemical properties and the environment in which they were formed.

65F3B7B0DFE70131A48368A86D17958E.description: Explain how the dynamic nature of the rock cycle accounts for the interrelationships among igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks.

65F35F50DFE70131A48268A86D17958E.description: Analyze surface features of Earth in order to identify geologic processes (including weathering, erosion, deposition, and glaciation) that are likely to have been responsible for their formation.

65F302E0DFE70131A48168A86D17958E.description: Explain how forces due to plate tectonics cause crustal changes as evidenced in earthquake activity, volcanic eruptions, and mountain building.

65F28E10DFE70131A48068A86D17958E.description: Summarize theory of plate tectonics (including the role of convection currents, the action at plate boundaries, and the scientific evidence for the theory).

65F22240DFE70131A47F68A86D17958E.description: Explain the differentiation of the structure of Earth's layers into a core, mantle, and crust based on the production of internal heat from the decay of isotopes and the role of gravitational energy.

65F1C580DFE70131A47E68A86D17958E.description: Summarize theories and evidence of the origin and formation of Earth's systems by using the concepts of gravitational force and heat production.

65F167A0DFE70131A47D68A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the internal and external dynamics of solid Earth.

65F0A2F0DFE70131A47B68A86D17958E.description: Explain how technology and computer modeling have increased our understanding of the universe.

65F044E0DFE70131A47A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how gravity and motion affect the formation and shapes of galaxies (including the Milky Way).

65EFDEC0DFE70131A47968A86D17958E.description: Summarize the life cycles of stars.

65EF60B0DFE70131A47868A86D17958E.description: Compare the information obtained through the use of x-ray, radio, and visual (reflecting and refracting) telescopes.

65EF0670DFE70131A47768A86D17958E.description: Classify stars by using the Hertzsprung-Russell diagram.

65EEA620DFE70131A47668A86D17958E.description: Explain the formation of elements that results from nuclear fusion occurring within stars or supernova explosions.

65EE5040DFE70131A47568A86D17958E.description: Summarize the evidence that supports the big bang theory and the expansion of the universe (including the red shift of light from distant galaxies and the cosmic background radiation).

65EDF860DFE70131A47468A86D17958E.description: Identify properties and features of the Moon that make it unique among other moons in the solar system.

65ED9FB0DFE70131A47368A86D17958E.description: Summarize the properties of the solar system that support the theory of its formation along with the planets.

65ED4280DFE70131A47268A86D17958E.description: Students will demonstrate an understanding of the structure and properties of the universe.

65EC8390DFE70131A47068A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate safety procedures when conducting investigations.

65EC2920DFE70131A46F68A86D17958E.description: Communicate and defend a scientific argument or conclusion.

65EBCB80DFE70131A46E68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a technological design or product on the basis of designated criteria (including cost, time, and materials).

65EB6DC0DFE70131A46D68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate conclusions based on qualitative and quantitative data (including the impact of parallax, instrument malfunction, or human error) on experimental results.

65EAF7F0DFE70131A46C68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the results of a controlled scientific investigation in terms of whether they refute or verify the hypothesis.

65EA8F00DFE70131A46B68A86D17958E.description: Organize and interpret the data from a controlled scientific investigation by using mathematics (including calculations in scientific notation, formulas, and dimensional analysis), graphs, tables, models, diagrams, and/or technology.

65EA19C0DFE70131A46A68A86D17958E.description: Design a scientific investigation with appropriate methods of control to test a hypothesis (including independent and dependent variables), and evaluate the designs of sample investigations.

65E9BC40DFE70131A46968A86D17958E.description: Use scientific instruments to record measurement data in appropriate metric units that reflect the precision and accuracy of each particular instrument.

65E95F40DFE70131A46868A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate laboratory apparatuses, technology, and techniques safely and accurately when conducting a scientific investigation.

65E8F960DFE70131A46768A86D17958E.description: Apply established rules for significant digits, both in reading scientific instruments and in calculating derived quantities from measurement.

65E89FD0DFE70131A46668A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of how scientific inquiry and technological design, including mathematical analysis, can be used appropriately to pose questions, seek answers, and develop solutions.

65E78B20DFE70131A46368A86D17958E.description: Summarize the functioning of heat transfer mechanisms (including engines and refrigeration systems).

65E726E0DFE70131A46268A86D17958E.description: Apply the concepts of heat capacity, specific heat, and heat exchange to solve calorimetry problems.

65E6CD40DFE70131A46168A86D17958E.description: Summarize the concepts involved in phase change.

65E66BC0DFE70131A46068A86D17958E.description: Differentiate heat and temperature in terms of molecular motion.

65E604C0DFE70131A45F68A86D17958E.description: Explain thermal expansion in solids, liquids, and gases in terms of kinetic theory and the unique behavior of water.

65E51990DFE70131A45D68A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship among internal energy, heat, and work.

65E4BD00DFE70131A45C68A86D17958E.description: Summarize the first and second laws of thermodynamics.

65E45760DFE70131A45B68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the principles of thermodynamics.

65E3FC30DFE70131A45A68A86D17958E.description: Exemplify the relationship between velocity and pressure by using Bernoulli's principle.

65E3A020DFE70131A45968A86D17958E.description: Apply fluid formulas to solve problems involving work and power.

65E340B0DFE70131A45868A86D17958E.description: Explain how depth and fluid density affect pressure.

65E2E910DFE70131A45768A86D17958E.description: Explain how the rate of flow of a fluid is affected by the size of the pipe, friction, and the viscosity of the fluid.

65E29240DFE70131A45668A86D17958E.description: Explain the factors that affect buoyancy.

65E23A80DFE70131A45568A86D17958E.description: Apply appropriate procedures to solve problems involving pressure, force, volume, and area.

65E1D8B0DFE70131A45468A86D17958E.description: Predict the behavior of fluids (including changing forces) in pneumatic and hydraulic systems.

65E170F0DFE70131A45368A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the principles of fluid mechanics.

65E10CC0DFE70131A45268A86D17958E.description: Compare the value of time, length, and momentum in the reference frame of an object moving at relativistic velocity to those values measured in the reference frame of an observer by applying Einstein's special theory of relativity.

65E0A280DFE70131A45168A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship between mass and energy that is represented in the equation E = mc² according to Einstein's special theory of relativity.

65E038D0DFE70131A45068A86D17958E.description: Interpret a representative nuclear decay series.

65DFD530DFE70131A44F68A86D17958E.description: Apply appropriate procedures to balance nuclear equations (including fusion, fission, alpha decay, beta decay, and electron capture).

65DF7150DFE70131A44E68A86D17958E.description: Predict the resulting isotope of a given alpha, beta, or gamma emission.

65DF1490DFE70131A44D68A86D17958E.description: Compare the nuclear binding energy to the energy released during a nuclear reaction, given the atomic masses of the constituent particles.

65DEB030DFE70131A44C68A86D17958E.description: Compare the strong and weak nuclear forces in terms of their roles in radioactivity.

65DE5590DFE70131A44B68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of nuclear physics and modern physics.

65DDF7B0DFE70131A44A68A86D17958E.description: Identify the parts of the eye and explain their function in image formation.

65DD9070DFE70131A44968A86D17958E.description: Illustrate the diffraction and interference of light.

65DD30C0DFE70131A44868A86D17958E.description: Compare color mixing in pigments to color mixing in light.

comments: The skills of scientific inquiry, including a knowledge of the use of tools, will be assessed cumulatively on statewide tests. 65A7FD20DFE70131A3BE68A86D17958E.description: Explain the Doppler effect conceptually in terms of the frequency of the waves and the pitch of the sound.

65A79B90DFE70131A3BD68A86D17958E.description: Summarize reflection and interference of both sound and light waves and the refraction and diffraction of light waves.

65A73450DFE70131A3BC68A86D17958E.description: Summarize the characteristics of the electromagnetic spectrum (including range of wavelengths, frequency, energy, and propagation without a medium).

65A6D480DFE70131A3BB68A86D17958E.description: Use the formulas v = f λ and v = d/t to solve problems related to the velocity of waves.

65A66480DFE70131A3BA68A86D17958E.description: Summarize characteristics of waves (including displacement, frequency, period, amplitude, wavelength, and velocity as well as the relationships among these characteristics).

65A5FDB0DFE70131A3B968A86D17958E.description: Compare the nature and properties of transverse and longitudinal/compressional mechanical waves.

65A58E80DFE70131A3B868A86D17958E.description: Illustrate ways that the energy of waves is transferred by interaction with matter (including transverse and longitudinal/compressional waves).

65A534C0DFE70131A3B768A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the nature and properties of mechanical and electromagnetic waves.

65A4DA50DFE70131A3B668A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship of magnetism to the movement of electric charges in electromagnets, simple motors, and generators.

65A47D60DFE70131A3B568A86D17958E.description: Compare alternating current (AC) and direct current (DC) in terms of the production of electricity and the direction of current flow.

65A42000DFE70131A3B468A86D17958E.description: Compare the functioning of simple series and parallel electrical circuits.

65A3A9D0DFE70131A3B368A86D17958E.description: Represent an electric circuit by drawing a circuit diagram that includes the symbols for a resistor, switch, and voltage source.

65A32BB0DFE70131A3B268A86D17958E.description: Use the formula V = IR to solve problems related to electric circuits.

65A2CD70DFE70131A3B168A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationships among voltage, resistance, and current in Ohm's law.

65A274A0DFE70131A3B068A86D17958E.description: Explain how objects can acquire a static electric charge through friction, induction, and conduction.

65A21A00DFE70131A3AF68A86D17958E.description: Use the formula W = Fd to solve problems related to work done on an object.

65A1B970DFE70131A3AE68A86D17958E.description: Explain work in terms of the relationship among the force applied to an object, the displacement of the object, and the energy transferred to the object.

65A15FC0DFE70131A3AD68A86D17958E.description: Explain the factors that determine potential and kinetic energy and the transformation of one to the other.

65A10180DFE70131A3AC68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the law of conservation of energy applies to the transformation of various forms of energy (including mechanical energy, electrical energy, chemical energy, light energy, sound energy, and thermal energy).

65A0A4B0DFE70131A3AB68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the nature, conservation, and transformation of energy.

65A049E0DFE70131A3AA68A86D17958E.description: Explain how the gravitational force between two objects is affected by the mass of each object and the distance between them.

659FEC90DFE70131A3A968A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship between mass and weight by using the formula F<sub>W</sub> = ma<sub>g</sub>.

659F94C0DFE70131A3A868A86D17958E.description: Use the formula F = ma to solve problems related to force.

659F3A90DFE70131A3A768A86D17958E.description: Explain the motion of objects on the basis of Newton's three laws of motion: inertia; the relationship among force, mass, and acceleration; and action and reaction forces.

659EE1B0DFE70131A3A668A86D17958E.description: Represent the linear motion of objects on distance-time graphs.

659E8200DFE70131A3A568A86D17958E.description: Explain how acceleration due to gravity affects the velocity of an object as it falls.

659E1A90DFE70131A3A468A86D17958E.description: Use the formula a = (v<sub>f</sub>-v<sub>i</sub>)/t to determine the acceleration of an object.

659DC220DFE70131A3A368A86D17958E.description: Explain how changes in velocity and time affect the acceleration of an object.

659D6A10DFE70131A3A268A86D17958E.description: Use the formula v = d/t to solve problems related to average speed or velocity.

659D1030DFE70131A3A168A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationship among distance, time, direction, and the velocity of an object.

659CB040DFE70131A3A068A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the nature of forces and motion.

659C4510DFE70131A39F68A86D17958E.description: Physics: The Interactions of Matter and Energy

659BD8F0DFE70131A39E68A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of temperature, concentration, surface area, and the presence of a catalyst on reaction rates.

659B63F0DFE70131A39D68A86D17958E.description: Recognize simple chemical equations (including single replacement and double replacement) as being balanced or not balanced.

659AEEC0DFE70131A39C68A86D17958E.description: Apply a procedure to balance equations for a simple synthesis or decomposition reaction.

659A8750DFE70131A39B68A86D17958E.description: Summarize evidence (including the evolution of gas; the formation of a precipitate; and/or changes in temperature, color, and/or odor) that a chemical reaction has occurred.

659A2C30DFE70131A39A68A86D17958E.description: Summarize characteristics of balanced chemical equations (including conservation of mass and changes in energy in the form of heat—that is, exothermic or endothermic reactions).

6599D080DFE70131A39968A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between chemical changes (including the formation of gas or reactivity with acids) and physical changes (including changes in size, shape, color, and/or phase).

659977F0DFE70131A39868A86D17958E.description: Predict the ratio by which the representative elements combine to form binary ionic compounds, and represent that ratio in a chemical formula.

65991700DFE70131A39768A86D17958E.description: Classify compounds as crystalline (containing ionic bonds) or molecular (containing covalent bonds) based on whether their outer electrons are transferred or shared.

6598AC40DFE70131A39668A86D17958E.description: Illustrate the fact that ions attract ions of opposite charge from all directions and form crystal lattices.

659854C0DFE70131A39568A86D17958E.description: Explain how the process of covalent bonding provides chemical stability through the sharing of electrons.

6597FAB0DFE70131A39468A86D17958E.description: Explain the role of bonding in achieving chemical stability.

65979DE0DFE70131A39368A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of chemical reactions and the classifications, structures, and properties of chemical compounds.

659736B0DFE70131A39268A86D17958E.description: Classify various solutions as acids or bases according to their physical properties, chemical properties (including neutralization and reaction with metals), generalized formulas, and pH (using pH meters, pH paper, and litmus paper).

6596C2A0DFE70131A39168A86D17958E.description: Explain the processes of phase change in terms of temperature, heat transfer, and particle arrangement.

65965770DFE70131A39068A86D17958E.description: Compare the properties of the four states of matter—solid, liquid, gas, and plasma—in terms of the arrangement and movement of particles.

6595F710DFE70131A38F68A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of temperature, particle size, and agitation on the rate at which a solid dissolves in a liquid.

65959770DFE70131A38E68A86D17958E.description: Classify matter as a pure substance (either an element or a compound) or as a mixture (either homogeneous or heterogeneous) on the basis of its structure and/or composition.

659522B0DFE70131A38D68A86D17958E.description: Illustrate the difference between a molecule and an atom.

6594C800DFE70131A38C68A86D17958E.description: Infer the practical applications of organic and inorganic substances on the basis of their chemical and physical properties.

65946B20DFE70131A38B68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish chemical properties of matter (including reactivity) from physical properties of matter (including boiling point, freezing/melting point, density [with density calculations], solubility, viscosity, and conductivity).

65940A10DFE70131A38A68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of various properties and classifications of matter.

65939900DFE70131A38968A86D17958E.description: Explain the consequences that the use of nuclear applications (including medical technologies, nuclear power plants, and nuclear weapons) can have.

65933850DFE70131A38868A86D17958E.description: Compare fission and fusion (including the basic processes and the fact that both fission and fusion convert a fraction of the mass of interacting particles into energy and release a great amount of energy).

6592DD80DFE70131A38768A86D17958E.description: Predict the charge that a representative element will acquire according to the arrangement of electrons in its outer energy level.

659280C0DFE70131A38668A86D17958E.description: Use the atomic number and the mass number to calculate the number of protons, neutrons, and/or electrons for a given isotope of an element.

65921F50DFE70131A38568A86D17958E.description: Explain the trends of the periodic table based on the elements' valence electrons and atomic numbers.

6591B440DFE70131A38468A86D17958E.description: Illustrate the fact that the atoms of elements exist as stable or unstable isotopes.

65914150DFE70131A38368A86D17958E.description: Compare the subatomic particles (protons, neutrons, electrons) of an atom with regard to mass, location, and charge, and explain how these particles affect the properties of an atom (including identity, mass, volume, and reactivity).

6590E960DFE70131A38268A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the structure and properties of atoms.

65909310DFE70131A38168A86D17958E.description: Chemistry: Structure and Properties of Matter

659039F0DFE70131A38068A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate safety procedures when conducting investigations.

658FD720DFE70131A37F68A86D17958E.description: Compare the processes of scientific investigation and technological design.

658F5AF0DFE70131A37E68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a technological design or product on the basis of designated criteria (including cost, time, and materials).

658F05E0DFE70131A37D68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the results of a controlled scientific investigation in terms of whether they refute or verify the hypothesis.

658EB030DFE70131A37C68A86D17958E.description: Organize and interpret the data from a controlled scientific investigation by using mathematics (including formulas and dimensional analysis), graphs, models, and/or technology.

658E5750DFE70131A37B68A86D17958E.description: Design a scientific investigation with appropriate methods of control to test a hypothesis (including independent and dependent variables), and evaluate the designs of sample investigations.

658DFAA0DFE70131A37A68A86D17958E.description: Use scientific instruments to record measurement data in appropriate metric units that reflect the precision and accuracy of each particular instrument.

658D96F0DFE70131A37968A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate laboratory apparatuses, technology, and techniques safely and accurately when conducting a scientific investigation.

658D3E70DFE70131A37868A86D17958E.description: Generate hypotheses on the basis of credible, accurate, and relevant sources of scientific information.

658CDE50DFE70131A37768A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of how scientific inquiry and technological design, including mathematical analysis, can be used appropriately to pose questions, seek answers, and develop solutions.

document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards for English Language Arts

5F673D40DFE701319A3C68A86D17958E.description: Design and carry out research projects by selecting a topic, constructing inquiry questions, accessing resources, and organizing information.

5F66EC70DFE701319A3B68A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of print and electronic reference materials.

5F6682D0DFE701319A3A68A86D17958E.description: Select appropriate graphics, in print or electronic form, to support written works, oral presentations, and visual presentations.

5F662C10DFE701319A3968A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate organizational strategies to prepare written works, oral and auditory presentations, and visual presentations.

5F65CAF0DFE701319A3868A86D17958E.description: Use vocabulary (including Standard American English) that is appropriate for the particular audience or purpose.

5F658800DFE701319A3768A86D17958E.description: Use a standardized system of documentation (for example, a list of sources with full publication information and the use of intext citations) to properly credit the work of others.

5F6540F0DFE701319A3668A86D17958E.description: Use direct quotations, paraphrasing, or summaries to incorporate into written, oral, auditory, or visual works the information gathered from a variety of research sources.

5F64FF50DFE701319A3568A86D17958E.description: Clarify and refine a research topic.

5F64BA40DFE701319A3468A86D17958E.description: The student will access and use information from a variety of sources.

5F645DF0DFE701319A3368A86D17958E.description: Applying the Skills of Inquiry and Oral Communication

5F63B0D0DFE701319A3168A86D17958E.description: Create persuasive writings (for example, print advertisements and commercial scripts) that develop a central idea with supporting evidence and use language appropriate for the specific audience.

5F636D90DFE701319A3068A86D17958E.description: Create written descriptions using precise language and vivid details.

5F632E20DFE701319A2F68A86D17958E.description: Create narratives that have a fully developed plot and a consistent point of view.

5F62EC40DFE701319A2E68A86D17958E.description: Create informational pieces (for example, brochures, pamphlets, and reports) that use language appropriate for the specific audience.

5F6294D0DFE701319A2D68A86D17958E.description: The student will write for a variety of purposes and audiences.

5F625300DFE701319A2C68A86D17958E.description: Producing Written Communications in a Variety of Forms

5F621470DFE701319A2B68A86D17958E.description: Spell correctly using Standard American English.

5F61D240DFE701319A2A68A86D17958E.description:
Edit for the correct use of written Standard American English, including
  • punctuation
    • semicolon,
    • commas to enclose appositives, and
    • commas to separate introductory clauses and phrases.
(See Instructional Appendix: Composite Writing Matrix.)

5F618EC0DFE701319A2968A86D17958E.description: Revise writing to improve clarity, tone, voice, content, and the development of ideas. (See Instructional Appendix: Composite Writing Matrix.)

5F614510DFE701319A2868A86D17958E.description:
Use grammatical conventions of written Standard American English, including
  • main and subordinate clauses,
  • indefinite pronouns,
  • pronoun-antecedent agreement, and
  • consistent verb tenses.
(See Instructional Appendix: Composite Writing Matrix.)

5F60E710DFE701319A2768A86D17958E.description: Create multiple-paragraph compositions that include a central idea with supporting details and use appropriate transitions between paragraphs.

5F608730DFE701319A2668A86D17958E.description: Use complete sentences in a variety of types (including simple, compound, and complex sentences) in writing.

5F6047F0DFE701319A2568A86D17958E.description: Organize written works using prewriting techniques, discussions, graphic organizers, models, and outlines.

5F600840DFE701319A2468A86D17958E.description: The student will create written work that has a clear focus, sufficient detail, coherent organization, effective use of voice, and correct use of the conventions of written Standard American English.

5F5F48F0DFE701319A2168A86D17958E.description: Spell new words using Greek and Latin roots and affixes. (See Instructional Appendix: Greek and Latin Roots and Affixes.)

5F5F0310DFE701319A2068A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between the denotation and the connotation of a given word.

5F5EB730DFE701319A1F68A86D17958E.description: Interpret the meaning of idioms and euphemisms encountered in texts.

5F5E7860DFE701319A1E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the meaning of words by using Greek and Latin roots and affixes within texts. (See Instructional Appendix: Greek and Latin Roots and Affixes.)

5F5E3800DFE701319A1D68A86D17958E.description: Use context clues (for example, those that provide an example, a definition, or restatement) to generate the meanings of unfamiliar and multiple-meaning words.

5F5DF680DFE701319A1C68A86D17958E.description: The student will use word analysis and vocabulary strategies to read fluently.

5F5D6F30DFE701319A1A68A86D17958E.description: Read independently for extended periods of time to gain information.

5F5D1EF0DFE701319A1968A86D17958E.description: Identify propaganda techniques (including testimonials and bandwagon) in informational texts.

5F5CC970DFE701319A1868A86D17958E.description: Predict events in informational texts on the basis of cause-and-effect relationships.

5F5C75D0DFE701319A1768A86D17958E.description: Interpret information from functional text features (for example, tables of contents and glossaries).

5F5C1E60DFE701319A1668A86D17958E.description: Interpret information from graphic features (for example, illustrations, graphs, charts, maps, diagrams, and graphic organizers).

5F5BD530DFE701319A1568A86D17958E.description: Interpret information that text elements (for example, print styles and chapter headings) provide to the reader.

5F5B7640DFE701319A1468A86D17958E.description: Create responses to informational texts through a variety of methods (for example, drawings, written works, oral and auditory presentations, discussions, and media productions).

5F5B0B00DFE701319A1368A86D17958E.description: Summarize author bias based on the omission of relevant facts and statements of unsupported opinions.

5F5AC490DFE701319A1268A86D17958E.description: Analyze informational texts to draw conclusions and make inferences.

5F5A8630DFE701319A1168A86D17958E.description: Analyze central ideas within and across informational texts.

5F5A4680DFE701319A1068A86D17958E.description: The student will read and comprehend a variety of informational texts in print and nonprint formats.

5F59BB40DFE701319A0E68A86D17958E.description: Read independently for extended periods of time for pleasure.

5F5966E0DFE701319A0D68A86D17958E.description: Predict events in literary texts on the basis of cause-and-effect relationships.

5F592740DFE701319A0C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze works of fiction (including legends and myths) and works of nonfiction (including speeches and personal essays) by characteristics.

5F58E850DFE701319A0B68A86D17958E.description: Understand the characteristics of poetry (including stanza, rhyme scheme, repetition, and refrain) and drama (including stage directions and the use of monologues).

5F58A840DFE701319A0A68A86D17958E.description: Create responses to literary texts through a variety of methods (for example, written works, oral and auditory presentations, discussions, media productions, and the visual and performing arts).

5F586670DFE701319A0968A86D17958E.description: Compare/contrast main ideas within and across literary texts.

5F582240DFE701319A0868A86D17958E.description: Interpret the effect of the author's craft (including tone and the use of flashback and foreshadowing) on the meaning of literary texts.

5F57D8E0DFE701319A0768A86D17958E.description: Analyze an author's development of characters, setting, and conflict in a given literary text.

5F5788C0DFE701319A0668A86D17958E.description: Interpret devices of figurative language (including simile, metaphor, personification, and hyperbole) and sound devices (including onomatopoeia and alliteration).

5F573A70DFE701319A0568A86D17958E.description: Differentiate among the first-person, limited-omniscient (third person), and omniscient (third person) points of view.

5F56EBB0DFE701319A0468A86D17958E.description: Analyze literary texts to draw conclusions and make inferences.

5F56ABE0DFE701319A0368A86D17958E.description: The student will read and comprehend a variety of literary texts in print and nonprint formats.

document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards for Mathematics

638C8140DFE70131A0BD68A86D17958E.description: Interpret graphic and tabular data representations by using range and the measures of central tendency (mean, median, and mode).

638BDC30DFE70131A0BB68A86D17958E.description: Apply procedures to compute the odds of a given event.

638B8E40DFE70131A0BA68A86D17958E.description: Interpret the probability for two dependent events.

638B5050DFE70131A0B968A86D17958E.description: Apply procedures to calculate the probability of two dependent events.

638B1130DFE70131A0B868A86D17958E.description: Use theoretical and experimental probability to make inferences and convincing arguments about an event or events.

638AD170DFE70131A0B768A86D17958E.description: Organize data in matrices or scatterplots as appropriate.

638A8F10DFE70131A0B668A86D17958E.description: Generalize the relationship between two sets of data by using scatterplots and lines of best fit.

638A4AC0DFE70131A0B568A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate through the mathematical processes an understanding of the relationships between two variables within one population or sample.

6389A9E0DFE70131A0B368A86D17958E.description: Use multistep unit analysis to convert between and within U.S. Customary System and the metric system.

63896B70DFE70131A0B268A86D17958E.description: Analyze a variety of measurement situations to determine the necessary level of accuracy and precision.

63892D80DFE70131A0B168A86D17958E.description: Apply formulas to determine the perimeters and areas of trapezoids.

6388ED70DFE70131A0B068A86D17958E.description: Apply formulas to determine the exact (pi) circumference and area of a circle.

6388AC10DFE70131A0AF68A86D17958E.description: Apply strategies and formulas to determine the volume of the three-dimensional shapes cone and sphere.

63886A70DFE70131A0AE68A86D17958E.description: Explain the effect on the area of two-dimensional shapes and on the volume of three-dimensional shapes when one or more of the dimensions are changed.

63881F40DFE70131A0AD68A86D17958E.description: Use proportional reasoning and the properties of similar shapes to determine the length of a missing side.

6387DED0DFE70131A0AC68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate through the mathematical processes an understanding of the proportionality of similar figures; the necessary levels of accuracy and precision in measurement; the use of formulas to determine circumference, perimeter, area, and volume; and the use of conversions within and between the U.S. Customary System and the metric system.

638750C0DFE70131A0AA68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the effect of a dilation on a square, rectangle, or right triangle in a coordinate plane.

638706A0DFE70131A0A968A86D17958E.description: Apply a dilation to a square, rectangle, or right triangle in a coordinate plane.

6386BB00DFE70131A0A868A86D17958E.description: Use ordered pairs, equations, intercepts, and intersections to locate points and lines in a coordinate plane.

638620A0DFE70131A0A668A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate through the mathematical processes an understanding of the Pythagorean theorem; the use of ordered pairs, equations, intercepts, and intersections to locate points and lines in a coordinate plane; and the effect of a dilation in a coordinate plane.

63859BB0DFE70131A0A468A86D17958E.description: Identify the slope of a linear equation from a graph, equation, and/or table.

63854F70DFE70131A0A368A86D17958E.description: Identify the coordinates of the x- and y-intercepts of a linear equation from a graph, equation, and/or table.

638506E0DFE70131A0A268A86D17958E.description: Classify relationships between two variables in graphs, tables, and/or equations as either linear or nonlinear.

6384A930DFE70131A0A168A86D17958E.description: Apply procedures to solve multistep equations.

63845520DFE70131A0A068A86D17958E.description: Use commutative, associative, and distributive properties to examine the equivalence of a variety of algebraic expressions.

63841220DFE70131A09F68A86D17958E.description: Represent algebraic relationships with equations and inequalities.

6383CED0DFE70131A09E68A86D17958E.description: Translate among verbal, graphic, tabular, and algebraic representations of linear functions.

63838A90DFE70131A09D68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate through the mathematical processes an understanding of equations, inequalities, and linear functions.

6382B4B0DFE70131A09A68A86D17958E.description: Apply strategies and procedures to approximate between two whole numbers the square roots or cube roots of numbers less than 1,000.

63826DA0DFE70131A09968A86D17958E.description: Apply the concept of absolute value.

63821C90DFE70131A09868A86D17958E.description: Compare rational and irrational numbers by using the symbols =, =, <, >, and =.

6381D0B0DFE70131A09768A86D17958E.description: Represent the approximate location of irrational numbers on a number line.

63818150DFE70131A09668A86D17958E.description: Understand the effect of multiplying and dividing a rational number by another rational number.

63813FD0DFE70131A09568A86D17958E.description: Apply an algorithm to add, subtract, multiply, and divide integers.

6380EFE0DFE70131A09468A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate through the mathematical processes an understanding of operations with integers, the effects of multiplying and dividing with rational numbers, the comparative magnitude of rational and irrational numbers, the approximation of cube and square roots, and the application of proportional reasoning.

63807040DFE70131A09268A86D17958E.description: Use standard and nonstandard representations to convey and support mathematical relationships.

638033F0DFE70131A09168A86D17958E.description: Generalize connections among a variety of representational forms and real-world situations.

637FF7A0DFE70131A09068A86D17958E.description: Use correct and clearly written or spoken words, variables, and notations to communicate about significant mathematical tasks.

637FB5E0DFE70131A08F68A86D17958E.description: Generalize mathematical statements based on inductive and deductive reasoning.

637F6F90DFE70131A08E68A86D17958E.description: Understand equivalent symbolic expressions as distinct symbolic forms that represent the same relationship.

637F0F00DFE70131A08D68A86D17958E.description: Use inductive and deductive reasoning to formulate mathematical arguments.

637EA520DFE70131A08C68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate conjectures and pose follow-up questions to prove or disprove conjectures.

637E5AB0DFE70131A08B68A86D17958E.description: Generate and solve complex abstract problems that involve modeling physical, social, or mathematical phenomena.

637E0700DFE70131A08A68A86D17958E.description: The student will understand and utilize the mathematical processes of problem solving, reasoning and proof, communication, connections, and representation.

document.title: South Carolina Social Studies Academic Standards

6787DD60DFE70131A66968A86D17958E.description: Recognize that families of the past have made choices to fulfill their wants and needs and that families do so in the present.

67879E20DFE70131A66868A86D17958E.description: Recognize the ways that community businesses have provided goods and services for families in the past and do so in the present.

67876360DFE70131A66768A86D17958E.description: Explain how changes in modes of transportation and communication have affected the way families live and work together.

67872870DFE70131A66668A86D17958E.description: Compare the daily lives of children and their families in the past and in the present.

6786EA00DFE70131A66568A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the way families live and work together today as well as in the past.
comments: We can better understand ourselves and others by examining American families in the present and in the past. To make connections between the past and the present, the student will utilize the knowledge and skills set forth in the following indicators:

6786ABF0DFE70131A66468A86D17958E.description: Describe the actions of important figures that reflect the values of American democracy, including George Washington, Abraham Lincoln, Susan B. Anthony, Rosa Parks, and Martin Luther King Jr.

67866700DFE70131A66368A86D17958E.description: Identify the reasons for our celebrating national holidays, including Veterans Day, Thanksgiving, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, President's Day, Memorial Day, and Independence Day.

67861F40DFE70131A66268A86D17958E.description: Recognize the significance of symbols of the United States that represent its democratic values, including the American flag, the bald eagle, the Statue of Liberty, the Pledge of Allegiance, and "The Star-Spangled Banner."

6785E130DFE70131A66168A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the values that American democracy represents and upholds.
comments: The core values of American democracy are reflected in the traditions and history of our country. To make connections among those traditions, history, and values, the student will utilize the knowledge and skills set forth in the following indicators:

6785A460DFE70131A66068A86D17958E.description: Explain how following rules and obeying authority figures reflect qualities of good citizenship, including honesty, responsibility, respect, fairness, and patriotism.

67856490DFE70131A65F68A86D17958E.description: Identify authority figures in the school and the community who enforce rules and laws that keep people safe, including crossing guards, bus drivers, firefighters, and police officers.

67852600DFE70131A65E68A86D17958E.description: Summarize the roles of authority figures in a child's life, including those of parents and teachers.

6784E850DFE70131A65D68A86D17958E.description: Explain the purpose of rules and laws and the consequences of breaking them.

67849D40DFE70131A65C68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the purpose of rules and the role of authority figures in a child's life.
comments: Rules and authority figures provide order, security, and safety in the home, school, and larger community. To participate effectively in civic life by acting responsibly with the interest of the larger community in mind, the student will utilize the knowledge and skills set forth in the following indicators:

67844E10DFE70131A65B68A86D17958E.description: Recognize natural features of his or her environment (e.g., mountains and bodies of water).

67840120DFE70131A65A68A86D17958E.description: Identify his or her personal connections to places, including home, school, neighborhood, and city or town.

6783B370DFE70131A65968A86D17958E.description: Illustrate the features of his or her home, school, and neighborhood by creating maps, models, and drawings.

67837290DFE70131A65868A86D17958E.description: Identify the location of his or her home, school, neighborhood, and city or town on a map.

comments: Maps and other geographic representations can communicate information about the location and features of one's surroundings. To access and utilize geographic information efficiently, effectively, and accurately, the student will utilize the knowledge and skills set forth in the following indicators:
67832D80DFE70131A65768A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of his or her surroundings.

6782DEF0DFE70131A65668A86D17958E.description: Foundations of Social Studies: Children as Citizens
comments: Social studies in kindergarten focuses on those aspects of living that affect the children and their families. The classroom serves as a model of society in which decisions are made with a sense of individual responsibility and with respect for the rules by which we all must live. The students learn about the nature of their physical environment—home, school, neighborhood, and town, including how the people in their community provide goods and services. They also learn about the role of families now and in the past; the need for rules and authority; and the values of American democracy as reflected in the traditions and history of the nation.

document.title: South Carolina Standards for Professional Development

B37D1EF9977748FD990A0F12F9E6B004.description: Assessment strategies are shared among teachers, schools, and districts.

6046CB251F15491A830E5B3985EF4849.description: Modifications and accommodations are made to meet special needs of students.

981C1575F9A642A693E4ED1C34353F51.description: Professional development on the design and use of assessments is provided.

C0667766AF904A24BBDF4F7E1A521944.description: Effective professional development prepares teachers to use various types of performance assessments in their classrooms.

78B681EE344B455F982C4294FDC86312.description: Participation of parents/families in educational activities at school and home increases.

A23F98E0F6CC4CFF89B62AA4889929C9.description: Increased communication about student academic progress and a partnership plan for student progress is created.

4C0983F0C890464894D3D8B9FDB0FA11.description: Active school/business partnerships support student learning. Volunteers and mentors are available to support student learning.

859E2F9BCDC1443DB2FA74E9DFA766E1.description: Effective professional development helps teachers and administrators engage families and communities in improving all children's academic achievement.

8763EBDD06164E299796631A5EEC79E6.description: Teachers and administrators believe students can learn at high levels.

B7E49F12E1514D48A447867FA4AA19E9.description: Evidence of high expectations exists in lesson plans, unit plans, performance assessments, school improvement plans, and district strategic plans.

BB5BD0E77A90467D873E8BFECEF0BC83.description: Staff participates in training about academic and professional development standards.

628D48F880054970A09E0953AA90079D.description: Increasing numbers of students experience a challenging core curriculum and improve their achievement.

AF413517F03D45F59C6C678364FBB291.description: Effective professional development prepares educators to demonstrate high expectations for student learning.

AF5BB7F0F41343859116294FA20D713B.description: Professional development incorporates diversity issues into all programs.

972D5E1CA53C4281A63FCC622A6DF2EA.description: Effective strategies to engage diverse learners and learning styles in the educational process are identified.

D5BF57483D464B739E29599260017BF3.description: Populations are identified by gender, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, and special needs.

773F761777974A299E86B2945408B5BE.description: Effective professional development addresses diversity to ensure an equitable and quality education is provided to all.

D00357C1EB844C769AF4E3DAF1360164.description: Data on student attendance, suspension, disciplinary referrals, and expulsions are reported and used to inform planning.

231CDB7CCFF84E0A8045EC024FD21605.description: There is a comprehensive school-wide guidance plan incorporating student documentation.

0EC970BA9185400694032BA4D152C040.description: Student's self-esteem increases their success in the classroom.

400DB5BA71C74EDDA39235A9787E9EF1.description: Educators develop the ability to respond to the uniqueness of each child and each situation. They implement effective classroom management strategies.

4931C69B36F84ED9AAEE825522A5665D.description: Effective professional development facilitates school-wide and classroom-based management strategies that maximize student learning.

D01495712CF24BC2AA3FC77D76366109.description: Student work is used to inform the staff about student progress and is used as a means by which to adjust instruction.

AEE3DFCE0BB94BF89D5EF98A04147456.description: Teachers adopt research-based programs and instructional strategies that are appropriate and effective for all children.

F9A91AB675944870BB5A35A2516555D2.description: School improvement occurs as educators see the discrepancy between the needs of children and the school's current practices each phase and appropriate interventions occur.

A02A6ED2C4D14675A2BDE68A403A9C70.description: Effective professional development increases administrators' and teachers' understanding of how to provide school environments, curriculum and instruction that are responsive to the needs of all students.

87BAFE339E7B4162B3DF741E220F558B.description: Staff share responsibility to conduct meetings, make shared decisions, solve problems, and work collegially.

059E37E56CFA4DD0BAB64A612E07CD97.description: Staff members know about and use interdisciplinary team organization and instruction.

D3A7DE067ABA4A58A06C33683FFB042B.description: Faculty and administration develop the skills to work collaboratively.

5EAADF60F5494B6EB17873A25E672D13.description: Effective Professional development uses the stages of group development to build effective, productive, and collegial teams.

48F51F1583B7421BB3EB7379508F5EDC.description: Opportunities to network and share ideas and resources are promoted.

E23DE0784B2546EEA3CB823CAD443662.description: The ability of staff members to analyze and self-correct their performance improves.

FCBAC73B4AF44FBD81A1AEE8AAEE5A22.description: All training designs include plans for follow-up. Follow-up is monitored and supported with human and financial resources. Desired changes in on-the-job behavior improve student performance.

4BEB766F7D59497AB16C8EC09819B199.description: Effective professional development provides the follow-up necessary to ensure improvement.

190E62091EF14AD0A6684B0BB7843AEC.description: A variety of readiness and professional development activities occur at each school site rather than uniform activities throughout a system.

86920801856347E4A1B325918F3F64EC.description: Training includes theory, demonstration, practice, feedback and coaching.

4052C79E63EE4593892E54C418488D22.description: Multiple formats are evident: action research, study groups, curriculum development, self-study, use of technology, and training. Methodology is appropriate to the intended outcomes.

9C85D171DD66420F904AC825B6200EF0.description: Effective professional development uses multiple approaches to improve student success.

0FD5264730B24CD4AAB687DA96ACDE10.description: Evaluation data include multiple sources of information and focus on all levels of the organization. Teachers use classroom assessments to measure immediate impact of professional development investments.

24E1EEC9D04E4AAEBB077403FE09A11B.description: Evaluation is considered an integral part of staff development program planning and implementation.

2E0B2309A2CD44039B441239E01FFBAD.description: Evaluations are designed to assess a variety of program outcomes, including participants' reaction to the program, participants' learning, participants' use of new knowledge and skills, impact on student outcomes, and impact on the organization.

0D7B8E8CF853478C8E31D14076B7523E.description: Effective professional development programs require an ongoing evaluation process.

4917CB19BEF0422C8EA3E6852E15025E.description: Successful practices are maintained and unsuccessful practices are abandoned when decisions are made to change goals or strategies.

7410E3591A5B4D86B6AA3781DB859BF3.description: All implementation efforts include descriptions of how each innovation related to other ongoing programs and to the mission of the organization.

51E9C9EE9A6E4494B36AADD0F64BD1B5.description: Improvement plans include a carefully and thoughtfully designed framework for integrating the innovations to be implemented.

6F38EAB432264084B48DF551C75DBD76.description: Effective professional development provides a framework for integrating and relating innovations to the mission of the organization.

813AFF04F7734FC8937A8DF744C583EE.description: The district strategic plan, school improvement plans, and individual improvement plans incorporate goal-setting using all available data.

1DEC931C4D0A4B248EC3EF5B2ED188FF.description: Gaps in achievement among all groups are addressed.

6A1D018B24754E1C9AAF2F8EE3D15D5A.description: Data is provided that links staff development initiatives and intended adult and student results.

D3647FCA8BF54037B1503D2BB2A62A5B.description: Effective professional development priorities are established following a careful analysis of disaggregated data regarding goals for student learning.

6211FB747B7645269742A453B2B54E5F.description: Collaboration is occurring among teachers to support change or innovation.

64E7A6B39629430CBA198BFACA836F82.description: All critical phases of the change process are addressed in the planning design, implementation, and evaluation of programs.

29B6ECA9847A41CEA1C656965EE5756D.description: Appropriate assessments occur at each phase and appropriate interventions occur.

B664A09318F64B5198A4343210E4DF9A.description: Effective professional development provides for three phases of the change process: initiation, implementation, and institutionalization.

B6797D9E48C54BF59D2A5436D4B4EA3D.description: Professional development relates the learning to the learners' goals and allows the learners to make choices linking their individual growth plans with school goals.

F684B5BC017A462893D395F7A17616F4.description: Professional development emphasizes how the learning can be used/applied.

91050901288A46E9944888829482CA23.description: The learning climate is collaborative, informal, and respectful. The providers of all professional development are credible.

A780C793E0C94FD590A0A6083471D445.description: Effective professional development is based on knowledge about adult learning and models this understanding in all activities.

FCEC1C08C686409CBD99BCC14AB76AFA.description: Site-based management teams use shared decision-making processes to determine professional development priorities.

5D5C54CAB54442DDBBEB67ECE954C010.description: Barriers to effective professional development within the organization are addressed.

0F54C3E7785A4FF78D08C4C3EF942E2E.description: All stakeholders are involved in the professional development. The stakeholders (at the state, district, or school level) complete a self-study of their effectiveness each year.

AEB4CCC8DD534327B52E636807CC4E4A.description: Effective professional development provides decision-makers with information about organization development and systems thinking.

0A2E98E170DF4FC7BB375505FE85F8AC.description: Schedules are designed to ensure time for the adults in the system to learn together and improve practice.

1244FA4D0E5645B7A6EA8F9E9DCA981A.description: Additional days for coordinated professional development efforts are built into the school calendar.

82E1A777470F43959E0E2776B6D04DD2.description: Time for professional development activities is provided during the work day (e.g. peer coaching, mentoring, and common planning time).

34C364BFA4B1453988DE6892505080E0.description: Effective professional development provides adequate time for staff members to learn and work together to accomplish the organization's mission and goals.

06D15FF8E19D45E0B212C185DEAA625A.description: Effective professional development is perceived as essential for achieving the purposes of the organization, is valued as an integral part of the strategic plan, and is seen as a key factor in improving student learning.

CC340AC91A7E45AF8CA4C96134ED01FE.description: Professional development is adequately funded. Priorities are set.

54E29D6FDED44C1CA8B7F9E13F6304F7.description: Professional development resources are coordinated to ensure that the professional development activities are aligned with the school improvement plan.

D83D54AAC8764133A607FB7DCD5B6514.description: Effective professional development is aligned with the organization's mission and strategic plan, is linked to student achievement, and is adequately funded by the budget.

C4E42D8121A94FA48BCDE9F0AC7BBCF9.description: Morale increases as a result of staff empowerment and effectiveness.

ACD04A0D922A48F0A464AE570746D934.description: School and district leaders participate with staff in professional development activities.

9D36AD8F39D14E2EBE7052A1C14A9941.description: Administrators, teacher leaders, school board members, community leaders, and others advocate for quality professional development.

F0F1CA40624545A5860F2E0661D909B8.description: Effective professional development requires strong leadership for continuous improvement.

587D23A0A7F440B6BDEDF600F259D47F.description: Staff use the ADEPT performance appraisal process to assess progress and influence continuous improvement.

5E4D51BE7F154BB9987F3C9DD4B69915.description: Staff can articulate the kinds of learning opportunities they access throughout the year.

0260DBDF86A048589D0A81AB374EE692.description: Educators constantly revisit and renew their organizational goals.

D309EBEC1C134764A35C98F6104D17A7.description: Effective professional development fosters the norm of continuous improvement.

document.title: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

620770B0DFE701319E1568A86D17958E.description: Graph the solutions to a linear inequality in two variables as a half-plane (excluding the boundary in the case of a strict inequality), and graph the solution set to a system of linear inequalities in two variables as the intersection of the corresponding half-planes.

62070F00DFE701319E1468A86D17958E.description: Explain why the x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations y = f(x) and y = g(x) intersect are the solutions of the equation f(x) = g(x); find the solutions approximately, e.g., using technology to graph the functions, make tables of values, or find successive approximations. Include cases where f(x) and/or g(x) are linear, polynomial, rational, absolute value, exponential, and logarithmic functions.<sup>★</sup>
comments: Modeling is best interpreted not as a collection of isolated topics but in relation to other standards. Making mathematical models is a Standard for Mathematical Practice, and specific modeling standards appear throughout the high school standards indicated by a star symbol (★). The star symbol sometimes appears on the heading for a group of standards; in that case, it should be understood to apply to all standards in that group.

6206B060DFE701319E1368A86D17958E.description: Understand that the graph of an equation in two variables is the set of all its solutions plotted in the coordinate plane, often forming a curve (which could be a line).

62065A70DFE701319E1268A86D17958E.description: Represent and solve equations and inequalities graphically

6205FBF0DFE701319E1168A86D17958E.description: (+) Find the inverse of a matrix if it exists and use it to solve systems of linear equations (using technology for matrices of dimension 3 × 3 or greater).

62059BB0DFE701319E1068A86D17958E.description: (+) Represent a system of linear equations as a single matrix equation in a vector variable.

62051E80DFE701319E0F68A86D17958E.description: Solve a simple system consisting of a linear equation and a quadratic equation in two variables algebraically and graphically.
comments: For example, find the points of intersection between the line y = -3x and the circle x² + y² = 3.

6204B2D0DFE701319E0E68A86D17958E.description: Solve systems of linear equations exactly and approximately (e.g., with graphs), focusing on pairs of linear equations in two variables.

62045920DFE701319E0D68A86D17958E.description: Prove that, given a system of two equations in two variables, replacing one equation by the sum of that equation and a multiple of the other produces a system with the same solutions.

6203AC00DFE701319E0B68A86D17958E.description: Solve quadratic equations by inspection (e.g., for x² = 49), taking square roots, completing the square, the quadratic formula and factoring, as appropriate to the initial form of the equation. Recognize when the quadratic formula gives complex solutions and write them as a ± bi for real numbers a and b.

620350C0DFE701319E0A68A86D17958E.description: Use the method of completing the square to transform any quadratic equation in x into an equation of the form (x - p)² = q that has the same solutions. Derive the quadratic formula from this form.

6202EB00DFE701319E0968A86D17958E.description: Solve quadratic equations in one variable.

62029770DFE701319E0868A86D17958E.description: Solve linear equations and inequalities in one variable, including equations with coefficients represented by letters.

62024020DFE701319E0768A86D17958E.description: Solve equations and inequalities in one variable

6201E730DFE701319E0668A86D17958E.description: Solve simple rational and radical equations in one variable, and give examples showing how extraneous solutions may arise.

62018B70DFE701319E0568A86D17958E.description: Explain each step in solving a simple equation as following from the equality of numbers asserted at the previous step, starting from the assumption that the original equation has a solution. Construct a viable argument to justify a solution method.

62012680DFE701319E0468A86D17958E.description: Understand solving equations as a process of reasoning and explain the reasoning

62005E40DFE701319E0268A86D17958E.description: Rearrange formulas to highlight a quantity of interest, using the same reasoning as in solving equations.
comments: For example, rearrange Ohm's law V = IR to highlight resistance R.

61FFFB00DFE701319E0168A86D17958E.description: Represent constraints by equations or inequalities, and by systems of equations and/or inequalities, and interpret solutions as viable or nonviable options in a modeling context.
comments: For example, represent inequalities describing nutritional and cost constraints on combinations of different foods.

61FF9B10DFE701319E0068A86D17958E.description: Create equations in two or more variables to represent relationships between quantities; graph equations on coordinate axes with labels and scales.

61FF2D40DFE701319DFF68A86D17958E.description: Create equations and inequalities in one variable and use them to solve problems. Include equations arising from linear and quadratic functions, and simple rational and exponential functions.

61FEA460DFE701319DFE68A86D17958E.description: Create equations that describe numbers or relationships

comments: Modeling is best interpreted not as a collection of isolated topics but in relation to other standards. Making mathematical models is a Standard for Mathematical Practice, and specific modeling standards appear throughout the high school standards indicated by a star symbol (★). The star symbol sometimes appears on the heading for a group of standards; in that case, it should be understood to apply to all standards in that group.

61FDD6B0DFE701319DFC68A86D17958E.description: (+) Understand that rational expressions form a system analogous to the rational numbers, closed under addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by a nonzero rational expression; add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational expressions.

61FD7FB0DFE701319DFB68A86D17958E.description: Rewrite simple rational expressions in different forms; write <sup>a(x </sup>/<sub>b(x)</sub> in the form q(x) + <sup>r(x)</sup>/<sub>b(x)</sub>, where a(x), b(x), q(x), and r(x) are polynomials with the degree of r(x) less than the degree of b(x), using inspection, long division, or, for the more complicated examples, a computer algebra system.

61FCD430DFE701319DF968A86D17958E.description: (+) Know and apply the Binomial Theorem for the expansion of (x + y)<sup>n</sup> in powers of x and y for a positive integer n, where x and y are any numbers, with coefficients determined for example by Pascal's Triangle.
comments: The Binomial Theorem can be proved by mathematical induction or by a combinatorial argument.

61FC7D00DFE701319DF868A86D17958E.description: Prove polynomial identities and use them to describe numerical relationships.
comments: For example, the polynomial identity (x² + y²)2 = (x² — y²)² + (2xy)² can be used to generate Pythagorean triples.

61FC2620DFE701319DF768A86D17958E.description: Use polynomial identities to solve problems

61FBBEB0DFE701319DF668A86D17958E.description: Identify zeros of polynomials when suitable factorizations are available, and use the zeros to construct a rough graph of the function defined by the polynomial.

61FB5C40DFE701319DF568A86D17958E.description: Know and apply the Remainder Theorem: For a polynomial p(x) and a number a, the remainder on division by x - a is p(a), so p(a) = 0 if and only if (x - a) is a factor of p(x).

61FAF760DFE701319DF468A86D17958E.description: Understand the relationship between zeros and factors of polynomials

61FA9570DFE701319DF368A86D17958E.description: Understand that polynomials form a system analogous to the integers, namely, they are closed under the operations of addition, subtraction, and multiplication; add, subtract, and multiply polynomials.

61F9DA20DFE701319DF168A86D17958E.description: Arithmetic with Polynomials and Rational Expressions

61F97A70DFE701319DF068A86D17958E.description: Derive the formula for the sum of a finite geometric series (when the common ratio is not 1), and use the formula to solve problems.<sup>★</sup>
comments: For example, calculate mortgage payments.

Modeling is best interpreted not as a collection of isolated topics but in relation to other standards. Making mathematical models is a Standard for Mathematical Practice, and specific modeling standards appear throughout the high school standards indicated by a star symbol (★). comments: Modeling is best interpreted not as a collection of isolated topics but in relation to other standards. Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.
E429E1AE6D874088BD09166283FD23F6.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.

77A980A1954E44CC99DC7ACF95BC6EF1.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

2290C88F5B084A4D939A49EE4F2A783F.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

239C0599F0B4412896898CB206296D0A.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.
comments: Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.
