53B5BBD0DFE7013187E068A86D17958E.description: Analyze and describe the relationship between the media arts and other arts disciplines and other content areas.

53B57970DFE7013187DF68A86D17958E.description: Analyze examples of media artwork to gain an awareness of the components that connect the media arts to everyday life and activities in the world at large.

53B53510DFE7013187DE68A86D17958E.description: The student will make connections between the media arts and other arts disciplines, other content areas, and the world.

53B49AB0DFE7013187DC68A86D17958E.description: Identify the techniques used in different media texts that reflect varying perspectives and points of view.

53B44460DFE7013187DB68A86D17958E.description: Identify creative techniques used in a variety of media texts (for example, television, film, radio, Internet).

53B40780DFE7013187DA68A86D17958E.description: Explain why different audiences might have different responses to a variety of media texts.

53B3CB60DFE7013187D968A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the effectiveness of the presentation and treatment of ideas in media texts.

53B34E30DFE7013187D768A86D17958E.description: Explain the ways that a variety of media texts address their intended purpose and audience.

53B31030DFE7013187D668A86D17958E.description: The student will access, analyze, interpret, and create media texts.

53B27900DFE7013187D468A86D17958E.description: Describe processes used in the creation of media artwork and identify the products that are the result of those processes.

53B23800DFE7013187D368A86D17958E.description: Design and create media artwork that communicates his or her experiences.

53B1F6C0DFE7013187D268A86D17958E.description: Expand his or her media arts vocabulary and identify elements of artistic design specific to individual media.

53B1B660DFE7013187D168A86D17958E.description: The student will create media artwork that demonstrates an understanding and command of the principles of artistic design.

53B0F650DFE7013187CF68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the use of self-led and peer-led instruction and assessment materials for evaluating media artwork.

53B0AB50DFE7013187CE68A86D17958E.description: Utilize information literacy skills to make informed decisions about his or her use of digital tools and resources.

53B06940DFE7013187CD68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an understanding of and respect for the accepted procedures regarding the responsible care of media arts equipment and materials.

53B025B0DFE7013187CC68A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of media technologies, techniques, and processes to communicate ideas.

53AFE0F0DFE7013187CB68A86D17958E.description: Identify the specific skills, knowledge, and abilities necessary for creating media artwork.

53AF9A80DFE7013187CA68A86D17958E.description: The student will develop and expand his or her knowledge of the processes, techniques, and applications used in the creation of media artwork.

document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards for the Visual and Performing Arts - Choral Music

57910700DFE701318E4568A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast various places where music is performed and identify appropriate audience behaviors for those performances.

5790C570DFE701318E4468A86D17958E.description: Discuss ways that activities performed in music classes can be used in other daily activities.

57907ED0DFE701318E4368A86D17958E.description: Sing songs and play games representative of daily real-life experiences.

57903210DFE701318E4268A86D17958E.description: Explore career options in music and recognize which options are a source of personal income.

578FEF60DFE701318E4168A86D17958E.description: Discuss the fact that music supplies, repairs, and replacements cost money.

578FAB70DFE701318E4068A86D17958E.description: Discuss the various tasks that musicians carry out in their jobs.

578F6910DFE701318E3F68A86D17958E.description: Describe music careers in familiar settings.

578F23C0DFE701318E3E68A86D17958E.description: Integrate the subject matter of non-arts classes into the music class by singing songs that reinforce language arts and mathematics curricula.

578EC200DFE701318E3D68A86D17958E.description: Integrate music and storytelling by creating sound stories and adding sound effects to stories and poems.

578E6C00DFE701318E3C68A86D17958E.description: The student will make connections between music and other arts disciplines, other content areas, and the world.

579235C0DFE701318E4968A86D17958E.description: Use personal vocabulary to describe voices, instruments, music notation, and stylistic differences in music of various genres from the diverse cultures of the world.

5791D8A0DFE701318E4868A86D17958E.description: Sing a diverse repertoire of music from various cultures.

579189D0DFE701318E4768A86D17958E.description: The student will examine and perform music from a variety of historical periods and cultures.

578DF160DFE701318E3A68A86D17958E.description: Identify his or her preference for specific musical works and performances.

578DB3B0DFE701318E3968A86D17958E.description: Identify specific elements of musical works that evoke emotion and response.

578D33C0DFE701318E3768A86D17958E.description: Use creative and choreographed movement in response to changes in beat, tempo, dynamics, and the lyrics.

578CE000DFE701318E3668A86D17958E.description: Identify the sources of a variety of sounds such as environmental, instrumental, and vocal (child, male, and female).

578C99F0DFE701318E3568A86D17958E.description: Identify and describe basic musical elements such as pitch, tempo, and dynamics.

578C5C10DFE701318E3468A86D17958E.description: Use movement and personal vocabulary to describe music from diverse cultures.

578C1B70DFE701318E3368A86D17958E.description: Identify examples of musical forms such as call and response and verse and refrain.

578B9810DFE701318E3168A86D17958E.description: The student will listen to, describe, analyze, and evaluate music and music performances.

578AF9D0DFE701318E2F68A86D17958E.description: Use icons and/or simple symbols to write musical ideas.

578A9C90DFE701318E2E68A86D17958E.description: Identify basic symbols such as staff, bar lines, measures, double bar line, repeat sign, and dynamics.

578A4730DFE701318E2D68A86D17958E.description: Use a system (for example, solfège syllables, numbers, note names) to read, write, and perform a melodic line in the pentatonic mode.

5789F490DFE701318E2C68A86D17958E.description: Use a system (for example, rhythm syllables, numbers) to read, write, and perform rhythm patterns including quarter notes, eighth notes, and quarter rests.

5789A2E0DFE701318E2B68A86D17958E.description: The student will read and notate music.

5788F4A0DFE701318E2968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate awareness of contrast and repetition in rhyme or song.

5788B5C0DFE701318E2868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate creativity by composing and using symbols to represent music beats.

578835E0DFE701318E2668A86D17958E.description: Use body percussion and classroom instruments to improvise simple rhythmic accompaniments.

5787EFC0DFE701318E2568A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between two or three rhythmic variations or melodic embellishments of phrases in familiar songs when presented aurally.

5787A6B0DFE701318E2468A86D17958E.description: Improvise songs and rhythm chants with words and syllables.

578728A0DFE701318E2268A86D17958E.description: The student will improvise, compose, and arrange music within specified guidelines.

5786A5C0DFE701318E2068A86D17958E.description: Explore a variety of pitched and unpitched instruments as well as other sound sources, including body percussion.

57861C40DFE701318E1E68A86D17958E.description: Sing in groups, using good posture and matching dynamic levels.

5785C7E0DFE701318E1D68A86D17958E.description: Sing developmentally appropriate songs representing a variety of cultures.

57858890DFE701318E1C68A86D17958E.description: Speak, chant, sing, and move to demonstrate awareness of beat, tempo, and dynamics.

578546D0DFE701318E1B68A86D17958E.description: Sing songs in a developmentally appropriate range, match the pitch, and maintain a steady tempo.

57850800DFE701318E1A68A86D17958E.description: Echo simple rhythmic and melodic patterns.

57847F80DFE701318E1868A86D17958E.description: The student will sing and perform on instruments a variety of music, alone and with others.

document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards and Performance Indicators for Science

4F027A3280BD40BB9091157AFE05BC3E.description: Define problems related to the communication of information over a distance and design devices or solutions that use sound to solve the problem.

9E9BB6A345344128B1F93649109995DC.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations and measurements to describe how changes in vibration affects the pitch and volume of sound.

6D6D9CAED0494AF59476FB98D0901596.description: Plan and conduct scientific investigations to test how different variables affect the properties of sound (including pitch and volume).

9CF740F198CF4F3C830A3E71CF95F8BC.description: Sound, as a form of energy, is produced by vibrating objects and has specific properties including pitch and volume. Sound travels through air and other materials and is used to communicate information in various forms of technology.

E463DB9234E141A9BA217592B2D4DFA2.description: Plan and conduct scientific investigations to explain how light behaves when it strikes transparent, translucent, and opaque materials.

6C3EB657550648C0B2DCFAE3D6CE057C.description: Develop and use models to describe how light travels and interacts when it strikes an object (including reflection, refraction, and absorption) using evidence from observations.

EDB4EFB86C7141D8A320B6CE622BA0AB.description: Obtain and communicate information to explain how the visibility of an object is related to light.

3F6D7ADF1C1441108C04A7FDCC892ADB.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations and measurements to describe how the apparent brightness of light can vary as a result of the distance and intensity of the light source.

70CBF449CD074DB6A9696CD29EE4122E.description: Construct scientific arguments to support the claim that white light is made up of different colors.

4C7425F0719D442596E6A4438D23CD36.description: Light, as a form of energy, has specific properties including color and brightness. Light travels in a straight line until it strikes an object. The way light reacts when it strikes an object depends on the object's properties.

8392C31780DB4158A4A696700C5F045D.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the properties of light and sound as forms of energy.

8EDC4799D009479A855F521D82AF1CA0.description: Physical Science: Forms of Energy - Light and Sound

EB17F1F3A64D481CB1845F0AFFF65690.description: Develop and use models to describe the factors (including tilt, revolution, and angle of sunlight) that result in Earth's seasonal changes.

67BDE1530E7442589745C7687C1112EF.description: Construct explanations of how the Sun appears to move throughout the day using observations of shadows.

28174261412C40EAB3BC569FF7391E84.description: Construct explanations of how day and night result from Earth's rotation on its axis.

7631159A2D674D9BA3FC4F9D6241225D.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations to describe patterns in the (1) location, (2) movement, and (3) appearance of the Moon throughout the year.

3012F97054084D76ABBE21D31A7BFFFA.description: Earth orbits around the Sun and the Moon orbits around Earth. These movements together with the rotation of Earth on a tilted axis result in patterns that can be observed and predicted.

B262A578951042A1A6AB22A030BF5E10.description: Construct scientific arguments to support claims about the importance of astronomy in navigation and exploration (including the use of telescopes, astrolabes, compasses, and sextants).

6AF94567341043FFB7F8E2A1A7590A6A.description: Obtain and communicate information to describe how constellations (including Ursa Major, Ursa Minor, and Orion) appear to move from Earth's perspective throughout the seasons.

9D6A45A8AA884BD0A4AE9DF3FFF9AF36.description: Develop and use models of Earth's solar system to exemplify the location and order of the planets as they orbit the Sun and the main composition (rock or gas) of the planets.

91BCCE701A934528BEA56D717C5B60C5.description: Astronomy is the study of objects in our solar system and beyond. A solar system includes a sun, (star), and all other objects that orbit that sun. Planets in our night sky change positions and are not always visible from Earth as they orbit our Sun. Stars that are beyond the solar system can be seen in the night sky in patterns called constellations. Constellations can be used for navigation and appear to move together across the sky because of Earth's rotation.

84DECE5406DA4260BB34B35B37212667.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the locations, movements, and patterns of stars and objects in the solar system.

221AB6AA03AE461E96FDB5FE6B1360AF.description: Earth Science: Stars and the Solar System

7D3419ACED2C4B9FB422C8B9B522A411.description: Construct explanations about regional climate differences using data from the long term weather conditions of the region.

A5EA11F2AD9C4D339053267C4338F19D.description: Obtain and communicate information about severe weather phenomena (including thunderstorms, hurricanes, and tornadoes) to explain steps humans can take to reduce the impact of severe weather phenomena.

6C569EBD086448729A519BAD06BBF508.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations, measurements, and weather maps to describe patterns in local weather conditions (including temperature, precipitation, wind speed/direction, relative humidity, and cloud types) and predict changes in weather over time.

3475318BCE27494BAA843A7D2AE5AA5E.description: Scientists record patterns in weather conditions across time and place to make predictions about what kind of weather might occur next. Climate describes the range of an area's typical weather conditions and the extent to which those conditions vary over long periods of time. Some weather conditions lead to severe weather phenomena that have different effects and safety concerns.

9913BD95CDBF4E3FAECD917C5B084D36.description: Develop and use models to explain how water changes as it moves between the atmosphere and Earth's surface during each phase of the water cycle (including evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and runoff).

921BF19FA6044E54B787A3298C13A163.description: Obtain and communicate information about some of the gases in the atmosphere (including oxygen, nitrogen, and water vapor) to develop models that exemplify the composition of Earth's atmosphere where weather takes place.

CE70683841D5432F843DA38715FBDD2B.description: Earth's atmosphere is a mixture of gases, including water vapor and oxygen. The movement of water, which is found almost everywhere on Earth including the atmosphere, changes form and cycles between Earth's surface and the air and back again. This cycling of water is driven by energy from the Sun. The movement of water in the water cycle is a major pattern that influences weather conditions. Clouds form during this cycle and various types of precipitation result.

255EA97DC7F843248028D8A367210E23.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the water cycle and weather and climate patterns.

3316D2315878485BB38676B74F06AEE0.description: Construct explanations for how structural adaptations (such as methods for defense, locomotion, obtaining resources, or camouflage) allow animals to survive in the environment.

E85417C2FAA147C8BFEE44A26C09C43A.description: Construct explanations for how structural adaptations (such as the types of roots, stems, or leaves; color of flowers; or seed dispersal) allow plants to survive and reproduce.

0DD66CC3B2114053A6A4F0DFF8E7A696.description: Develop and use models to compare how humans and other animals use their senses and sensory organs to detect and respond to signals from the environment.

7A192272DACF4244B40DD80F06AEA30A.description: Plants and animals have physical characteristics that allow them to receive information from the environment. Structural adaptations within groups of plants and animals allow them to better survive and reproduce.

AF02D8AA1F42439BB25E65E67F59EF20.description: Construct scientific arguments to support claims that some characteristics of organisms are inherited from parents and some are influenced by the environment.

AB4694A8F03045E78BB9B47E85B5621F.description: Develop and use models to compare the stages of growth and development in various animals.

8FE0344668B642CB9DDF07CA4284A148.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations and measurements to compare the stages of development of different seed plants.

66BAFB8F70DC4DA1AFEDA4D2A9EF9B24.description: Obtain and communicate information about the characteristics of plants and animals to develop models which classify plants as flowering or nonflowering and animals as vertebrate or invertebrate.

A4B4F44622D849D9ABE365E07250CFC9.description: Scientists have identified and classified many types of plants and animals. Each plant or animal has a unique pattern of growth and development called a life cycle. Some characteristics (traits) that organisms have are inherited and some result from interactions with the environment.

2520EFAB34DD4BD78265F2D72780A2DB.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of how the structural characteristics and traits of plants and animals allow them to survive, grow, and reproduce.

8B58DF17D7FE4AD7A9F87AEE53C7EBEB.description: Life Science: Characteristics and Growth of Organisms

BDE48C48FB3844F9ADEFC4AF8AAE77EC.description: Construct devices or design solutions to solve specific problems or needs: (1) ask questions to identify problems or needs, (2) ask questions about the criteria and constraints of the devices or solutions, (3) generate and communicate ideas for possible devices or solutions, (4) build and test devices or solutions, (5) determine if the devices or solutions solved the problem and refine the design if needed, and (6) communicate the results.

8ACFC924D937444687CB3998A0B95912.description: Technology is any modification to the natural world created to fulfill the wants and needs of humans. The engineering design process involves a series of iterative steps used to solve a problem and often leads to the development of a new or improved technology.

4EC7ED14C9BA44758683897CC01958D5.description: Obtain and evaluate informational texts, observations, data collected, or discussions to (1) generate and answer questions, (2) understand phenomena, (3) develop models, or (4) support explanations, claims, or designs. Communicate observations and explanations using the conventions and expectations of oral and written language.

7F1F35B0ABF243668B100DE0AC56E596.description: Construct scientific arguments to support claims, explanations, or designs using evidence from observations, data, or informational texts.

FD0921D75D734E48BE30FB83D95C2F58.description: Construct explanations of phenomena using (1) scientific evidence and models, (2) conclusions from scientific investigations, (3) predictions based on observations and measurements, or (4) data communicated in graphs, tables, or diagrams.

3860B1030A324D5093DBE512B0E75C88.description: Use mathematical and computational thinking to (1) express quantitative observations using appropriate English or metric units, (2) collect and analyze data, or (3) understand patterns, trends and relationships between variables.

0BA8B734AFE64EEAAC7A2006AD0A13D2.description: Analyze and interpret data from informational texts, observations, measurements, or investigations using a range of methods (such as tabulation or graphing) to (1) reveal patterns and construct meaning or (2) support explanations, claims, or designs.

25B2AFE845394D1DA7B8B088B075B287.description: Plan and conduct scientific investigations to answer questions, test predictions and develop explanations: (1) formulate scientific questions and predict possible outcomes, (2) identify materials, procedures, and variables, (3) select and use appropriate tools or instruments to collect qualitative and quantitative data, and (4) record and represent data in an appropriate form. Use appropriate safety procedures.

0966900959224F5FB0E5F106B76ED92A.description: Develop, use, and refine models to (1) understand or represent phenomena, processes, and relationships, (2) test devices or solutions, or (3) communicate ideas to others.

983B981D91B34C4BA02F92456E3B4713.description: Ask questions that can be (1) answered using scientific investigations or (2) used to refine models, explanations, or designs.

0E2CA450091F4E4899F6043EE6FB99B4.description: The practices of science and engineering support the development of science concepts, develop the habits of mind that are necessary for scientific thinking, and allow students to engage in science in ways that are similar to those used by scientists and engineers.

D14C928F41E144D5AD37FB7674ECEB97.description: The student will use the science and engineering practices, including the processes and skills of scientific inquiry, to develop understandings of science content.

document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards for English Language Arts

5FACC890DFE701319AAD68A86D17958E.description: Design and carry out research projects by selecting a topic, constructing inquiry questions, accessing resources, evaluating credibility, and selecting and organizing information.

5FAC8530DFE701319AAC68A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of print and electronic reference materials.

5FAC4040DFE701319AAB68A86D17958E.description: Select appropriate graphics, in print or electronic form, to support written works, oral presentations, and visual presentations.

5FABEC80DFE701319AAA68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate organizational strategies to prepare written works, oral and auditory presentations, and visual presentations.

5FAB8B20DFE701319AA968A86D17958E.description: Use vocabulary (including Standard American English) that is appropriate for the particular audience or purpose.

5FAB3790DFE701319AA868A86D17958E.description: Use a standardized system of documentation (including a list of sources with full publication information and the use of intext citations) to properly credit the work of others.

5FAAF290DFE701319AA768A86D17958E.description: Use direct quotations, paraphrasing, or summaries to incorporate into written, oral, auditory, or visual works the information gathered from a variety of research sources.

5FAAB040DFE701319AA668A86D17958E.description: Clarify and refine a research topic.

5FAA6FC0DFE701319AA568A86D17958E.description: The student will access and use information from a variety of sources.

5FAA2EE0DFE701319AA468A86D17958E.description: Applying the Skills of Inquiry and Oral Communication

5FA98560DFE701319AA268A86D17958E.description: Create persuasive pieces (for example, editorials, essays, or speeches) that support a clearly stated position with concrete evidence.

5FA94050DFE701319AA168A86D17958E.description: Create descriptions for use in other modes of written works (for example, narrative, expository, and persuasive).

5FA90060DFE701319AA068A86D17958E.description: Create narratives (for example, memoirs) that communicate the significance of particular personal relationships.

5FA8C030DFE701319A9F68A86D17958E.description: Create informational pieces (for example, reports and letters of request, inquiry, or complaint) that use language appropriate for the specific audience.

5FA880B0DFE701319A9E68A86D17958E.description: The student will write for a variety of purposes and audiences.

5FA83F90DFE701319A9D68A86D17958E.description: Producing Written Communications in a Variety of Forms

5FA7F9A0DFE701319A9C68A86D17958E.description: Spell correctly using Standard American English.

5FA7A960DFE701319A9B68A86D17958E.description: Edit for the correct use of written Standard American English, including ellipses and parentheses. (See Instructional Appendix: Composite Writing Matrix.)

5FA76330DFE701319A9A68A86D17958E.description: Revise writing to improve clarity, tone, voice, content, and the development of ideas. (See Instructional Appendix: Composite Writing Matrix.)

5FA71BA0DFE701319A9968A86D17958E.description: Use grammatical conventions of written Standard American English, including the reinforcement of conventions previously taught. (See Instructional Appendix: Composite Writing Matrix.)

5FA6CE00DFE701319A9868A86D17958E.description: Create multiple-paragraph compositions that include a central idea with supporting details and use appropriate transitions between paragraphs.

5FA67C70DFE701319A9768A86D17958E.description: Use complete sentences in a variety of types (including simple, compound, complex, and compound-complex).

5FA62600DFE701319A9668A86D17958E.description: Organize written works using prewriting techniques, discussions, graphic organizers, models, and outlines.

5FA5C190DFE701319A9568A86D17958E.description: The student will create written work that has a clear focus, sufficient detail, coherent organization, effective use of voice, and correct use of the conventions of written Standard American English.

5FA4FBC0DFE701319A9268A86D17958E.description: Spell new words using Greek and Latin roots and affixes. (See Instructional Appendix: Greek and Latin Roots and Affixes.)

5FA4B6C0DFE701319A9168A86D17958E.description: Interpret the connotations of words to understand the meaning of a given text.

5FA463F0DFE701319A9068A86D17958E.description: Interpret the meaning of idioms and euphemisms encountered in texts.

5FA3F280DFE701319A8F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the meaning of words by using Greek and Latin roots and affixes within texts. (See Instructional Appendix: Greek and Latin Roots and Affixes.)

5FA393C0DFE701319A8E68A86D17958E.description: Use context clues (for example, those that provide an example, a definition, a restatement, or a comparison/contrast) to generate the meanings of unfamiliar and multiple-meaning words.

5FA35140DFE701319A8D68A86D17958E.description: The student will use word analysis and vocabulary strategies to read fluently.

5FA2C2A0DFE701319A8B68A86D17958E.description: Read independently for extended periods of time to gain information.

5FA26F20DFE701319A8A68A86D17958E.description: Identify the use of propaganda techniques (including card stacking, plain folks, and transfer) in informational texts.

5FA229D0DFE701319A8968A86D17958E.description: Analyze information from graphic features (for example, charts and graphs) in informational texts.

5FA1E5D0DFE701319A8868A86D17958E.description: Analyze the impact that text elements (for example, print styles and chapter headings) have on the meaning of a given informational text.

5FA19870DFE701319A8768A86D17958E.description: Create responses to informational texts through a variety of methods (for example, drawings, written works, oral and auditory presentations, discussions, and media productions).

5FA14B20DFE701319A8668A86D17958E.description: Analyze informational texts for author bias (for example, word choice and the exclusion and inclusion of particular information).

5FA0E690DFE701319A8568A86D17958E.description: Compare/contrast information within and across texts to draw conclusions and make inferences.

5FA09610DFE701319A8468A86D17958E.description: Compare/contrast central ideas within and across informational texts.

5FA05830DFE701319A8368A86D17958E.description: The student will read and comprehend a variety of informational texts in print and nonprint formats.

5F9FDDE0DFE701319A8168A86D17958E.description: Read independently for extended periods of time for pleasure.

5F9F9FC0DFE701319A8068A86D17958E.description: Compare/contrast literary texts from various genres (for example, poetry, drama, novels, and short stories).

5F9F60F0DFE701319A7F68A86D17958E.description: Create responses to literary texts through a variety of methods (for example, written works, oral and auditory presentations, discussions, media productions, and the visual and performing arts).

5F9F1F80DFE701319A7E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the effect of the author's craft (including tone and the use of imagery, flashback, foreshadowing, symbolism, irony, and allusion) on the meaning of literary texts.

5F9ED290DFE701319A7D68A86D17958E.description: Analyze a given literary text to determine its theme.

5F9E8AE0DFE701319A7C68A86D17958E.description: Interpret devices of figurative language (including extended metaphor, oxymoron, and paradox).

5F9E3F20DFE701319A7B68A86D17958E.description: Explain the effect of point of view on a given literary text.

5F9DEEA0DFE701319A7A68A86D17958E.description: Compare/contrast ideas within and across literary texts to make inferences.

5F9DA9D0DFE701319A7968A86D17958E.description: The student will read and comprehend a variety of literary texts in print and nonprint formats.

document.title: South Carolina Social Studies Academic Standards

67AF88F0DFE70131A69668A86D17958E.description: Recall stories and songs that reflect the cultural history of various regions in the United States, including stories of regional folk figures, Native American legends, and African American folktales.

67AF3D60DFE70131A69568A86D17958E.description: Recognize the cultural contributions of Native American tribal groups, African Americans, and immigrant groups.

67AEF8A0DFE70131A69468A86D17958E.description: Compare the historic and cultural traditions of various regions in the United States and recognize the ways that these elements have been and continue to be passed across generations.

67AEA470DFE70131A69368A86D17958E.description: Recognize the basic elements that make up a cultural region in the United States, including language, beliefs, customs, art, and literature.

67AE6730DFE70131A69268A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of cultural contributions made by people from the various regions in the United States.
comments: Diverse cultures have contributed to our nation's heritage. To understand cultural differences and appreciate diverse ideals and values within his or her community, the student will utilize the knowledge and skills set forth in the following indicators:

67AE2BD0DFE70131A69168A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of supply and demand on the price of goods and services.

67ADEF80DFE70131A69068A86D17958E.description: Identify examples of markets and price in the local community and explain the roles of buyers and sellers in creating markets and pricing.

67ADB1C0DFE70131A68F68A86D17958E.description: Explain ways that people may obtain goods and services that they do not produce, including the use of barter and money.

67AD70A0DFE70131A68E68A86D17958E.description: Explain how people's choices about what to buy will determine what goods and services are produced.

67AD2B90DFE70131A68D68A86D17958E.description: Summarize the role of community workers who provide goods and services.

67ACD820DFE70131A68C68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the role of goods and services and supply and demand in a community.
comments: People's choices affect the types of goods and services that are produced as well as the price of those goods and services. To understand the role that choice plays in the American economy, the student will utilize the knowledge and skills set forth in the following indicators:

67AC9D40DFE70131A68B68A86D17958E.description: Explain the role of elected leaders, including mayor, governor, and president.

67AC6130DFE70131A68A68A86D17958E.description: Identify the roles of leaders and officials in government, including law enforcement and public safety officials.

67AC2620DFE70131A68968A86D17958E.description: Recognize different types of laws and those people who have the power and authority to enforce them.

67ABE510DFE70131A68868A86D17958E.description: Identify the basic functions of government, including making and enforcing laws, protecting citizens, and collecting taxes.

67AB9ED0DFE70131A68768A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the structure and function of local, state, and national government.
comments: Knowledge of the structure and functions of government enables participation in the democratic process. To participate effectively in civic life, the student will utilize the knowledge and skills set forth in the following indicators:

67AB58E0DFE70131A68668A86D17958E.description: Identify on a map or globe the location of his or her local community, state, nation, and continent.

67AB1120DFE70131A68568A86D17958E.description: Summarize changes that have occurred in the local community over time, including changes in the use of land and in the way people earn their living.

67AAD160DFE70131A68468A86D17958E.description: Recognize the features of urban, suburban, and rural areas of the local region.

67AA91E0DFE70131A68368A86D17958E.description: Recognize characteristics of the local region, including its geographic features and natural resources.

67AA4D30DFE70131A68268A86D17958E.description: Identify on a map the location of places and geographic features of the local community (e.g., landforms, bodies of water, parks) using the legend and the cardinal directions.

67AA04B0DFE70131A68168A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the local community as well as the fact that geography influences not only the development of communities but also the interactions between people and the environment.
comments: Geography influences the development of communities. To understand the connections between communities and the environment, the student will utilize the knowledge and skills set forth in the following indicators:

The focus for social studies in grade two is on communities and the diverse cultures that have contributed to the nation's heritage. Students examine not only the geographic locations but also the cultural characteristics and contributions that have shaped communities and regions. They continue their study of government by identifying its functions and its leaders. Additionally, students focus on the fact the public's choices about what to buy determines what goods and services are produced.

document.title: South Carolina Social Studies Academic Standards

679B3C10DFE70131A67E68A86D17958E.description: Explain the concept of scarcity and the way it forces individuals and families to make choices about which goods and services they can obtain.

comments: People from various cultures are both similar to and different from one another. To understand and develop an appreciation for the similarities and differences across cultures, the student will utilize the knowledge and skills set forth in the following indicators:

6799F190DFE70131A67968A86D17958E.description: Summarize the contributions to democracy that have been made by historic and political figures in the United States, including Benjamin Franklin, Thomas Jefferson, Dorothea Dix, Frederick Douglass, Mary McLeod Bethune, and Franklin D. Roosevelt.

6799A540DFE70131A67868A86D17958E.description: Identify ways that all citizens can serve the common good, including serving as public officials and participating in the election process.

67996620DFE70131A67768A86D17958E.description: Describe the fundamental principles of American democracy, including respect for the rights, opinions, and property of others; fair treatment for all; and respect for the rules by which we live.

67992390DFE70131A67668A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the principles of American democracy and the role of citizens in upholding those principles.
comments: The principles of American democracy are reflected in the rights, responsibilities, and actions of citizens both in the past and in the present. To participate effectively in civic life by acting responsibly with the interest of the larger community in mind, the student will utilize the knowledge and skills set forth in the following indicators:

6798E7C0DFE70131A67568A86D17958E.description: Summarize the possible consequences of an absence of government.

6798AC00DFE70131A67468A86D17958E.description: Illustrate ways that government affects the lives of individuals and families, including taxation that provides services such as public education and health, roads, and security.

67986E10DFE70131A67368A86D17958E.description: Summarize the concept of authority and give examples of people in authority, including school officials, public safety officers, and government officials.

67982770DFE70131A67268A86D17958E.description: Explain the making and enforcing of laws as a basic function of government.

6797DAC0DFE70131A67168A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of how government functions and how government affects families.
comments: Government influences the lives of individuals and families as well as the community at large. To participate effectively in civic life through an understanding of governmental processes, the student will utilize the knowledge and skills set forth in the following indicators:

6797A140DFE70131A67068A86D17958E.description: Compare the ways that people use land and natural resources in different settings around the world.

67976690DFE70131A66F68A86D17958E.description: Identify various natural resources (e.g., water, animals, plants, minerals) around the world.

67972B30DFE70131A66E68A86D17958E.description: Compare schools and neighborhoods that are located in different settings around the world.

6796E550DFE70131A66D68A86D17958E.description: Identify a familiar area of the neighborhood or local community on a simple map, using the legend and basic map symbols.

6796A0E0DFE70131A66C68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of how families interact with their environment both locally and globally.
comments: People interact not only with each other and but also with the environment. To demonstrate an understanding of the connections between people and the environment, the student will utilize the knowledge and skills set forth in the following indicators:

The focus for social studies in the first grade is the family in America and in other countries around the world. Students explore their own culture and then expand their study to other lands and peoples to learn about the ways that those families live and work. They also learn about the connections between families and the environment and explore the concept of government, including the role of government in making and enforcing laws.

2E3E967AA3A441E896627652443BCE66.description: Demonstrate proper lifting and carrying techniques to prevent physical injury.

8C7FE2BAE1BD4510BA2812E5232657CD.description: Demonstrate proper training techniques to prevent physical injury (stretching, strengthening, conditioning, etc.).

1A2AEA52CDE84A6CA396646C0D7CA7B2.description: Demonstrate use of navigation skills (maps, GPS units, Google Earth, etc.).

61CD32699EA7449190DD6BFD6F44609B.description: Demonstrate use of visual aids (binoculars, telescopes, night vision goggles (NVG), thermal imaging, etc.) including verbalizing the objects or people that visual aids are being used to identify.

15244E3BE95E42C59B9682EEA4DEA108.description: Demonstrate proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE and BSI).

comments: Healthcare professionals will apply technical skills required for all career specialties. They will demonstrate skills and knowledge as appropriate.

BD29943DF1594A45974E6BDA17A2E478.description: Discuss the relationship between health, lifestyle, and personal risk factors.

3A020BDC64B84C679469CA516B81F5A3.description: Identify behaviors and factors affecting the EMS professional's health and well-being negatively.

111566D172F745A0A525A8C9C593A9C7.description: Discuss positive steps that the EMS professional takes to help reduce/alleviate stress and promote health and wellness.

C286D37E37984F80B11D140285F6EBA5.description: Explain how to recognize the causes and signals of personal stress.

982D2DBEAA8B4CE088339248F3170E87.description: Recognize the signs and symptoms of critical incident stress.

AB879427A1AA412299E829CEEA211B46.description: Discuss possible emotional reactions that EMS professionals, patient, and family may experience when faced with trauma, illness, death, and dying.

comments: Healthcare professionals will understand the fundamentals of wellness and the prevention of disease processes. They will practice preventive health behaviors among the clients.

D095EF38969942E9B2C020D26C863B31.description: Apply effective techniques for managing team conflict.

03F8BFC313CC494196E022C2167E47BB.description: Analyze attributes and attitudes of an effective leader.

C2418C4385204DBD8AB5533D98E15BB0.description: Recognize methods for building positive team relationships.

7268C75A1D314D4585A19633328BBB4E.description: Understand roles and responsibilities of team members.

comments: Healthcare professionals will understand the roles and responsibilities of individual members as part of the healthcare team, including their ability to promote the delivery of quality healthcare. They will interact effectively and sensitively with all members of the healthcare team.

4E2BE3E0E56E46E79E7B5E8EF59E6AB2.description: Explain the need to determine scene safety.

9C3D0308018C42E5A944B54103F66977.description: Discuss principles of basic emergency response in natural disasters and other emergencies.

F41469EF323A45F79D6D899374463F87.description: Describe fire safety in a healthcare setting.

285A6AAFF74048C589A2DE2A4D97D88A.description: Recognize basic safety labels and placards (biohazards, poisons, etc.).

EEF37030F59B4C4E87A88DD372DB1A78.description: Apply safety techniques in the work environment.

2F3DBD5EDE064BEEA3B120B6A3008718.description: Discuss the principles of infection control, personal protective equipment (PPE), and body substance isolation (BSI).

comments: Healthcare professionals will understand the existing and potential hazards to clients, co-workers, and self. They will prevent injury or illness through safe work practices and follow health and safety policies and procedures.

070B945941894B45970A775BC953442A.description: Evaluate the cultural use of verbal and nonverbal language in a variety of healthcare scenarios.

101C5D2CC85B4A959ADF8D985E8E497F.description: Demonstrate respectful and empathetic treatment of ALL patients/clients (customer service).

DB978E7F2E264BE18D9490BA966B78A0.description: Understand cultural diversity as it impacts healthcare.

47305404CF754EFDB6B969A2006B4A72.description: Apply procedures for reporting activities and behaviors that affect the health, safety, and welfare of others.

BD691ADD1B844C3A82A6E2E0E114400C.description: Recognize ethical issues and their implications related to healthcare.

3B98D4342C2545BAAE3FF97EF31BC5F4.description: Differentiate between ethical and legal issues impacting healthcare.

403A8AD0BE5E41799EB3BB6543DB2A15.description: Identify code of ethics (e.g., National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians [NREMT] Code of Ethics, National Association of Emergency Medical Technicians [NAEMT] Code of Ethics).

BCAA4B4D5BBF44DAA9DC4FB6C3914560.description: Define basic terms and standards related to ethical practices.

comments: Healthcare professionals will understand accepted ethical practices with respect to cultural, social, and ethnic differences within the healthcare environment. They will perform quality healthcare delivery.

D9E8ACFD23FB4228903ADE8351798D72.description: Identify forms of unsafe or hostile work environments.

847933D6ADD4445FB08E0B35379E72E8.description: Differentiate the actions and responsibilities of EMS professionals when interacting with law enforcement.

24E66832A24C438B8E3ADF06DB79173F.description: Explain the importance, necessity, and legality of patient confidentiality (e.g., Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act [HIPAA] and Family Education Rights and Privacy Act [FERPA]).

2DFBBCDE36B24D77A243A4AE9988466E.description: Discuss the issues of abandonment, negligence, and battery and their implications for EMS professionals.

9CD21FF70C52435B9ECCAEB6933AF727.description: Discuss the methods of obtaining consent.

842AE9470FBB407E9648D0651533610D.description: Discuss advance directives and local or state provisions regarding EMS application.

3983BC562CCA4B65AA81B777D6958F00.description: Define the EMS professional's scope of practice.

67CEB93C4DCA44988CC237B8690D8A08.description: Define terms and standards related to legal responsibilities.

comments: Healthcare professionals will understand the legal responsibilities, limitations, and implications of their actions within the healthcare delivery setting. They will perform their duties according to regulations, policies, laws and legislated rights of clients.

B22B44F1ED1148DFA9AEA64E6944EA86.description: Observe and participate in service learning/work-based learning (virtual, guest speakers, etc.) and HOSA activities.

CC5C658567F74FF0BB0C5B63B737A21E.description: Compare careers within the health science career pathways (diagnostic services, therapeutic services, health informatics, support services, or biotechnology research and development).

A31D7B0CE5ED488CAFDF50BD1F446775.description: Discuss levels of education, credentialing requirements, and employment trends in healthcare.

C996E0F97CF44B6DBD0054CBF8B5D91C.description: Apply employability skills in healthcare (attendance policy and time management).

697B5C7832194765BE0258FC093132D0.description: Summarize professional standards as they apply to hygiene, dress, language, confidentiality, and behavior.

6EE85C02C59E41AE9EAEF44B78E3066F.description: Classify the personal traits and attitudes desirable in a member of the healthcare team.

comments: Healthcare professionals will understand how employability skills enhance their employment opportunities and job satisfaction. They will demonstrate key employability skills and will maintain and upgrade skills, as needed.

BBD5BCDC44FA425083E1A5FEB67726E1.description: Characterize the various methods used to access the EMS system in your community.

B18CB7E4D34140BBBDB9EA28AFC3F162.description: Define medical direction, and discuss the EMS professional's role in the process.

5265880D5A2E4C3B85C7496D6A84E72A.description: Define quality improvement, and discuss the EMS professional's role in the process.

08CCEE4B26D846F0946E1A4985FAA3D0.description: Differentiate the roles and responsibilities of EMS professionals from other healthcare professionals.

47E8475C1F2A4871B3510BA597E0C23E.description: Understand the healthcare delivery system (public, private, government, and non-profit).

B05E9B32A0F8474DA003C8094B958CD1.description: Explain the factors influencing healthcare delivery systems.

comments: Healthcare professionals will understand how their role fits into their department, their organization and the overall healthcare environment. They will identify how key systems affect services they perform and quality of care.

CE65EDBBB5E940C6B6CF5AE4DAA30814.description: Apply procedures for accurate documentation and record keeping.

425847F856C445699A579C241822AD0A.description: Recognize elements of written and electronic communication (spelling, grammar, and formatting).

02C74C2CE23E4A0EB2999C552B0E0EDD.description: Apply speaking and active listening skills.

26379CD4BA2B4B5CA92A62081A98C7C9.description: Recognize the elements of communication using a sender-receiver model.

comments: Healthcare professionals will know the various methods of giving and obtaining information. They will communicate effectively, both orally and in writing.

EAE377E107AC40D9A119D3C371A4A904.description: Demonstrate sound study skills, test taking skills, and note taking skills.

B1B1F5A8A3B44D048059B80ED95B3961.description: Apply mathematical computations related to healthcare procedures (metric and household, conversions and measurements).

C3583E185A6048A380C6A9034EE3AF25.description: Recognize body planes, directional terms, quadrants, and cavities.

9E8623CD47004C79A31C7CF7C56E7826.description: Identify basic structure of the human body.

comments: Healthcare professionals will know the academic subject matter required for proficiency within their area. They will use this knowledge as needed in their role. The following accountability criteria are considered essential for students in a health science program of study.

document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards and Performance Indicators for Science

6FB093B2C71F445EB0ECB9E943A96F00.description: Plan and conduct scientific investigations to determine the factors that affect the strength of an electromagnet.

4990ADB760344881A014D9B7A4ACD2C1.description: Develop and use models to describe and compare the properties of magnets and electromagnets (including polarity, attraction, repulsion, and strength).

871726364FD3483D8E27566FD87AA03E.description: Magnets can exert forces on other magnets or magnetizable materials causing energy transfer between them, even when the objects are not touching. An electromagnet is produced when an electric current passes through a coil of wire wrapped around an iron core. Magnets and electromagnets have unique properties.

87AF4E249F794D608DE798568C6D9600.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations and investigations to classify different materials as either an insulator or conductor of electricity.

9B13B2F3A6F940CFB11DFCDD7DF9AE2B.description: Develop and use models to describe the path of an electric current in a complete simple circuit as it accomplishes a task (such as lighting a bulb or making a sound).

0F5637C776614088B8289ACF6D4A045E.description: Obtain and communicate information to develop models showing how electrical energy can be transformed into other forms of energy (including motion, sound, heat, or light).

389452DFCFFC4647B8297E5AF522FA0A.description: Energy can be transferred from place to place by electric currents. Electric currents flowing through a simple circuit can be used to produce motion, sound, heat, or light. Some materials allow electricity to flow through a circuit and some do not.

52E516425C4A447AB91ADF274F76B162.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of how electricity transfers energy and how magnetism can result from electricity.

B788289DCF7E4766ABB9B48236F535D2.description: Physical Science: Energy Transfer - Electricity and Magnetism

FDC3EA1F4BB14DF99D67FD9B5A0661AE.description: Define problems related to heat transfer and design devices or solutions that facilitate (conductor) or inhibit (insulator) the transfer of heat.

1133B681475740F49F9397267619F2A6.description: Obtain and communicate information to compare how different processes (including burning, friction, and electricity) serve as sources of heat energy.

D81069D0E0E9474EAB4AA915FCAF3C0F.description: Plan and conduct scientific investigations to determine how changes in heat (increase or decrease) change matter from one state to another (including melting, freezing, condensing, boiling, and evaporating).

AA6F86BF45C644ADA0B59CD407DBD5B9.description: Construct explanations using observations and measurements to describe how matter can be classified as a solid, liquid or gas.

E09C9C03975540C5A339995B37B3BFDC.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations and measurements to describe and compare the physical properties of matter (including length, mass, temperature, and volume of liquids).

60B31D56DBDE4E9F85B5A101B01D4941.description: Matter exists in several different states and is classified based on observable and measurable properties. Matter can be changed from one state to another when heat (thermal energy) is added or removed.

A8DFA63F4B914B8A96DC54570AAE21F4.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the properties used to classify matter and how heat energy can change matter from one state to another.

403DADD7FCD24C7AAD6E3D21D6EAADB7.description: Physical Science: Properties and Changes in Matter

8A4460F46BAB47199093A706C6C6EE5A.description: Define problems caused by a natural event or human activity and design devices or solutions to reduce the impact on the environment.

70855D9C677E431591A218EFA89FAB38.description: Obtain and communicate information to explain how natural events (such as fires, landslides, earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, or floods) and human activities (such as farming, mining, or building) impact the environment.

7119A6804E5741959CA01801F3D935FA.description: Plan and conduct scientific investigations to determine how natural processes (including weathering, erosion, and gravity) shape Earth's surface.

F15CE423EB5045F4864E9D7CE142C68C.description: Develop and use models to describe the characteristics of Earth's continental landforms and classify landforms as volcanoes, mountains, valleys, canyons, plains, and islands.

913E4126556C4305883F79ADE66145B4.description: Earth's surface has changed over time by natural processes and by human activities. Humans can take steps to reduce the impact of these changes.

86444AACA2C541DCB10402E0203DE587.description: Obtain and communicate information to exemplify how humans obtain, use, and protect renewable and nonrenewable Earth resources.

663AC90AFB3A4E09BCB1D535EC609F3F.description: Develop and use models to describe and classify the pattern distribution of land and water features on Earth.

6F35EFD5A0D941B7A26AE3B0A1D377B1.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations and measurements to describe and compare different Earth materials (including rocks, minerals, and soil) and classify each type of material based on its distinct physical properties.

7D9318C956DE40C7B6EA84A66A68C630.description: Earth is made of materials (including rocks, minerals, soil, and water) that have distinct properties. These materials provide resources for human activities.

675EF78C3D8F48C9B48A573EDE5A58C1.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the composition of Earth and the processes that shape features of Earth's surface.

72C4A1EEFD0B4FBEAAE5423B086E1CD2.description: Earth Science: Earth's Materials and Processes

34C75D3536234D3488D5D7735099F92A.description: Construct scientific arguments using evidence from fossils of plants and animals that lived long ago to infer the characteristics of early environments.

49CEAAABACAE46189AF2C08DC93D780B.description: Develop and use models to explain how changes in a habitat cause plants and animals to respond in different ways (such as hibernating, migrating, responding to light, death, or extinction).

9E73ACF3B3814A948D2B75A55C839A86.description: Obtain and communicate information to explain how changes in habitats (such as those that occur naturally or those caused by organisms) can be beneficial or harmful to the organisms that live there.

4EABCEEDCEDF49C99C82332ADEF80479.description: When the environment or habitat changes, some plants and animals survive and reproduce, some move to new locations, and some die. Fossils can be used to infer characteristics of environments from long ago.

CA87B1C92655481EBC20566EA2DAB4AD.description: Develop and use a food chain model to classify organisms as producers, consumers, and decomposers and to describe how organisms obtain energy.

D492DFCCB64E40F6B0426E8BD6FB431D.description: Analyze and interpret data about the characteristics of environments (including salt and fresh water, deserts, grasslands, forests, rain forests, and polar lands) to describe how the environment supports a variety of organisms.

FFBCF5E7D92546D9A1D5150AF2342A37.description: The characteristics of an environment (including physical characteristics, temperature, availability of resources, or the kinds and numbers of organisms present) influence the diversity of organisms that live there. Organisms can survive only in environments where their basic needs are met. All organisms need energy to live and grow. This energy is obtained from food. The role an organism serves in an ecosystem can be described by the way in which it gets its energy.

4316A220530D4B1D801ED67B449D55AD.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of how the characteristics and changes in environments and habitats affect the diversity of organisms.

222BF4E0F8B3475BBBA08D7F7E65FADC.description: Construct devices or design solutions to solve specific problems or needs: (1) ask questions to identify problems or needs, (2) ask questions about the criteria and constraints of the devices or solutions, (3) generate and communicate ideas for possible devices or solutions, (4) build and test devices or solutions, (5) determine if the devices or solutions solved the problem and refine the design if needed, and (6) communicate the results.

0C146196C4F84BEFB18895C8248E23B0.description: Technology is any modification to the natural world created to fulfill the wants and needs of humans. The engineering design process involves a series of iterative steps used to solve a problem and often leads to the development of a new or improved technology.

448BCC5C73FB4EE28A4DAAD88EB65F02.description: Obtain and evaluate informational texts, observations, data collected, or discussions to (1) generate and answer questions, (2) understand phenomena, (3) develop models, or (4) support explanations, claims, or designs. Communicate observations and explanations using the conventions and expectations of oral and written language.

301F747E0BA044DE82BB8B19728FF9C3.description: Construct scientific arguments to support claims, explanations, or designs using evidence from observations, data, or informational texts.

F8EC2263F48742129548FE79C72D32D9.description: Construct explanations of phenomena using (1) scientific evidence and models, (2) conclusions from scientific investigations, (3) predictions based on observations and measurements, or (4) data communicated in graphs, tables, or diagrams.

8402136162934CA79E13549B98E52A25.description: Use mathematical and computational thinking to (1) express quantitative observations using appropriate English or metric units, (2) collect and analyze data, or (3) understand patterns, trends and relationships.

1F6EB40198EE4D89A41701B9BC3CE135.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations, measurements, or investigations to understand patterns and meanings.

B1EA761C2B054B67AF0B6C00E4F51988.description: Plan and conduct scientific investigations to answer questions, test predictions and develop explanations: (1) formulate scientific questions and predict possible outcomes, (2) identify materials, procedures, and variables, (3) select and use appropriate tools or instruments to collect qualitative and quantitative data, and (4) record and represent data in an appropriate form. Use appropriate safety procedures.

B0495016C53E4F6C8C36D84B79DFBF8F.description: Develop, use, and refine models to (1) understand or represent phenomena, processes, and relationships, (2) test devices or solutions, or (3) communicate ideas to others.

89F1B2FFA03149A6BB4AE1C211AF329D.description: Ask questions that can be (1) answered using scientific investigations or (2) used to refine models, explanations, or designs.

62118C39016048CFBF2A94B22B7A2844.description: The practices of science and engineering support the development of science concepts, develop the habits of mind that are necessary for scientific thinking, and allow students to engage in science in ways that are similar to those used by scientists and engineers.

B779CB352822414A9AE69731C0F3174B.description: The student will use the science and engineering practices, including the processes and skills of scientific inquiry, to develop understandings of science content.

document.title: South Carolina College- and Career-Ready Standards for Mathematics

03E2D50F5F4C46DE9A28CFA1CC39A33A.description: Explain graphically and verbally the properties of the definite integral. Apply these properties to evaluate basic definite integrals.

492BC639B7674D6CAD42DC6F0B047C7A.description: Apply the Fundamental Theorems of Calculus to solve mathematical and real-world problems.

61AD8B4BA32F4096895AE502A263DB8D.description: Apply theorems and rules of integration to solve mathematical and real-world problems.

697234D34E6346DC87E9458DCF2E364D.description: Explain the relationship between the integral and derivative as expressed in both parts of the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus. Interpret the relationship in terms of rates of change.

B85173A552C647C58C84ECA51C400070.description: Interpret the definite integral as a limit of Riemann sums.

0993B084D27E4832AC3D6DD8615E801D.description: Approximate definite integrals by calculating Riemann sums using left, right, and mid-point evaluations, and using trapezoidal sums.

26EF6B7304ED4D37ACB870E608FDF604.description: Explain how the definite integral is used to solve area problems.

FAE562A2211B4D6498EBD8DE15F74B81.description: Understand the concept of the integral of a function geometrically, numerically, analytically, and contextually.

AA006DC27D4D4193938D9E2B30B40704.description: Solve a variety of real-world problems involving related rates, optimization, linear approximation, and rates of change.

E9B70C1461FB46EBA3450378F378B1AB.description: Explain the relationships among the concavity of the graph of ƒ, the increasing/decreasing behavior of ƒ′ and the signs of ƒ″. Use those relationships to generate graphs of ƒ, ƒ′, and ƒ″ given any one of them and identify the points of inflection of ƒ.

B92B84F3AA1C4902B7AC62877BFC6445.description: Explain the relationship between the increasing/decreasing behavior of ƒ and the signs of ƒ′. Use the relationship to generate a graph of ƒ given the graph of ƒ′, and vice versa, and to identify relative and absolute extrema of ƒ.

37DD03B1C004416887F16E6951F288E9.description: Write an equation of a line tangent to the graph of a function at a point.

A76BC95ECD744639B83706BA373B1769.description: Explain geometrically and verbally the mathematical and real-world meanings of the Extreme Value Theorem and the Mean Value Theorem.

5F35220CEDBA4E03A7ACF71788E2136D.description: Apply theorems and rules of differentiation to solve mathematical and real-world problems.

A3341C35FB4F420CB0FE4DA0F2B73D18.description: Understand and apply the methods of implicit and logarithmic differentiation.

D84666D423D742F5B2244E3EAD6B0C66.description: Use the constant multiple, sum, difference, product, quotient, and chain rules to find the derivatives of functions.

82D7E5D82CC54704A625B598F3A1E33C.description: Know and apply the derivatives of constant, power, trigonometric, inverse trigonometric, exponential, and logarithmic functions.

10E42731776349628FAA52E55D0C1738.description: Apply the rules of differentiation to functions.

46A2A1FB67C44CB4B4587B0736AA6F7B.description: Understand the definition of the derivative and use this definition to determine the derivatives of various functions.

95819C96760443D595AF5CA6A4097E70.description: Explain graphically and analytically the relationship between the average rate of change and the instantaneous rate of change.

B4CBD61D53E44907A77A89D16ABF7D34.description: Understand and explain graphically and analytically the relationship between differentiability and continuity.

E59406A9EE48484C89D993EB3E073281.description: Approximate the derivative graphically by finding the slope of the tangent line drawn to a curve at a given point and numerically by using the difference quotient.

2E7B1A73D4B7417F958E27240915A7E9.description: Interpret the value of the derivative as an instantaneous rate of change in a variety of real-world contexts such as velocity and population growth.

E5F3A8387022419F91C0EE689A39E090.description: Interpret the value of the derivative of a function as the slope of the corresponding tangent line.

004140FC7D2F4C3DA9578B05D0098EDE.description: Understand the concept of the derivative of a function geometrically, numerically, analytically, and verbally.

7378D098CD964006B726A29916D10853.description: Understand the Intermediate Value Theorem and apply the theorem to prove the existence of solutions of equations arising in mathematical and real-world problems.

5412CCD1314D4AB3942BE9D37BC01453.description: Classify discontinuities as removable, jump, or infinite. Justify that classification using the definition of continuity.

DC7AB9A6845C4794A8DDE292CFB695D8.description: Apply the definition of continuity of a function at a point to solve problems.

EB334918BBA64581915CED57F8345EC2.description: Understand the definition and graphical interpretation of continuity of a function.

48AA519C67AB433BB9D5CE687315ACAE.description: Calculate infinite limits and limits at infinity. Understand that infinite limits and limits at infinity provide information regarding the asymptotes of certain functions, including rational, exponential and logarithmic functions.

F47CD525A7674204AEF4D1C9FCB67CE7.description: Calculate limits, including one-sided limits, algebraically using direct substitution, simplification, rationalization, and the limit laws for constant multiples, sums, differences, products, and quotients.

A6BE5281DD704282890926E4131DC5F6.description: Estimate and verify limits using tables, graphs of functions, and technology.

B2490D16272742CB8098CDE33C58B232.description: Understand the concept of a limit graphically, numerically, analytically, and contextually.

37F4E7167F2E4C4A892A0D9EBF810E43.description: Analyze decisions and strategies using probability concepts.

31A28E3A382B44FE9F408876EB9E2785.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions. Use probabilities to make fair decisions.

1BBB369126F3468DA2028F25309FBB0B.description: Use probability to evaluate outcomes of decisions by finding expected values and determine if decisions are fair.

71A486550CEF42CC95463FB1B0CA9E9F.description: Construct and compare theoretical and experimental probability distributions and use those distributions to find expected values.

00C48DD90EA645358EAEE7632E79427D.description: Calculate the expected value of a random variable as the mean of its probability distribution. Find expected values by assigning probabilities to payoff values. Use expected values to evaluate and compare strategies in real-world scenarios.

EA9E6337EBC347D29A0A9837C51DC48F.description: Develop the probability distribution for a random variable defined for a sample space in which a theoretical probability can be calculated and graph the distribution.

FB8FC80DA27A4B8F9911133C914B54B3.description: Create residual plots and analyze those plots to compare the fit of linear, quadratic, and exponential models to a given data set. Select the appropriate model and use it for interpolation.

D97A0CCFF4C24C76B1D9FFDADF1CC095.description: Differentiate between correlation and causation when describing the relationship between two variables. Identify potential lurking variables which may explain an association between two variables.

EE8D72CFE66F4529B60F957A9D698356.description: Using technology, compute and interpret the correlation coefficient of a linear fit.

85A9A4381BC145BF8AD8C1745AF664B4.description: Create a linear function to graphically model data from a real-world problem and interpret the meaning of the slope and intercept(s) in the context of the given problem.

B1166B5CDFC74CCF90984694ECDBCF25.description: Using technology, create scatterplots and analyze those plots to compare the fit of linear, quadratic, or exponential models to a given data set. Select the appropriate model, fit a function to the data set, and use the function to solve problems in the context of the data.

808DD27293F846A9994982A032306D56.description: Analyze bivariate categorical data using two-way tables and identify possible associations between the two categories using marginal, joint, and conditional frequencies.

47D66BEBADA44125B4E74524BBF10B90.description: Use the mean and standard deviation of a data set to fit it to a normal distribution and to estimate population percentages. Recognize that there are data sets for which such a procedure is not appropriate. Use calculators, spreadsheets, and tables to estimate areas under the normal curve.

4312858206E34E92BC9A08380706A3AC.description: Summarize and represent data from a single data set. Interpret differences in shape, center, and spread in the context of the data set, accounting for possible effects of extreme data points (outliers).

7C5760BA7EF6480DB61FA947EC727A16.description: Use statistics appropriate to the shape of the data distribution to compare center and spread of two or more different data sets that include all real numbers.
