62CC8BE0DFE701319F7168A86D17958E.description: Apply an algorithm to add and subtract whole numbers fluently.

62CC45C0DFE701319F7068A86D17958E.description: Represent in word form whole numbers through nine hundred ninety-nine thousand.

62CBFC60DFE701319F6F68A86D17958E.description: Compare whole-number quantities through 999,999 by using the terms is less than, is greater than, and is equal to and the symbols <, >, and =.

62CBBD10DFE701319F6E68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate through the mathematical processes an understanding of the representation of whole numbers and fractional parts; the addition and subtraction of whole numbers; accurate, efficient, and generalizable methods of multiplying whole numbers; and the relationships among multiplication, division, and related basic facts.

62CB4120DFE701319F6C68A86D17958E.description: Recognize the limitations of various forms of mathematical representations.

62CAC030DFE701319F6A68A86D17958E.description: Generalize connections between new mathematical ideas and related concepts and subjects that have been previously considered.

62CA7430DFE701319F6968A86D17958E.description: Use correct, complete, and clearly written and oral mathematical language to pose questions, communicate ideas, and extend problem situations.

62CA2C40DFE701319F6868A86D17958E.description: Generate descriptions and mathematical statements about relationships between and among classes of objects.

62C9E4B0DFE701319F6768A86D17958E.description: Explain and justify answers on the basis of mathematical properties, structures, and relationships.

62C9A1C0DFE701319F6668A86D17958E.description: Construct arguments that lead to conclusions about general mathematical properties and relationships.

62C95F20DFE701319F6568A86D17958E.description: Analyze information to solve increasingly more sophisticated problems.

62C91980DFE701319F6468A86D17958E.description: The student will understand and utilize the mathematical processes of problem solving, reasoning and proof, communication, connections, and representation.

document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards for the Visual and Performing Arts - Theatre

54F3A690DFE701318A1F68A86D17958E.description: Recognize ways that live and recorded theatre relates to real life.

54F35F20DFE701318A1E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the historical and cultural contexts of improvisations and published plays.

54F2FA70DFE701318A1D68A86D17958E.description: Identify theatrical practices in a variety of historical periods and cultures and recognize them in contemporary informal and formal productions.

54F2A270DFE701318A1C68A86D17958E.description: The student will understand context by analyzing the role of theatre, film, television, and other electronic media in his or her community and the state of South Carolina as well as in other cultures, both past and present.

54F21D60DFE701318A1A68A86D17958E.description: Critique classroom performances on the basis of characterization, diction, pacing, and staging and then make suggestions for improvement.

54F1D4F0DFE701318A1968A86D17958E.description: Develop standards to critique both live and electronic theatre productions.

54F17110DFE701318A1868A86D17958E.description: Incorporate components of dramatic criticism to evaluate dramatic texts.

54F118E0DFE701318A1768A86D17958E.description: Use audience etiquette during theatre performances.

54F0DBE0DFE701318A1668A86D17958E.description: The student will analyze, evaluate, and derive meanings from improvised and scripted scenes, live theatre performances, and theatrical performances on film, television, and other electronic media.

54F05C60DFE701318A1468A86D17958E.description: Recognize that theatre is a synthesis of all the arts.

54F01A80DFE701318A1368A86D17958E.description: Compare and contrast different career and social roles within the arts.

54EFD6D0DFE701318A1268A86D17958E.description: Integrate the use of creative writing, visual arts, dance, music, and/or electronic media to enhance theatre activities.

54EF8E70DFE701318A1168A86D17958E.description: The student will make connections between theatre and other arts disciplines, other content areas, and the world.

54EF11E0DFE701318A0F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the use and importance of headshot photographs for those pursuing a career in acting.

54EED370DFE701318A0E68A86D17958E.description: Research the components of a résumé for various careers in theatre.

54EE95B0DFE701318A0D68A86D17958E.description: Use print and nonprint sources to research careers in theatre.

54EE4F30DFE701318A0C68A86D17958E.description: Apply research from print and nonprint sources to plan writing, acting, designing, and directing activities.

54EE0360DFE701318A0B68A86D17958E.description: Research the cultural and historical contexts of theatre to support improvised and scripted scenes.

54ED9FC0DFE701318A0A68A86D17958E.description: The student will use appropriate practices to research and inform his or her understanding of all aspects of theatre.

54ED1A60DFE701318A0868A86D17958E.description: Direct short scenes incorporating simple blocking techniques.

54ECD860DFE701318A0768A86D17958E.description: Identify the requirements of basic stage composition.

54EC9860DFE701318A0668A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the role and responsibilities of the director.

54EC0050DFE701318A0468A86D17958E.description: Design coherent stage management, promotional, and marketing plans.

54EB9620DFE701318A0368A86D17958E.description: Create technical elements for the theatre (for example, scenery, lighting, sound) incorporating the fundamental principles of design.

54EB43B0DFE701318A0268A86D17958E.description: Analyze improvised and scripted scenes for basic technical requirements and justify his or her choices.

54EAFDA0DFE701318A0168A86D17958E.description: Identify tools and materials for basic technical design and construction of scenery, lighting, sound, costumes, and makeup.

54EABF40DFE701318A0068A86D17958E.description: Categorize the functions and interrelated nature of scenery, props, lighting, sound, costumes, and makeup in creating an environment appropriate for scripted and nonscripted theatre.

54EA7F00DFE7013189FF68A86D17958E.description: The student will design a variety of technical elements for the theatre.

54E9F140DFE7013189FD68A86D17958E.description: Act as an improvised or scripted character in an ensemble.

54E9B230DFE7013189FC68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the given circumstances of the script or scenario in order to explain and justify character motivation.

54E96DE0DFE7013189FB68A86D17958E.description: Research and observe people to create characters.

54E92D30DFE7013189FA68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate skills of sensory recall, concentration, collaboration, and ensemble building.

54E8EB60DFE7013189F968A86D17958E.description: Utilize vocal acting skills (for example, breath control, appropriate tone of voice, voice placement, and effective speech).

54E8A790DFE7013189F868A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate physical control and expression through improvisation, pantomime, and character exercises.

54E86290DFE7013189F768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate a knowledge of essential acting vocabulary (for example, blocking, objective, motivation, projection, diction, rate, pitch).

54E81910DFE7013189F668A86D17958E.description: The student will develop acting skills that allow him or her to portray a variety of characters in both improvised and scripted dramatic presentations.

54E79B30DFE7013189F468A86D17958E.description: Use correct playwriting format to write and revise monologues and scenes that include the basic elements of plot structure.

54E75C90DFE7013189F368A86D17958E.description: Use theatre vocabulary to analyze the elements of a drama (including theme, character, climax, and catharsis).

54E713D0DFE7013189F268A86D17958E.description: Improvise characters, environments, dialogue, and action both individually and in groups.

54E6CDE0DFE7013189F168A86D17958E.description: The student will create improvised scenes and written scripts based on his or her own experiences and imagination as well as on literature, history and culture, and current events.

document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards for Health and Safety Education

695D2D30DFE70131A9B868A86D17958E.description: Encourage peers, family, and others to choose healthy foods and be physically active.

695CE120DFE70131A9B768A86D17958E.description: Utilize strategies to promote keeping the environment clean and safe.

695C8CF0DFE70131A9B668A86D17958E.description: Advocate for disaster preparedness for home and school.

695C4C30DFE70131A9B568A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate the ability to advocate for personal, family, and consumer health.

695C09B0DFE70131A9B468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate food choices and physical activity behaviors that reduce or help eliminate health risks, including obesity and tooth decay.

695BB520DFE70131A9B368A86D17958E.description: Implement strategies for dealing with peer pressure.

695B6C30DFE70131A9B268A86D17958E.description: Practice safety rules when he or she is home alone and with others.

695B24F0DFE70131A9B168A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate strategies for dealing with conflict, bullying, and violence.

695ADBA0DFE70131A9B068A86D17958E.description: Implement safety strategies to avoid causing injury to him- or herself and to others (for example, wearing sunscreen, wearing flotation equipment, being aware of weather conditions, knowing fire safety procedures).

695A8F20DFE70131A9AF68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate positive self-management skills (for example, managing stress, controlling anger and other impulses).

695A4BF0DFE70131A9AE68A86D17958E.description: Practice behaviors that promote healthy relationships with families and peers.

695A0920DFE70131A9AD68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate the ability to practice health-enhancing behaviors and avoid or reduce health risks.

6959C3F0DFE70131A9AC68A86D17958E.description: Construct a plan, including monitoring and assessing progress, to achieve a health goal (for example, reduce stress, be physically active, get more sleep, limit the amount of sugary foods/drinks in the diet.)

69597D40DFE70131A9AB68A86D17958E.description: Identify ways that ATOD use can interfere with a person's achievement of his or her goals.

69592C00DFE70131A9AA68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate the ability to use goal-setting skills to enhance health.

6958CC00DFE70131A9A968A86D17958E.description: Describe physical activities that promote health-related fitness.

69587DC0DFE70131A9A868A86D17958E.description: Select healthy foods from a fast food restaurant menu.

69583B40DFE70131A9A768A86D17958E.description: Discuss the benefits of deciding to abstain from sexual activity and to remain abstinent.

6957F910DFE70131A9A668A86D17958E.description: Explain how ATOD can affect the way individuals make decisions and perform tasks.

6957B3B0DFE70131A9A568A86D17958E.description: Describe what to do if someone displays a weapon at home, at the school, or in the community.

695771E0DFE70131A9A468A86D17958E.description: Decide when he or she needs to seek help to protect personal safety or that of others.

69572BB0DFE70131A9A368A86D17958E.description: Identify instances when it is important to seek information, support, and assistance regarding mental, emotional, and social health.

6956E190DFE70131A9A268A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate the ability to use decision-making skills to enhance health.

6956A240DFE70131A9A168A86D17958E.description: Discuss with family members and peers ways to minimize screen time and be physically active.

69566080DFE70131A9A068A86D17958E.description: Discuss with family members and peers ways to make healthy food choices.

695618A0DFE70131A99F68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate refusal skills to avoid or reduce health risks.

6955B670DFE70131A99E68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ways to ask for assistance in harmful situations or relationships.

695546E0DFE70131A99D68A86D17958E.description: Discuss ways to communicate with parents, teachers, or other trustworthy adults about the stages of growth and development that take place during adolescence.

695506C0DFE70131A99C68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate effective refusal skills regarding ATOD.

6954C5C0DFE70131A99B68A86D17958E.description: Utilize effective communication strategies (including negotiation skills) to resolve conflicts and promote personal safety.

69548050DFE70131A99A68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate the ability to use interpersonal communication skills to enhance health and avoid or reduce health risks.

695438B0DFE70131A99968A86D17958E.description: Locate resources that provide information on the link between excessive sugar consumption and diseases (for example, obesity, diabetes, tooth decay).

6953F6D0DFE70131A99868A86D17958E.description: Locate resources from home, school, and community that provide valid health information.

6953AF90DFE70131A99768A86D17958E.description: Locate people in the family, school or community (for example, parents, teachers, nurses, doctors, clergy) who can provide valid health information about the changes that occur during puberty.

69535A70DFE70131A99668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to locate valid information and resources concerning ATOD.

69531B90DFE70131A99568A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate the ability to access valid information and products and services to enhance health.

6952DB90DFE70131A99468A86D17958E.description: Examine the various strategies used by the media to influence food choices and physical activity.

695297E0DFE70131A99368A86D17958E.description: Discuss how the family, peers, school, community, and culture can influence personal health practices and behaviors.

69525860DFE70131A99268A86D17958E.description: Discuss the influences of peers and family on behaviors related to the use of tobacco products, including smokeless tobacco.

69521550DFE70131A99168A86D17958E.description: Analyze media messages on the subject of violence and risk behaviors.

6951CC00DFE70131A99068A86D17958E.description: Discuss family, peer, and cultural influences on the way an individual deals with conflict.

69517900DFE70131A98F68A86D17958E.description: Explain ways that the media influences an individual's thoughts, feelings, self-concept, and health behaviors.

69513110DFE70131A98E68A86D17958E.description: The student will analyze the influence of family, peers, culture, media, technology, and other factors on health behaviors.

6950E1D0DFE70131A98D68A86D17958E.description: Explain basic precautions to help prevent injury during physical activity.

69509B60DFE70131A98C68A86D17958E.description: Discuss the benefits of moderate to vigorous physical activity.

695054F0DFE70131A98B68A86D17958E.description: Describe methods of safe food handling and preparation.

694FF720DFE70131A98A68A86D17958E.description: Identify the benefits of following the federal dietary guidelines.

694F9050DFE70131A98968A86D17958E.description: Examine the six essential nutrients, their function, and foods or food groups in which they are present.

694F5100DFE70131A98868A86D17958E.description: Identify ways that health care providers promote health and detect and treat problems.

694F1310DFE70131A98768A86D17958E.description: Describe ways that family health history can affect a person's health (for example, heart disease, diabetes, sickle cell anemia).

694ED500DFE70131A98668A86D17958E.description: Discuss the barriers to a person's practicing healthy behaviors.

694E5330DFE70131A98468A86D17958E.description: Describe the physical, emotional, and social changes that occur in puberty and adolescence (for example, changes in voice, growth of body and facial hair, sensitivity to peer influence, mood swings).

694E0BE0DFE70131A98368A86D17958E.description: Describe the link between alcohol use, injury, and disease.

694DBBF0DFE70131A98268A86D17958E.description: Explain the link between tobacco use and diseases, including oral disease.

694D31F0DFE70131A98068A86D17958E.description: Discuss the social, economic, and physical consequences of ATOD use.

694CF030DFE70131A97F68A86D17958E.description: Describe the structures and function of the respiratory system (for example, lungs, bronchioles, diaphragm).

694CACB0DFE70131A97E68A86D17958E.description: Explain CPR (cardiopulmonary resuscitation) and rescue breathing.

694C6370DFE70131A97D68A86D17958E.description: Examine the impact of violent and unsafe behaviors.

694BF7F0DFE70131A97C68A86D17958E.description: Describe coping strategies to promote mental health (for example, engaging in physical activity, reading, playing or listening to music, writing).

694AADA0DFE70131A97B68A86D17958E.description: The student will comprehend concepts related to health promotion to enhance health.

document.title: Common Core State Standards for Mathematics

61A4F4B0DFE701319D6E68A86D17958E.description: Design and use a simulation to generate frequencies for compound events.
comments: For example, use random digits as a simulation tool to approximate the answer to the question: If 40% of donors have type A blood, what is the probability that it will take at least 4 donors to find one with type A blood?

61A49B70DFE701319D6D68A86D17958E.description: Represent sample spaces for compound events using methods such as organized lists, tables and tree diagrams. For an event described in everyday language (e.g., "rolling double sixes"), identify the outcomes in the sample space which compose the event.

61A44840DFE701319D6C68A86D17958E.description: Understand that, just as with simple events, the probability of a compound event is the fraction of outcomes in the sample space for which the compound event occurs.

61A3EF50DFE701319D6B68A86D17958E.description: Find probabilities of compound events using organized lists, tables, tree diagrams, and simulation.

61A38250DFE701319D6A68A86D17958E.description: Develop a probability model (which may not be uniform) by observing frequencies in data generated from a chance process.
comments: For example, find the approximate probability that a spinning penny will land heads up or that a tossed paper cup will land open-end down. Do the outcomes for the spinning penny appear to be equally likely based on the observed frequencies?

61A33330DFE701319D6968A86D17958E.description: Develop a uniform probability model by assigning equal probability to all outcomes, and use the model to determine probabilities of events.
comments: For example, if a student is selected at random from a class, find the probability that Jane will be selected and the probability that a girl will be selected.

61A2EC00DFE701319D6868A86D17958E.description: Develop a probability model and use it to find probabilities of events. Compare probabilities from a model to observed frequencies; if the agreement is not good, explain possible sources of the discrepancy.

61A2A860DFE701319D6768A86D17958E.description: Approximate the probability of a chance event by collecting data on the chance process that produces it and observing its long-run relative frequency, and predict the approximate relative frequency given the probability.
comments: For example, when rolling a number cube 600 times, predict that a 3 or 6 would be rolled roughly 200 times, but probably not exactly 200 times.

61A264C0DFE701319D6668A86D17958E.description: Understand that the probability of a chance event is a number between 0 and 1 that expresses the likelihood of the event occurring. Larger numbers indicate greater likelihood. A probability near 0 indicates an unlikely event, a probability around 1/2 indicates an event that is neither unlikely nor likely, and a probability near 1 indicates a likely event.

61A22270DFE701319D6568A86D17958E.description: Investigate chance processes and develop, use, and evaluate probability models.

comments: For example, decide whether the words in a chapter of a seventh-grade science book are generally longer than the words in a chapter of a fourth-grade science book.
61A1DBA0DFE701319D6468A86D17958E.description: Use measures of center and measures of variability for numerical data from random samples to draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

61A18F30DFE701319D6368A86D17958E.description: Informally assess the degree of visual overlap of two numerical data distributions with similar variabilities, measuring the difference between the centers by expressing it as a multiple of a measure of variability.
comments: For example, the mean height of players on the basketball team is 10 cm greater than the mean height of players on the soccer team, about twice the variability (mean absolute deviation) on either team; on a dot plot, the separation between the two distributions of heights is noticeable.

61A14170DFE701319D6268A86D17958E.description: Draw informal comparative inferences about two populations.

61A0F7D0DFE701319D6168A86D17958E.description: Use data from a random sample to draw inferences about a population with an unknown characteristic of interest. Generate multiple samples (or simulated samples) of the same size to gauge the variation in estimates or predictions.
comments: For example, estimate the mean word length in a book by randomly sampling words from the book; predict the winner of a school election based on randomly sampled survey data. Gauge how far off the estimate or prediction might be.

61A0B0D0DFE701319D6068A86D17958E.description: Understand that statistics can be used to gain information about a population by examining a sample of the population; generalizations about a population from a sample are valid only if the sample is representative of that population. Understand that random sampling tends to produce representative samples and support valid inferences.

61A06AA0DFE701319D5F68A86D17958E.description: Use random sampling to draw inferences about a population.

619FCA50DFE701319D5D68A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems leading to inequalities of the form px + q > r or px + q < r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Graph the solution set of the inequality and interpret it in the context of the problem.
comments: For example: As a salesperson, you are paid $50 per week plus $3 per sale. This week you want your pay to be at least $100. Write an inequality for the number of sales you need to make, and describe the solutions.

619F6110DFE701319D5C68A86D17958E.description: Solve word problems leading to equations of the form px + q = r and p(x + q) = r, where p, q, and r are specific rational numbers. Solve equations of these forms fluently. Compare an algebraic solution to an arithmetic solution, identifying the sequence of the operations used in each approach.
comments: For example, the perimeter of a rectangle is 54 cm. Its length is 6 cm. What is its width?

619F1530DFE701319D5B68A86D17958E.description: Use variables to represent quantities in a real-world or mathematical problem, and construct simple equations and inequalities to solve problems by reasoning about the quantities.

comments: For example: If a woman making $25 an hour gets a 10% raise, she will make an additional 1/10 of her salary an hour, or $2.50, for a new salary of $27.50. If you want to place a towel bar 9 3/4 inches long in the center of a door that is 27 1/2 inches wide, you will need to place the bar about 9 inches from each edge; this estimate can be used as a check on the exact computation.
619ECAF0DFE701319D5A68A86D17958E.description: Solve multi-step real-life and mathematical problems posed with positive and negative rational numbers in any form (whole numbers, fractions, and decimals), using tools strategically. Apply properties of operations to calculate with numbers in any form; convert between forms as appropriate; and assess the reasonableness of answers using mental computation and estimation strategies.

619E8610DFE701319D5968A86D17958E.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems using numerical and algebraic expressions and equations.

619E3590DFE701319D5868A86D17958E.description: Understand that rewriting an expression in different forms in a problem context can shed light on the problem and how the quantities in it are related.
comments: For example, a + 0.05a = 1.05a means that "increase by 5%" is the same as "multiply by 1.05."

619DD5F0DFE701319D5768A86D17958E.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add, subtract, factor, and expand linear expressions with rational coefficients.

619D8330DFE701319D5668A86D17958E.description: Use properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

comments: Computations with rational numbers extend the rules for manipulating fractions to complex fractions.
619CEC30DFE701319D5468A86D17958E.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the four operations with rational numbers.

619CAA30DFE701319D5368A86D17958E.description: Convert a rational number to a decimal using long division; know that the decimal form of a rational number terminates in 0s or eventually repeats.

619C6540DFE701319D5268A86D17958E.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to multiply and divide rational numbers.

619C17E0DFE701319D5168A86D17958E.description: Understand that integers can be divided, provided that the divisor is not zero, and every quotient of integers (with non-zero divisor) is a rational number. If p and q are integers, then -(p/q) = (-p)/q = p/(-q). Interpret quotients of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

619BC760DFE701319D5068A86D17958E.description: Understand that multiplication is extended from fractions to rational numbers by requiring that operations continue to satisfy the properties of operations, particularly the distributive property, leading to products such as (-1)(-1) = 1 and the rules for multiplying signed numbers. Interpret products of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

619B8300DFE701319D4F68A86D17958E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers.

619B3F50DFE701319D4E68A86D17958E.description: Apply properties of operations as strategies to add and subtract rational numbers.

619AF340DFE701319D4D68A86D17958E.description: Understand subtraction of rational numbers as adding the additive inverse, p - q = p + (-q). Show that the distance between two rational numbers on the number line is the absolute value of their difference, and apply this principle in real-world contexts.

619AA700DFE701319D4C68A86D17958E.description: Understand p + q as the number located a distance |q| from p, in the positive or negative direction depending on whether q is positive or negative. Show that a number and its opposite have a sum of 0 (are additive inverses). Interpret sums of rational numbers by describing real-world contexts.

619A5010DFE701319D4B68A86D17958E.description: Describe situations in which opposite quantities combine to make 0.
comments: For example, a hydrogen atom has 0 charge because its two constituents are oppositely charged.

6199EDF0DFE701319D4A68A86D17958E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of addition and subtraction to add and subtract rational numbers; represent addition and subtraction on a horizontal or vertical number line diagram.

6199AD50DFE701319D4968A86D17958E.description: Apply and extend previous understandings of operations with fractions to add, subtract, multiply, and divide rational numbers.

61992A00DFE701319D4768A86D17958E.description: Use proportional relationships to solve multistep ratio and percent problems.
comments: Examples: simple interest, tax, markups and markdowns, gratuities and commissions, fees, percent increase and decrease, percent error.

6198E5B0DFE701319D4668A86D17958E.description: Explain what a point (x, y) on the graph of a proportional relationship means in terms of the situation, with special attention to the points (0, 0) and (1, r) where r is the unit rate.

comments: For example, if total cost t is proportional to the number n of items purchased at a constant price p, the relationship between the total cost and the number of items can be expressed as t = pn.

619844C0DFE701319D4468A86D17958E.description: Identify the constant of proportionality (unit rate) in tables, graphs, equations, diagrams, and verbal descriptions of proportional relationships.

6197F380DFE701319D4368A86D17958E.description: Decide whether two quantities are in a proportional relationship, e.g., by testing for equivalent ratios in a table or graphing on a coordinate plane and observing whether the graph is a straight line through the origin.

6197B040DFE701319D4268A86D17958E.description: Recognize and represent proportional relationships between quantities.

comments: For example, if a person walks 1/2 mile in each 1/4 hour, compute the unit rate as the complex fraction <sup>1/2</sup>/<sub>1/4</sub> miles per hour, equivalently 2 miles per hour.
61976B80DFE701319D4168A86D17958E.description: Compute unit rates associated with ratios of fractions, including ratios of lengths, areas and other quantities measured in like or different units.

61972790DFE701319D4068A86D17958E.description: Analyze proportional relationships and use them to solve real-world and mathematical problems.

6196A190DFE701319D3E68A86D17958E.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, volume and surface area of two- and three-dimensional objects composed of triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, cubes, and right prisms.

619652E0DFE701319D3D68A86D17958E.description: Use facts about supplementary, complementary, vertical, and adjacent angles in a multi-step problem to write and solve simple equations for an unknown angle in a figure.

619608A0DFE701319D3C68A86D17958E.description: Know the formulas for the area and circumference of a circle and use them to solve problems; give an informal derivation of the relationship between the circumference and area of a circle.

6195AEC0DFE701319D3B68A86D17958E.description: Solve real-life and mathematical problems involving angle measure, area, surface area, and volume.

61955CF0DFE701319D3A68A86D17958E.description: Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.

61950A80DFE701319D3968A86D17958E.description: Draw (freehand, with ruler and protractor, and with technology) geometric shapes with given conditions. Focus on constructing triangles from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle.

6194C050DFE701319D3868A86D17958E.description: Solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures, including computing actual lengths and areas from a scale drawing and reproducing a scale drawing at a different scale.

61947430DFE701319D3768A86D17958E.description: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them.

6193E370DFE701319D3568A86D17958E.description: Look for and express regularity in repeated reasoning.
comments: Mathematically proficient students notice if calculations are repeated, and look both for general methods and for shortcuts. Upper elementary students might notice when dividing 25 by 11 that they are repeating the same calculations over and over again, and conclude they have a repeating decimal. By paying attention to the calculation of slope as they repeatedly check whether points are on the line through (1, 2) with slope 3, middle school students might abstract the equation (y – 2)/(x – 1) = 3. Noticing the regularity in the way terms cancel when expanding (x – 1)(x + 1), (x – 1)(x² + x + 1), and (x – 1)(x³ + x² + x + 1) might lead them to the general formula for the sum of a geometric series. As they work to solve a problem, mathematically proficient students maintain oversight of the process, while attending to the details. They continually evaluate the reasonableness of their intermediate results.

61939590DFE701319D3468A86D17958E.description: Look for and make use of structure.
comments: Mathematically proficient students look closely to discern a pattern or structure. Young students, for example, might notice that three and seven more is the same amount as seven and three more, or they may sort a collection of shapes according to how many sides the shapes have. Later, students will see 7 × 8 equals the well remembered 7 × 5 + 7 × 3, in preparation for learning about the distributive property. In the expression x² + 9x + 14, older students can see the 14 as 2 × 7 and the 9 as 2 + 7. They recognize the significance of an existing line in a geometric figure and can use the strategy of drawing an auxiliary line for solving problems. They also can step back for an overview and shift perspective. They can see complicated things, such as some algebraic expressions, as single objects or as being composed of several objects. For example, they can see 5 – 3(x – y)² as 5 minus a positive number times a square and use that to realize that its value cannot be more than 5 for any real numbers x and y.

Mathematically proficient students try to communicate precisely to others. They try to use clear definitions in discussion with others and in their own reasoning. They state the meaning of the symbols they choose, including using the equal sign consistently and appropriately. They are careful about specifying units of measure, and labeling axes to clarify the correspondence with quantities in a problem. They calculate accurately and efficiently, express numerical answers with a degree of precision appropriate for the problem context. In the elementary grades, students give carefully formulated explanations to each other. By the time they reach high school they have learned to examine claims and make explicit use of definitions.

Mathematically proficient students consider the available tools when solving a mathematical problem. These tools might include pencil and paper, concrete models, a ruler, a protractor, a calculator, a spreadsheet, a computer algebra system, a statistical package, or dynamic geometry software. Proficient students are sufficiently familiar with tools appropriate for their grade or course to make sound decisions about when each of these tools might be helpful, recognizing both the insight to be gained and their limitations. For example, mathematically proficient high school students analyze graphs of functions and solutions generated using a graphing calculator. They detect possible errors by strategically using estimation and other mathematical knowledge. When making mathematical models, they know that technology can enable them to visualize the results of varying assumptions, explore consequences, and compare predictions with data. Mathematically proficient students at various grade levels are able to identify relevant external mathematical resources, such as digital content located on a website, and use them to pose or solve problems. They are able to use technological tools to explore and deepen their understanding of concepts.

Mathematically proficient students can apply the mathematics they know to solve problems arising in everyday life, society, and the workplace. In early grades, this might be as simple as writing an addition equation to describe a situation. In middle grades, a student might apply proportional reasoning to plan a school event or analyze a problem in the community. By high school, a student might use geometry to solve a design problem or use a function to describe how one quantity of interest depends on another. Mathematically proficient students who can apply what they know are comfortable making assumptions and approximations to simplify a complicated situation, realizing that these may need revision later. They are able to identify important quantities in a practical situation and map their relationships using such tools as diagrams, two-way tables, graphs, flowcharts and formulas. They can analyze those relationships mathematically to draw conclusions. They routinely interpret their mathematical results in the context of the situation and reflect on whether the results make sense, possibly improving the model if it has not served its purpose.

61921AD0DFE701319D3068A86D17958E.description: Construct viable arguments and critique the reasoning of others.
comments: Mathematically proficient students understand and use stated assumptions, definitions, and previously established results in constructing arguments. They make conjectures and build a logical progression of statements to explore the truth of their conjectures. They are able to analyze situations by breaking them into cases, and can recognize and use counterexamples. They justify their conclusions, communicate them to others, and respond to the arguments of others. They reason inductively about data, making plausible arguments that take into account the context from which the data arose. Mathematically proficient students are also able to compare the effectiveness of two plausible arguments, distinguish correct logic or reasoning from that which is flawed, and—if there is a flaw in an argument—explain what it is. Elementary students can construct arguments using concrete referents such as objects, drawings, diagrams, and actions. Such arguments can make sense and be correct, even though they are not generalized or made formal until later grades. Later, students learn to determine domains to which an argument applies. Students at all grades can listen or read the arguments of others, decide whether they make sense, and ask useful questions to clarify or improve the arguments.

Mathematically proficient students make sense of quantities and their relationships in problem situations. They bring two complementary abilities to bear on problems involving quantitative relationships: the ability to decontextualize—to abstract a given situation and represent it symbolically and manipulate the representing symbols as if they have a life of their own, without necessarily attending to their referents—and the ability to contextualize, to pause as needed during the manipulation process in order to probe into the referents for the symbols involved. Quantitative reasoning entails habits of creating a coherent representation of the problem at hand; considering the units involved; attending to the meaning of quantities, not just how to compute them; and knowing and flexibly using different properties of operations and objects.

Mathematically proficient students start by explaining to themselves the meaning of a problem and looking for entry points to its solution. They analyze givens, constraints, relationships, and goals. They make conjectures about the form and meaning of the solution and plan a solution pathway rather than simply jumping into a solution attempt. They consider analogous problems, and try special cases and simpler forms of the original problem in order to gain insight into its solution. They monitor and evaluate their progress and change course if necessary. Older students might, depending on the context of the problem, transform algebraic expressions or change the viewing window on their graphing calculator to get the information they need. Mathematically proficient students can explain correspondences between equations, verbal descriptions, tables, and graphs or draw diagrams of important features and relationships, graph data, and search for regularity or trends. Younger students might rely on using concrete objects or pictures to help conceptualize and solve a problem. Mathematically proficient students check their answers to problems using a different method, and they continually ask themselves, "Does this make sense?" They can understand the approaches of others to solving complex problems and identify correspondences between different approaches.
61917AC0DFE701319D2E68A86D17958E.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards for the Visual and Performing Arts - Visual Arts

AE9F73AA19874FFD8D7680C0459BFDAF.description: Develop an understanding of mixed numbers (i.e., denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10) as iterations of unit fractions on a number line.

84D5EC320E9D4D55ADD0C64DB38050FD.description: fractions with the same numerator or same denominator can be compared by reasoning about their size based on the same whole.

F9CB1AEB561D4012A991305C514B1582.description: whole numbers can be written as fractions (e.g., 4 = 4/1 and 1 = 4/4);

E2BDB3F3D23F41C58494D7E6FD5D3048.description: fraction equivalence can be represented using set, area, and linear models;

AF9B4A60699F440EBC5D785457C7DFF1.description: two fractions are equal if they are the same size, based on the same whole, or at the same point on a number line;

E757B70D33624D2DA56AB9B617EE756E.description: Explain fraction equivalence (i.e., denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10) by demonstrating an understanding that:

D1872551D8CB486CBD667C6C2A6AAC39.description: A fraction can be represented using set, area, and linear models.

17F0366449E043C797E7CB3B60AC44E2.description: A fraction is a number that can be represented on a number line based on counts of a unit fraction;

7324FFC0D89E4C37A19745952934C25A.description: A fraction a/b is the quantity formed by a parts of size 1/b;

FEC5B78E7EA94BC78406A6AB67982D77.description: A fraction 1/b (called a unit fraction) is the quantity formed by one part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts;

429E1F5196FD4784AE65FA1F58DF9D9E.description: Develop an understanding of fractions (i.e., denominators 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10) as numbers.

923B3E9595DD448D9D6B527D3E94E9D4.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving perimeters of polygons, including finding the perimeter given the side lengths, finding an unknown side length, and exhibiting rectangles with the same perimeter and different areas or with the same area and different perimeters.

6B509CD0392E40B980F336BB66F601CD.description: Determine the area of a rectilinear polygon and relate to multiplication and addition.

37FC8EA0780947278BD24FB1A7A3CD4B.description: Measure area by building arrays and counting standard unit squares;

E0A5820838854CF19690A0F7BF8CCD11.description: Recognize area as an attribute of plane figures;

DF59D99768EA4D35B01947E3D5A69002.description: Understand the concept of area measurement.

EC457AF6365F40C8AE63A257F6944FF9.description: Generate data by measuring length to the nearest inch, half-inch and quarter-inch and organize the data in a line plot using a horizontal scale marked off in appropriate units.

0957C1ABB2F74AEBA311FAB4E2DD0A27.description: Collect, organize, classify, and interpret data with multiple categories and draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent the data.

04CCAB065B6249F6B62A7F114A556263.description: Estimate and measure liquid volumes (capacity) in customary units (i.e., c., pt., qt., gal.) and metric units (mL, L) to the nearest whole unit.

E10988849FF74A688E7704539DDCA244.description: Use analog and digital clocks to determine and record time to the nearest minute, using a.m. and p.m.; measure time intervals in minutes; and solve problems involving addition and subtraction of time intervals within 60 minutes.

3ACE9AEE2DC34767B4790B6FBE565B47.description: Identify a three-dimensional shape (i.e., right rectangular prism, right triangular prism, pyramid) based on a given two-dimensional net and explain the relationship between the shape and the net.

9AC4832F73AE464892C22C479E2FBD82.description: Use a right angle as a benchmark to identify and sketch acute and obtuse angles.

BC467BBDD68D4BE3B3928F499C10831C.description: Partition two-dimensional shapes into 2, 3, 4, 6, or 8 parts with equal areas and express the area of each part using the same unit fraction. Recognize that equal parts of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

CE0E8AFA1582479BBE0BCDE669C3E0F4.description: Understand that shapes in different categories (e.g., rhombus, rectangle, square, and other 4-sided shapes) may share attributes (e.g., 4-sided figures) and the shared attributes can define a larger category (e.g., quadrilateral). Recognize rhombuses, rectangles, and squares as examples of quadrilaterals, and draw examples of quadrilaterals that do not belong to any of these subcategories.

9F0728FD28EB4C9A92F1FB7A6FA01B01.description: Identify a rule for an arithmetic pattern (e.g., patterns in the addition table or multiplication table).

B610C7C9916C4A36A94171EF736B6B80.description: Solve two-step real-world problems using addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of whole numbers and having whole number answers. Represent these problems using equations with a letter for the unknown quantity.

D2DA6A1E49BA415CBDF7D9FBCD60C98E.description: Demonstrate fluency with basic multiplication and related division facts of products and dividends through 100.

BE9473CF479243FCA3808EF98A32341A.description: Understand division as a missing factor problem.

C0A3DF3067FB4DC5AE35CA8EA19CB924.description: Apply properties of operations (i.e., Commutative Property of Multiplication, Associative Property of Multiplication, Distributive Property) as strategies to multiply and divide and explain the reasoning.

CDDC9E1DA61C48F69A9C1C3F0E9CBD6A.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers when the unknown is a missing factor, product, dividend, divisor, or quotient.

65011B0BC5F34BD897F84B289EEAE6D3.description: Solve real-world problems involving equal groups, area/array, and number line models using basic multiplication and related division facts. Represent the problem situation using an equation with a symbol for the unknown.

DED75CDCBEAB41B3888917A8790CA5F6.description: Use concrete objects, drawings and symbols to represent division without remainders and explain the relationship among the whole number quotient (i.e., 0 – 10), divisor (i.e., 0 – 10), and dividend.

C27926D175D04C4A83CB2B06C1BAE629.description: Use concrete objects, drawings and symbols to represent multiplication facts of two single-digit whole numbers and explain the relationship between the factors (i.e., 0 – 10) and the product.

D3C0C002ACC345AB9FC05E3CBC2A19BD.description: Compare and order numbers through 999,999 and represent the comparison using the symbols >, =, or <.

82DEEF7D7EED43C79FD805D381BA0ABC.description: Read and write numbers through 999,999 in standard form and equations in expanded form.

C8C29C7FD9CE4224979EC3E14BF81EBD.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10 – 90, using knowledge of place value and properties of operations.

4BCD5F8FDD7249A090F24554A617168F.description: Add and subtract whole numbers fluently to 1,000 using knowledge of place value and properties of operations.

2088CB7A58994F239C631C5E18817443.description: Use place value understanding to round whole numbers to the nearest 10 or 100.

2977A9B288214CD4B9B8264B25CAD22F.description: Look for structures to interpret meaning and develop solution strategies.

BEE6ACD8EF144F4EBD07E4484D1A622C.description: Recognize mathematical repetition in order to make generalizations.

3727713D74994E43BEEE8FFB1CFF5434.description: Recognize complex mathematical objects as being composed of more than one simple object.

60C5BEC5FB734F8B9B639BD2F8879B79.description: Identify and utilize structure and patterns.

65F55BD4ECEE4A53B62D459BA96C16D9.description: Use appropriate units, scales, and labels.

D40A84EDDF334A6694C595121CC37445.description: Use appropriate and precise mathematical language.

6CFE68822EA84D8ABC92C15C7ABFF17C.description: Represent numbers in an appropriate form according to the context of the situation.

FF966001A1984AECA512685451774CEC.description: Express numerical answers with the degree of precision appropriate for the context of a situation.

260016B6D8AB4EE789AFB82C19DE5280.description: Communicate mathematically and approach mathematical situations with precision.

18F9F1E8457140B7A144A0D1F3EED4A4.description: Use technological tools and other external mathematical resources to explore and deepen understanding of concepts.

A54D79110508436185C7C9492DC462D3.description: Select and use appropriate tools when solving a mathematical problem.

82F6EED11F3C4E2FAFE51C612B53F31E.description: Use a variety of mathematical tools effectively and strategically.

5904D271CA8E456BA6F83EB242DC4826.description: Evaluate the reasonableness of a model and refine if necessary.

119F4C0C15D1488D83725FA9F9AA3D3C.description: Make assumptions and estimates to simplify complicated situations.

B992147F6C7E4B53A11194B54101DF28.description: Interpret mathematical models in the context of the situation.

0BA2A725ECB644C690FCB7940D2075DC.description: Identify relevant quantities and develop a model to describe their relationships.

08F482E798C5427DAE63567E5EE67B70.description: Connect mathematical ideas and real-world situations through modeling.

D758108E985E4F82B1D68EF8363DFBDA.description: Reflect on and provide thoughtful responses to the reasoning of others.

BAC0A9B57A1A4762B4AFAC05881F3D55.description: Make conjectures and explore their validity.

4D55021A6DDD4FB4AD924A9ADC13F020.description: Compare and discuss the validity of various reasoning strategies.

4043169A8A17490FB41449A108DA477C.description: Construct and justify a solution to a problem.

E0088E3763B14FB39CEECF1E9524AF39.description: Use critical thinking skills to justify mathematical reasoning and critique the reasoning of others.

6DE275221D364A149BAE5B2AB1FF75F0.description: Connect the meaning of mathematical operations to the context of a given situation.

1835F2B128CB4D769800107AD665C210.description: Translate among multiple mathematical representations and compare the meanings each representation conveys about the situation.

708C06F9BA7C4130921CEEB73613149C.description: Describe a given situation using multiple mathematical representations.

C7B65C2659064E83B05F62E7373C050B.description: Make sense of quantities and their relationships in mathematical and real-world situations.

86B79D022C604919B8733EF518D171FE.description: Evaluate the success of an approach to solve a problem and refine it if necessary.

7DB477FB0D8A4F8D83B5850DAD44C6DA.description: Analyze what is given, what is not given, what is being asked, and what strategies are needed, and make an initial attempt to solve a problem.

B91BD90D5D664E6981C11A96ED776DCC.description: Recognize there may be multiple entry points to a problem and more than one path to a solution.

5566540CABA545FE8A4C81E057A1EFA9.description: Relate a problem to prior knowledge.

55397AC089FC4543B459BD1C40C15B07.description: Make sense of problems and persevere in solving them.

document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards and Performance Indicators for Science

3E2F62E6625C45A1912A2093F3C524E2.description: Conduct structured investigations to answer questions about which materials have the properties that are best suited to solve a problem or need.

2B121317B12F40E1ABB89CFA04C54416.description: Develop and use models to describe and compare the properties of different materials (including wood, plastic, metal, cloth, and paper) and classify materials by their observable properties, by their uses, and by whether they are natural or human-made.

0CA6631083EE45EF90D574D4402D6383.description: Analyze and interpret data to compare the qualitative properties of objects (such as size, shape, color, texture, weight, flexibility, attraction to magnets, or ability to sink or float) and classify objects based on similar properties.

B2C5511999344C4AA514469598121091.description: Objects can be described and classified by their observable properties, by their uses, and by whether they occur naturally or are manufactured (human-made). Different properties of objects are suited for different purposes.

9D218266139D48A6AD2E65992F80166B.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the observable properties of matter.

268D30E577D349DE8C1F82B24E4513DC.description: Physical Science: Exploring Properties of Objects and Materials

3BAC430B2AF8442A921067D4EE125874.description: Define problems caused by the effects of weather on human activities and design solutions or devices to solve the problem.

6FDD192991154BCBA758E838B68F28B5.description: Obtain and communicate information to support claims about how changes in seasons affect plants and animals.

2755C64F30914FCBA0CAA8B73166BA06.description: Develop and use models to predict seasonal weather patterns and changes.

50162E34BFD54CF4B8AECF46B2FA6CAD.description: Analyze and interpret local weather condition data (including precipitation, wind, temperature, and cloud cover) to describe weather patterns that occur from day to day, using simple graphs and pictorial weather symbols.

2829B0BDC7CD4CA986BA96FFE6803423.description: Weather is a combination of sunlight, wind, snow or rain, and temperature in a particular region at a particular time. Scientists measure weather conditions to describe and record the weather and to notice patterns over time. Plants and animals (including humans) respond to different weather conditions in different ways.

57AE5C00223B41EBA7018A92457ABCA5.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of daily and seasonal weather patterns.

B8325D9A99A74BEF8A3160507ED68FB7.description: Obtain and communicate information about the needs of organisms to explain why they live in particular areas.

E509632197BD4201AAC492D4063B628B.description: Construct explanations from observations of what animals need to survive and grow (including air, water, nutrients, and shelter).

4CAE89A6B4DB4E0D9193DE7C8AFB23B5.description: Analyze and interpret data to describe how humans use their senses to learn about the world around them.

D4B0741248C345F4911E36A90B109C06.description: Develop and use models to exemplify how animals use their body parts to (1) obtain food and other resources, (2) protect themselves, and (3) move from place to place.

040A67708FEC4F49A2D52E136130692E.description: Conduct structured investigations to determine what plants need to live and grow (including water and light).

496D5C6550D140008C6ACE351A9E4A55.description: Obtain information to answer questions about different organisms found in the environment (such as plants, animals, or fungi).

15E6D1D55C51471D9DB5307179C08C41.description: The environment consists of many types of organisms including plants, animals, and fungi. Organisms depend on the land, water, and air to live and grow. Plants need water and light to make their own food. Fungi and animals cannot make their own food and get energy from other sources. Animals (including humans) use different body parts to obtain food and other resources needed to grow and survive. Organisms live in areas where their needs for air, water, nutrients, and shelter are met.

37AB18BD03B943DBAAEDA6193CA83950.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of organisms found in the environment and how these organisms depend on the environment to meet those needs.

982BD96DF3244E1A9A93674F4786DD82.description: Life Science: Exploring Organisms and the Environment

BACC04A0C25F407DAF2FF2CD3474CD14.description: Construct devices or design solutions to solve specific problems or needs: (1) ask questions to identify problems or needs, (2) ask questions about the criteria and constraints of the devices or solutions, (3) generate and communicate ideas for possible devices or solutions, (4) build and test devices or solutions, (5) determine if the devices or solutions solved the problem, and (6) communicate the results.

359CE844E9A540948012313849C53390.description: Technology is any modification to the natural world created to fulfill the wants and needs of humans. The engineering design process involves a series of iterative steps used to solve a problem and often leads to the development of a new or improved technology.

AF0338326AB04DD9AF47F5F1C00CE090.description: Obtain and evaluate informational texts, observations, data collected, or discussions to (1) generate and answer questions about the natural world, (2) understand phenomena, (3) develop models, or (4) support explanations. Communicate observations and explanations using oral and written language.

684D6EA962C84E72B7F751332D5615ED.description: Construct scientific arguments to support explanations using evidence from observations or data collected.

9265BABD649D4B86835E3A6D7C14FA69.description: Construct explanations of phenomena using (1) student-generated observations and measurements, (2) results of investigations, or (3) data communicated in graphs, tables, or diagrams.

E380B08E948941D8907A6B54FAE5C36E.description: Use mathematical thinking to (1) recognize and express quantitative observations, (2) collect and analyze data, or (3) understand patterns and relationships.

BE8532F5EB1C45EA8CAF6F7718B18338.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations, measurements, or investigations to understand patterns and meanings.

A2B42CD25EEE4AE7A598DDE1FC52EB4C.description: With teacher guidance, conduct structured investigations to answer scientific questions, test predictions and develop explanations: (1) predict possible outcomes, (2) identify materials and follow procedures, (3) use appropriate tools or instruments to make qualitative observations and take nonstandard measurements, and (4) record and represent data in an appropriate form. Use appropriate safety procedures.

E966934F6B8A4845A1F1BEA6100E7C77.description: Develop and use models to (1) understand or represent phenomena, processes, and relationships, (2) test devices or solutions, or (3) communicate ideas to others.

C30F618825B241F1AABDE5EDBB793117.description: Ask and answer questions about the natural world using explorations, observations, or structured investigations.

392BC6A7834D40B5B2694EF12D77636B.description: The practices of science and engineering support the development of science concepts, develop the habits of mind that are necessary for scientific thinking, and allow students to engage in science in ways that are similar to those used by scientists and engineers.

B753D2926FFF4900B5928B8F5E7924DC.description: The student will use the science and engineering practices, including the processes and skills of scientific inquiry, to develop understandings of science content.

document.title: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

5DF42030DFE70131979368A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately general academic and domain-specific words and phrases, sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

5DF3C670DFE70131979268A86D17958E.description: Analyze nuances in the meaning of words with similar denotations.

5DF35810DFE70131979168A86D17958E.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., euphemism, oxymoron) in context and analyze their role in the text.

5DF2F720DFE70131979068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

5DF2A080DFE70131978F68A86D17958E.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

5DF24AD0DFE70131978E68A86D17958E.description: Consult general and specialized reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning, its part of speech, or its etymology.

5DF1F3F0DFE70131978D68A86D17958E.description: Identify and correctly use patterns of word changes that indicate different meanings or parts of speech (e.g., analyze, analysis, analytical; advocate, advocacy).

5DF19CC0DFE70131978C68A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence, paragraph, or text; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

5DF13E50DFE70131978B68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grades 9—10 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

5DF099E0DFE70131978968A86D17958E.description: Write and edit work so that it conforms to the guidelines in a style manual (e.g., MLA Handbook, Turabian's Manual for Writers) appropriate for the discipline and writing type.

5DF039E0DFE70131978868A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

5DEF1350DFE70131978568A86D17958E.description: Use a colon to introduce a list or quotation.

5DEEC010DFE70131978468A86D17958E.description: Use a semicolon (and perhaps a conjunctive adverb) to link two or more closely related independent clauses.

5DEE69E0DFE70131978368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

5DEE05E0DFE70131978268A86D17958E.description: Use various types of phrases (noun, verb, adjectival, adverbial, participial, prepositional, absolute) and clauses (independent, dependent; noun, relative, adverbial) to convey specific meanings and add variety and interest to writing or presentations.

5DED5500DFE70131978068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

5DEC5490DFE70131977D68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

5DEBF470DFE70131977C68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately a range of general academic and domain-specific words and phrases sufficient for reading, writing, speaking, and listening at the college and career readiness level; demonstrate independence in gathering vocabulary knowledge when encountering an unknown term important to comprehension or expression.

5DEB9510DFE70131977B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

5DEB1540DFE70131977A68A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases by using context clues, analyzing meaningful word parts, and consulting general and specialized reference materials, as appropriate.

5DEA4480DFE70131977868A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of language to understand how language functions in different contexts, to make effective choices for meaning or style, and to comprehend more fully when reading or listening.

5DE9A340DFE70131977668A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

5DE95060DFE70131977568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English grammar and usage when writing or speaking.

5DE89AE0DFE70131977368A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Language

5DE83970DFE70131977268A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

5DE7D5F0DFE70131977168A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media (e.g., textual, graphical, audio, visual, and interactive elements) in presentations to enhance understanding of findings, reasoning, and evidence and to add interest.

5DE784B0DFE70131977068A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence clearly, concisely, and logically such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, substance, and style are appropriate to purpose, audience, and task.

5DE6D6B0DFE70131976E68A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric, identifying any fallacious reasoning or exaggerated or distorted evidence.

5DE688B0DFE70131976D68A86D17958E.description: Integrate multiple sources of information presented in diverse media or formats (e.g., visually, quantitatively, orally) evaluating the credibility and accuracy of each source.

5DE639C0DFE70131976C68A86D17958E.description: Respond thoughtfully to diverse perspectives, summarize points of agreement and disagreement, and, when warranted, qualify or justify their own views and understanding and make new connections in light of the evidence and reasoning presented.

5DE5EB60DFE70131976B68A86D17958E.description: Propel conversations by posing and responding to questions that relate the current discussion to broader themes or larger ideas; actively incorporate others into the discussion; and clarify, verify, or challenge ideas and conclusions.

5DE59C00DFE70131976A68A86D17958E.description: Work with peers to set rules for collegial discussions and decision-making (e.g., informal consensus, taking votes on key issues, presentation of alternate views), clear goals and deadlines, and individual roles as needed.

5DE54920DFE70131976968A86D17958E.description: Come to discussions prepared, having read and researched material under study; explicitly draw on that preparation by referring to evidence from texts and other research on the topic or issue to stimulate a thoughtful, well-reasoned exchange of ideas.

5DE4EC50DFE70131976868A86D17958E.description: Initiate and participate effectively in a range of collaborative discussions (one-on-one, in groups, and teacher-led) with diverse partners on grades 9—10 topics, texts, and issues, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

5DE3FF50DFE70131976568A86D17958E.description: Adapt speech to a variety of contexts and communicative tasks, demonstrating command of formal English when indicated or appropriate.

5DE3AAA0DFE70131976468A86D17958E.description: Make strategic use of digital media and visual displays of data to express information and enhance understanding of presentations.

5DE34CE0DFE70131976368A86D17958E.description: Present information, findings, and supporting evidence such that listeners can follow the line of reasoning and the organization, development, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

5DE26F80DFE70131976168A86D17958E.description: Evaluate a speaker's point of view, reasoning, and use of evidence and rhetoric.

5DE1F0F0DFE70131976068A86D17958E.description: Integrate and evaluate information presented in diverse media and formats, including visually, quantitatively, and orally.

5DE1A140DFE70131975F68A86D17958E.description: Prepare for and participate effectively in a range of conversations and collaborations with diverse partners, building on others' ideas and expressing their own clearly and persuasively.

5DE0EC90DFE70131975D68A86D17958E.description: College and Career Readiness Anchor Standards for Speaking and Listening

5DE09E80DFE70131975C68A86D17958E.description: Write routinely over extended time frames (time for reflection and revision) and shorter time frames (a single sitting or a day or two) for a range of discipline-specific tasks, purposes, and audiences.

5DDFFF20DFE70131975A68A86D17958E.description: Draw evidence from informational texts to support analysis, reflection, and research.

5DDFADB0DFE70131975968A86D17958E.description: Gather relevant information from multiple authoritative print and digital sources, using advanced searches effectively; assess the usefulness of each source in answering the research question; integrate information into the text selectively to maintain the flow of ideas, avoiding plagiarism and following a standard format for citation.

5DDF56C0DFE70131975868A86D17958E.description: Conduct short as well as more sustained research projects to answer a question (including a self-generated question) or solve a problem; narrow or broaden the inquiry when appropriate; synthesize multiple sources on the subject, demonstrating understanding of the subject under investigation.

5DDEEE80DFE70131975768A86D17958E.description: Research to Build and Present Knowledge

5DDE9870DFE70131975668A86D17958E.description: Use technology, including the Internet, to produce, publish, and update individual or shared writing products, taking advantage of technology's capacity to link to other information and to display information flexibly and dynamically.

5DDDD660DFE70131975468A86D17958E.description: Produce clear and coherent writing in which the development, organization, and style are appropriate to task, purpose, and audience.

5DDE3820DFE70131975568A86D17958E.description: Develop and strengthen writing as needed by planning, revising, editing, rewriting, or trying a new approach, focusing on addressing what is most significant for a specific purpose and audience.

5DDD1BB0DFE70131975268A86D17958E.description: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the information or explanation presented (e.g., articulating implications or the significance of the topic).

5DDCC4A0DFE70131975168A86D17958E.description: Establish and maintain a formal style and objective tone while attending to the norms and conventions of the discipline in which they are writing.

5DDC6E00DFE70131975068A86D17958E.description: Use precise language and domain-specific vocabulary to manage the complexity of the topic and convey a style appropriate to the discipline and context as well as to the expertise of likely readers.
