document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards and Performance Indicators for Science

78C26B0484924FC1A0B5A36775BB1AC6.description: Define problems caused by the introduction of a new species in an environment and design devices or solutions to minimize the impact(s) to the balance of an ecosystem.

598F25BFAE0943E7839B133412843862.description: Analyze and interpret data to predict how changes in the number of organisms of one species affects the balance of an ecosystem.

90D1F49E7BF94F9CAE9DFCC0ACD2D23E.description: Develop and use models (food webs and energy pyramids) to exemplify how the transfer of energy in an ecosystem supports the concept that energy is conserved.

D6BAF92E0D944583AEC2DA4A0B8D5F94.description: Develop and use models to explain how organisms interact in a competitive or mutually beneficial relationship for food, shelter, or space (including competition, mutualism, commensalism, parasitism, and predator-prey relationships).

45BCAE38EEF740F29E346B398F5C5B30.description: Organisms in all ecosystems interact with and depend upon each other. Organisms with similar needs compete for limited resources. Food webs and energy pyramids are models that demonstrate how energy is transferred within an ecosystem.

74AED940410D4026B411AADF9899BBCC.description: Analyze and interpret data to predict changes in the number of organisms within a population when certain changes occur to the physical environment (such as changes due to natural hazards or limiting factors).

7A2BDCFB074B41259C7E537DF819911C.description: Construct explanations of how soil quality (including composition, texture, particle size, permeability, and pH) affects the characteristics of an ecosystem using evidence from soil profiles.

D2A0B0EFD9AB41E5ADB27391B53A15E0.description: Develop and use models to describe the characteristics of the levels of organization within ecosystems (including species, populations, communities, ecosystems, and biomes).

C60590D2B1A34E95A1D7855A7900B9D7.description: In all ecosystems, organisms and populations of organisms depend on their environmental interactions with other living things (biotic factors) and with physical (abiotic) factors (such as light, temperature, water, or soil quality). Disruptions to any component of an ecosystem can lead to shifts in its diversity and abundance of populations.

56D6BDDEBAE3411BA63DDB7B1B826ACB.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of how organisms interact with and respond to the biotic and abiotic components of their environments.

296BC2DC13A5478F813482AE1E736DD4.description: Ecology: Interactions of Living Systems and the Environment

7CF5315F884A49E281253AD46F3EB315.description: Develop and use models to explain how chemical reactions are supported by the law of conservation of matter.

9E55E6E969DD4BB19945D9F2BD3095FB.description: Plan and conduct controlled scientific investigations to answer questions about how physical and chemical changes affect the properties of different substances.

00D2383D18E247D0B3DBC462A9344839.description: Analyze and interpret data to compare the physical properties, chemical properties (neutralization to form a salt, reaction with metals), and pH of various solutions and classify solutions as acids or bases.

58B9A3A742AF4025B0DAD59C035589D5.description: Use mathematical and computational thinking to describe the relationship between the mass, volume, and density of a given substance.

28200D70157F4F4198C24B350D75DE1B.description: Analyze and interpret data to describe substances using physical properties (including state, boiling/melting point, density, conductivity, color, hardness, and magnetic properties) and chemical properties (the ability to burn or rust).

05A60FBD9356417C8D5398962D0E35CF.description: Substances (such as metals or acids) are identified according to their physical or chemical properties. Changes to substances can either be physical or chemical. Many substances react chemically with other substances to form new substances with different properties. According to the law of conservation of matter, total mass does not change in a chemical reaction.

9AA62CA910384CACA5E11BA9E27E137B.description: Construct explanations for how compounds are classified as ionic (metal bonded to nonmetal) or covalent (nonmetals bonded together) using chemical formulas.

A3DF7ECD1B9347B69E2023E7E34146B9.description: Analyze and interpret data to describe and classify matter as pure substances (elements or compounds) or mixtures (heterogeneous or homogeneous) based on composition.

1F385DD5427C497CA79298E903BA36A2.description: Obtain and use information about elements (including chemical symbol, atomic number, atomic mass, and group or family) to describe the organization of the periodic table.

9EFC6AE0EFEB45C5A2A1CF6B5E8AFA5F.description: Develop and use simple atomic models to illustrate the components of elements (including the relative position and charge of protons, neutrons, and electrons).

F5A740845F7E4DE78476B7DC61533C80.description: All substances are composed of one or more elements. Elements are pure substances which contain only one kind of atom. The periodic table organizes these elements based on similar properties. Compounds are substances composed of two or more elements. Chemical formulas can be used to describe compounds.

73198805CDE6499580700B0A9F7C9FD3.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the structure and properties of matter and that matter is conserved as it undergoes changes.

CF1FE960BFB5450A928B3A465876D648.description: Physical Science: Classification and Conservation of Matter

EA2D26DBF0554FBEA60A1D952CCE7A08.description: Construct scientific arguments using evidence to support claims concerning the advantages and disadvantages of the use of technology (such as selective breeding, genetic engineering, or biomedical research) in influencing the transfer of genetic information.

45847492A7254CA4917296754132616C.description: Construct scientific arguments using evidence to support claims for how changes in genes (mutations) may have beneficial, harmful, or neutral effects on organisms.

48B813D4E3BD45B7A71987CB06F0DFF7.description: Use mathematical and computational thinking to predict the probability of phenotypes and genotypes based on patterns of inheritance.

ABD97687D3FE4C8FB65F3BAA9E832C69.description: Develop and use models (Punnett squares) to describe and predict patterns of the inheritance of single genetic traits from parent to offspring (including dominant and recessive traits, incomplete dominance, and codominance).

111F1E9DB9CC4E99A6F980A634B86B2D.description: Construct explanations for how genetic information is transferred from parent to offspring in organisms that reproduce sexually.

4081BEDFAF6945EA87E6FC91A7BD361E.description: Obtain and communicate information about the relationship between genes and chromosomes to construct explanations of their relationship to inherited characteristics.

8CE4F624B0F4449993F76DB792C9F866.description: Inheritance is the key process causing similarities between parental organisms and their offspring. Organisms that reproduce sexually transfer genetic information (DNA) to their offspring. This transfer of genetic information through inheritance leads to greater similarity among individuals within a population than between populations. Technology allows humans to influence the transfer of genetic information.

CC8FAE0DF7714F0CBCAF6F8178F42B58.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of how genetic information is transferred from parent to offspring and how environmental factors and the use of technologies influence the transfer of genetic information.

52E1EC9E055141C0AA70CC2BB8143424.description: Life Science: Heredity - Inheritance and Variation of Traits

4A5EA1D151A84F12988925B17DB0BCB6.description: Construct explanations for how systems in the human body (including circulatory, respiratory, digestive, excretory, nervous, and musculoskeletal systems) work together to support the essential life functions of the body.

BB535D10C6474D4395465008D5DC4DCA.description: Develop and use models to explain how the structural organizations within multicellular organisms function to serve the needs of the organism.

A33BD1AB8227491C84CFA453BA402EEA.description: Multicellular organisms (including humans) are complex systems with specialized cells that perform specific functions. Organs and organ systems are composed of cells that function to serve the needs of cells which in turn serve the needs of the organism.

D58981DBE5E7498F955DDF2EC5FDC02A.description: Construct scientific arguments to support claims that bacteria are both helpful and harmful to other organisms and the environment.

0DB7013803F8480A937FD43E6FCAC8BD.description: Develop and use models to explain how the relevant structures within cells (including cytoplasm, cell membrane, cell wall, nucleus, mitochondria, chloroplasts, lysosomes, and vacuoles) function to support the life of plant, animal, and bacterial cells.

90B0246C6C3A407A8512D45C4E20D0DF.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations to describe different types of cells and classify cells as plant, animal, protist, or bacteria.

1A70C9F57D984648988D70FC17E8079B.description: Obtain and communicate information to support claims that (1) organisms are made of one or more cells, (2) cells are the basic unit of structure and function of organisms, and (3) cells come only from existing cells.

4F9E0D22B1D64D02A6ECE8FFB27EEBA5.description: Cells are the most basic unit of any living organism. All organisms are composed of one (unicellular) or many cells (multicellular) and require food and water, a way to dispose of waste, and an environment in which they can live in order to survive. Through the use of technology, scientists have discovered special structures within individual cells that have specific functions that allow the cell to grow, survive, and reproduce. Bacteria are one-celled organisms found almost everywhere and can be both helpful and harmful. They can be simply classified by their size, shape and whether or not they can move.

5A6485B929074600BC5C6B232B708B19.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of how the levels of organization within organisms support the essential functions of life.

54C7F4D5A93143CDA76A02C27723809D.description: Life Science: Organization in Living Systems

23B826BB97DA486EB90AFF9919F4479C.description: Construct devices or design solutions using scientific knowledge to solve specific problems or needs: (1) ask questions to identify problems or needs, (2) ask questions about the criteria and constraints of the device or solutions, (3) generate and communicate ideas for possible devices or solutions, (4) build and test devices or solutions, (5) determine if the devices or solutions solved the problem and refine the design if needed, and (6) communicate the results.

9BF37EF8CD6E4521A254B7FDD4CF2F89.description: Technology is any modification to the natural world created to fulfill the wants and needs of humans. The engineering design process involves a series of iterative steps used to solve a problem and often leads to the development of a new or improved technology.

1C3BFD8C9CC2466FB53BE1030197AB5A.description: Obtain and evaluate scientific information to (1) answer questions, (2) explain or describe phenomena, (3) develop models, (4) evaluate hypotheses, explanations, claims, or designs or (5) identify and/or fill gaps in knowledge. Communicate using the conventions and expectations of scientific writing or oral presentations by (1) evaluating grade-appropriate primary or secondary scientific literature, or (2) reporting the results of student experimental investigations.

36AF4DC3484743CE9610D856B2F3746C.description: Construct and analyze scientific arguments to support claims, explanations, or designs using evidence from observations, data, or informational texts.

DC77A3EFE06E4BE5821E4F1B11C65D01.description: Construct explanations of phenomena using (1) primary or secondary scientific evidence and models, (2) conclusions from scientific investigations, (3) predictions based on observations and measurements, or (4) data communicated in graphs, tables, or diagrams.

64DD40927CA54C66B13990496E61B8EC.description: Use mathematical and computational thinking to (1) use and manipulate appropriate metric units, (2) collect and analyze data, (3) express relationships between variables for models and investigations, or (4) use grade-level appropriate statistics to analyze data.

E2355347DD9546EF90FDB7904006D6F3.description: Analyze and interpret data from informational texts, observations, measurements, or investigations using a range of methods (such as tabulation, graphing, or statistical analysis) to (1) reveal patterns and construct meaning or (2) support hypotheses, explanations, claims, or designs.

6CE7452224C14133832D9E876ABD26FF.description: Plan and conduct controlled scientific investigation to answer questions, test hypotheses, and develop explanations: (1) formulate scientific questions and testable hypotheses, (2) identify materials, procedures, and variables, (3) select and use appropriate tools or instruments to collect qualitative and quantitative data, and (4) record and represent data in an appropriate form. Use appropriate safety procedures.

71860F47DC6940D9B6DE9959D9846E1F.description: Develop, use, and refine models to (1) understand or represent phenomena, processes, and relationships, (2) test devices or solutions, or (3) communicate ideas to others.

A5E6E2B2F6384006831F5743CC353EF0.description: Ask questions to (1) generate hypotheses for scientific investigations, (2) refine models, explanations, or designs, or (3) extend the results of investigations or challenge claims.

38CB63BD67B544B8A8A36F3AABBCBFF9.description: The practices of science and engineering support the development of science concepts, develop the habits of mind that are necessary for scientific thinking, and allow students to engage in science in ways that are similar to those used by scientists and engineers.

2DDCF817AE76456596B9EB6706E14070.description: The student will use the science and engineering practices, including the processes and skills of scientific inquiry, to develop understandings of science content.

document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards and Performance Indicators for Science

88210E3C9F67486589BDBE1474D7F69B.description: Develop and use models to describe what happens when light shines on mirrors based on observations and data collected.

8EC3261941524A539D21F71481F8B966.description: Conduct structured investigations to answer questions about how shadows change when the position of the light source changes.

84C476135D21489E80B9BDE8640E7B57.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations to compare how light behaves when it shines on different materials.

A02784E38D7F467AB8B4855E38D463A4.description: Obtain and communicate information to describe how light is required to make objects visible.

A43141F44E5C4D1FBE30324FD08006AE.description: Objects can only be seen when light shines on them. Some materials allow light to pass through them; others allow only some light to pass through; and some do not allow any light to pass through and will create a shadow of the object. Technology such as mirrors can change the direction of a beam of light.

548B91E9670A47EDA7368D6550F3BAE1.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the properties of light and how shadows are formed.

E6EBE1FB06D441A9871DD2998293A7F7.description: Physical Science: Exploring Light and Shadows

5039323B119A40FE8569A3367F8054BA.description: Obtain and communicate information to explain ways natural resources can be conserved (such as reducing trash through reuse, recycling, or replanting trees).

51717EB641DD44F588729082AE4D39F8.description: Obtain and communicate information to summarize how natural resources are used in different ways (such as soil and water to grow plants; rocks to make roads, walls, or buildings; or sand to make glass).

97CB750561D2492D9A8B493EA3D7C736.description: Natural resources are things that people use that come from Earth (such as land, water, air, and trees). Natural resources can be conserved.

F5D8809A0C1C4CC4882A76F124BF1653.description: Conduct structured investigations to answer questions about how the movement of water can change the shape of the land.

DC0F6C07B8BA4C17A45E19E33385968A.description: Develop and use models (such as drawings or maps) to describe patterns in the distribution of land and water on Earth and classify bodies of water (including oceans, rivers and streams, lakes, and ponds).

7DFFC7DADD634D7D9F782958A54F9A02.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations and measurements to compare the properties of Earth materials (including rocks, soils, sand, and water).

AA48EF24212A4CAC824CE1386E4352EB.description: Earth is made of different materials, including rocks, sand, soil, and water. An Earth material is a resource that comes from Earth. Earth materials can be classified by their observable properties.

0D486B807B8841CA8CEAD947CE89A4A8.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the properties and uses of Earth's natural resources.

F52106F179904A2D89427E71C2DF8505.description: Define problems related to the warming effect of sunlight and design possible solutions to reduce its impact on a particular area.

FAC52E669D0045188B86FD3B1B4AE981.description: Conduct structured investigations to answer questions about the effect of sunlight on Earth's surface.

A9C46A1974A048BDA9AB9F764BA3099E.description: Obtain and communicate information to describe how technology has enabled the study of the Sun, the Moon, planets, and stars.

456FE9D21B03400C95B176BB46E2D53A.description: Use data from personal observations to describe, predict, and develop models to exemplify how the appearance of the moon changes over time in a predictable pattern.

BDD0BA6F65CF4DABAFB9D50BE54F731B.description: Use, analyze, and interpret data from observations to describe and predict seasonal patterns of sunrise and sunset.

F1E008E2AC194170AE59CC9AABB4948E.description: Objects in the sky move in predictable patterns. Some objects are better seen in the day sky and some are better seen in the night sky. The Sun is a star that provides heat and light energy for Earth.

7F74CF3D6CCC4CEB9170C60FC9CA500D.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the patterns of the Sun and the Moon and the Sun's effect on Earth.

D64A585D59B34E74BC0302D6A8DC21FD.description: Earth Science: Exploring the Sun and Moon

38EAE397B920455DA6B10547C36BEA55.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations to describe how changes in the environment cause plants to respond in different ways (such as turning leaves toward the Sun, leaves changing color, leaves wilting, or trees shedding leaves).

A1AE4CD4FE5A49AE9AC56AF5A2042FDF.description: Develop and use models to compare how the different characteristics of plants help them survive in distinct environments (including deserts, forests, and grasslands).

C928A446DC2445FE876006CC1556A30E.description: Conduct structured investigations to answer questions about what plants need to live and grow (including air, water, sunlight, minerals, and space).

84038EA6BA40429CAC35E5B1459CEBD0.description: Plants have basic needs that provide energy in order to grow and be healthy. Each plant has a specific environment where it can thrive. There are distinct environments in the world that support different types of plants. These environments can change slowly or quickly. Plants respond to these changes in different ways.

526DC97749D945888C049518BD5E9ABC.description: Construct explanations of the stages of development of a flowering plant as it grow from a seed using observations and measurements.

1A8598C629A44CA8880378C6F5903B2D.description: Obtain and communicate information to construct explanations for how different plant structures (including roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, and seeds) help plants survive, grow, and produce more plants.

D9AF4C0FCFCE4603A0B6D1AEDBFC2B79.description: Plants have specific structures that help them survive, grow, and produce more plants. Plants have predictable characteristics at different stages of development.

4F4A830CBD644B4D8503392B8B4039D8.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of how the structures of plants help them survive and grow in their environments.

E8C4F019946148A59A113D54D86B0718.description: Life Science: Plants and their Environments

8BFFF590912B4695B8A75CC0602F39BE.description: Construct devices or design solutions to solve specific problems or needs: (1) ask questions to identify problems or needs, (2) ask questions about the criteria and constraints of the devices or solutions, (3) generate and communicate ideas for possible devices or solutions, (4) build and test devices or solutions, (5) determine if the devices or solutions solved the problem, and (6) communicate the results.

079FC6D35BC64FA28036CE18E30DF23A.description: Technology is any modification to the natural world created to fulfill the wants and needs of humans. The engineering design process involves a series of iterative steps used to solve a problem and often leads to the development of a new or improved technology.

D48944207E3B44428C07B740E5EC3711.description: Obtain and evaluate informational texts, observations, data collected, or discussions to (1) generate and answer questions about the natural world, (2) understand phenomena, (3) develop models, or (4) support explanations. Communicate observations and explanations clearly through oral and written language.

73EA2378C3D544CF98EBB7B05255EEDA.description: Construct scientific arguments to support claims or explanations using evidence from observations or data collected.

C4905D5180DC4163B5C3AE99853F21DB.description: Construct explanations of phenomena using (1) student-generated observations and measurements, (2) results of scientific investigations, or (3) data communicated in graphs, tables, or diagrams.

37A6D49D65E04905B26E4EF01AF9EADF.description: Use mathematical and computational thinking to (1) recognize and express quantitative observations, (2) collect and analyze data, or (3) understand patterns and relationships.

93A1CB6114264E77971B577B05353091.description: Analyze and interpret data from observations, measurements, or investigations to understand patterns and meanings.

33357835BC0244E9870A20166F10F15D.description: With teacher guidance, conduct structured investigations to answer scientific questions, test predictions and develop explanations: (1) predict possible outcomes, (2) identify materials and follow procedures, (3) use appropriate tools or instruments to collect qualitative and quantitative data, and (4) record and represent data in an appropriate form. Use appropriate safety procedures.

C3DF05CB9694400E96312F8894ED148D.description: Develop and use models to (1) understand or represent phenomena, processes, and relationships, (2) test devices or solutions, or (3) communicate ideas to others.

04236D314F444C71BC082225F7478A12.description: Ask and answer questions about the natural world using explorations, observations, or structured investigations.

7B5F8D0715174116A80C989FEBAF1D0C.description: The practices of science and engineering support the development of science concepts, develop the habits of mind that are necessary for scientific thinking, and allow students to engage in science in ways that are similar to those used by scientists and engineers.

8ED0DF51B4674EFFB611DBEBCFA82F87.description: The student will use the science and engineering practices, including the processes and skills of scientific inquiry, to develop understandings of science content.

document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards for English Language Arts

5EDE4FD0DFE70131994C68A86D17958E.description: Use Standard American English when appropriate in conversations and discussions.

5EDE0260DFE70131994B68A86D17958E.description: Use the Internet with the aid of a teacher.

5EDDC110DFE70131994A68A86D17958E.description: Create categories (for example, solids and liquids) to classify information.

5EDD7810DFE70131994968A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of print sources (for example, books, pictures, charts, graphs, diagrams, and picture dictionaries) and nonprint sources to access information.

5EDD2C00DFE70131994868A86D17958E.description: Generate how and why questions about a topic of interest.

5EDCDC00DFE70131994768A86D17958E.description: The student will access and use information from a variety of sources.

5EDC8D00DFE70131994668A86D17958E.description: Applying the Skills of Inquiry and Oral Communication

5EDBF290DFE70131994468A86D17958E.description: Create written pieces (for example, rhymes, poems, and songs) to entertain others.

5EDB8AF0DFE70131994368A86D17958E.description: Create written pieces that describe objects, people, places, or events and that use words that appeal to the senses.

5EDB3B60DFE70131994268A86D17958E.description: Create narratives (for example, stories and journal entries) that follow a logical sequence of events.

5EDAF8A0DFE70131994168A86D17958E.description: Create written communications (for example, directions and instructions) to inform a specific audience.

5EDAB080DFE70131994068A86D17958E.description: The student will write for a variety of purposes and audiences.

5EDA63B0DFE70131993F68A86D17958E.description: Producing Written Communications in a Variety of Forms

5EDA1E60DFE70131993E68A86D17958E.description: Use correct letter formation when using manuscript or cursive writing.

5ED9DBC0DFE70131993D68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate spacing between words when writing on a page.

5ED98820DFE70131993C68A86D17958E.description:
Edit for the correct use of written Standard American English, including
  • capitalization
    • proper nouns,
    • initials of a person's name,
    • courtesy titles (Mr., Ms.),
    • days of the week,
    • months of the year, and
    • titles of books, poems, and songs;
  • punctuation
    • apostrophes in contractions,
    • commas in a series,
    • commas in dates, and
    • quotation marks to show someone is speaking; and
  • spelling
    • words that do not fit regular spelling patterns (for example, was, were, says, said),
    • high-frequency words, and
    • basic short-vowel, long-vowel, r-controlled, and consonant-blend patterns.
(See Instructional Appendix: High-Frequency Words.)

5ED942E0DFE70131993B68A86D17958E.description: Revise the organization and development of content and the quality of voice in written works. (See Instructional Appendix: Composite Writing Matrix.)

5ED8FBC0DFE70131993A68A86D17958E.description:
Use grammatical conventions of Standard American English, including
  • personal pronouns
  • common and proper nouns,
  • singular and plural nouns,
  • proper adjectives, and
  • conjunctions (and, but, or).
(See Instructional Appendix: Composite Writing Matrix.)

5ED8AB10DFE70131993968A86D17958E.description: Create a paragraph that follows a logical sequence (including a beginning, middle, and end) and uses transitional words.

5ED85190DFE70131993868A86D17958E.description: Use complete sentences (including simple sentences with compound subjects and predicates) in writing.

5ED80180DFE70131993768A86D17958E.description: Generate ideas for writing using prewriting techniques (for example, creating lists, having discussions, and examining literary models).

5ED7A880DFE70131993668A86D17958E.description: The student will create written work that has a clear focus, sufficient detail, coherent organization, effective use of voice, and correct use of the conventions of written Standard American English.

5ED6C660DFE70131993368A86D17958E.description: Apply knowledge of alphabetizing a series of words to the second and third letters.

5ED68120DFE70131993268A86D17958E.description: Spell high-frequency words. (See Instructional Appendix: High-Frequency Words.)

5ED63640DFE70131993168A86D17958E.description: Spell basic short-vowel, long-vowel, r-controlled, and consonant-blend patterns correctly.

5ED5E390DFE70131993068A86D17958E.description: Spell frequently used irregular words correctly (for example, was, were, says, said, who, what, why).

5ED590B0DFE70131992F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze spelling patterns in context and parts of multisyllabic words (for example, onsets and rimes).

5ED53E40DFE70131992E68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of spelling patterns and high-frequency words to read fluently. (See Instructional Appendix: High-Frequency Words.)

5ED4AD90DFE70131992C68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate rate, word automaticity, phrasing, and expression to read fluently.

5ED42AE0DFE70131992A68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of individual words to determine the meaning of compound words.

5ED3E890DFE70131992968A86D17958E.description: Recognize synonyms, antonyms, and homonyms in context.

5ED34CC0DFE70131992768A86D17958E.description: Recognize high-frequency words in context. (See Instructional Appendix: High-Frequency Words.)

5ED2FA30DFE70131992668A86D17958E.description: Construct meaning through a knowledge of base words, prefixes (including -un, -re, -pre, -bi, -mis, -dis) and suffixes (including -er, -est, -ful) in context.

5ED28DC0DFE70131992568A86D17958E.description: Use context clues to determine the meaning of unfamiliar words.

5ED20470DFE70131992368A86D17958E.description: The student will use word analysis and vocabulary strategies to read fluently.

5ED1BD60DFE70131992268A86D17958E.description: Read independently for extended periods of time to gain information.

5ED16EA0DFE70131992168A86D17958E.description: Explain cause-and-effect relationships in informational texts.

5ED12C10DFE70131992068A86D17958E.description: Use functional text features (including tables of contents and glossaries) as sources of information.

5ED0E4E0DFE70131991F68A86D17958E.description: Use graphic features (for example, illustrations, graphs, charts, maps, and diagrams) as sources of information.

5ED092B0DFE70131991E68A86D17958E.description: Use headings, subheadings, and print styles (for example, italics, bold, larger type) to gain information.

5ECFF690DFE70131991D68A86D17958E.description: Create responses to informational texts through a variety of methods (for example, drawings, written works, and oral presentations).

5ECFA8D0DFE70131991C68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between facts and opinions in informational texts.

5ECF6910DFE70131991B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze informational texts to draw conclusions and make inferences during classroom discussions.

5ECF2A00DFE70131991A68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the central idea and supporting evidence in an informational text during classroom discussion.

5ECEEA80DFE70131991968A86D17958E.description: The student will read and comprehend a variety of informational texts in print and nonprint formats.

5ECE6800DFE70131991768A86D17958E.description: Read independently for extended periods of time for pleasure.

5ECE1EF0DFE70131991668A86D17958E.description: Explain cause-and-effect relationships in literary texts.

5ECDDD70DFE70131991568A86D17958E.description: Classify works of fiction (including fables, tall tales, and folktales) and works of nonfiction (including biographies) by characteristics.

5ECD9C10DFE70131991468A86D17958E.description: Create responses to literary texts through a variety of methods (for example, writing, creative dramatics, and the visual and performing arts).

5ECD5590DFE70131991368A86D17958E.description: Explain the effect of the author's craft (for example, word choice and the use of repetition) on the meaning of a given literary text.

5ECD07B0DFE70131991268A86D17958E.description: Analyze a narrative text to identify characters, setting, and plot.

5ECCA480DFE70131991168A86D17958E.description: Find examples of devices of figurative language (including simile) and sound devices (including onomatopoeia and alliteration).

5ECC59A0DFE70131991068A86D17958E.description: Analyze the text to determine the narrator.

5ECC17B0DFE70131990F68A86D17958E.description: Analyze a given literary text to make, revise, and confirm predictions.

5ECBD470DFE70131990E68A86D17958E.description: Analyze the details that support the expression of the main idea in a given literary text.

5ECB8F70DFE70131990D68A86D17958E.description: The student will read and comprehend a variety of literary texts in print and nonprint formats.

document.title: South Carolina Science Academic Standards

65527810DFE70131A33768A86D17958E.description: Compare physical changes (including changes in size, shape, and state) to chemical changes that are the result of chemical reactions (including changes in color or temperature and formation of a precipitate or gas).

65522890DFE70131A33668A86D17958E.description: Compare physical properties of matter (including melting or boiling point, density, and color) to the chemical property of reactivity with a certain substance (including the ability to burn or to rust).

6551DC90DFE70131A33568A86D17958E.description: Explain how a balanced chemical equation supports the law of conservation of matter.

65518D00DFE70131A33468A86D17958E.description: Identify the reactants and products in chemical equations.

65514930DFE70131A33368A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between acids and bases and use indicators (including litmus paper, pH paper, and phenolphthalein) to determine their relative pH.

655106E0DFE70131A33268A86D17958E.description: Translate chemical symbols and the chemical formulas of common substances to show the component parts of the substances (including NaCl [table salt], H<sub>2</sub>O [water], C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>12</sub>O<sub>6</sub> [simple sugar], O<sub>2</sub> [oxygen gas], CO<sub>2</sub> [carbon dioxide], and N<sub>2</sub> [nitrogen gas]).

6550B970DFE70131A33168A86D17958E.description: Use the periodic table to identify the basic organization of elements and groups of elements (including metals, nonmetals, and families).

65505FB0DFE70131A33068A86D17958E.description: Compare the physical properties of metals and nonmetals.

654FFE30DFE70131A32F68A86D17958E.description: Classify matter as element, compound, or mixture on the basis of its composition.

654FBA60DFE70131A32E68A86D17958E.description: Recognize that matter is composed of extremely small particles called atoms.

654F6FD0DFE70131A32D68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the classifications and properties of matter and the changes that matter undergoes. (Physical Science)

654ED470DFE70131A32B68A86D17958E.description: Classify resources as renewable or nonrenewable and explain the implications of their depletion and the importance of conservation.

654E96B0DFE70131A32A68A86D17958E.description: Summarize how the location and movement of water on Earth's surface through groundwater zones and surface-water drainage basins, called watersheds, are important to ecosystems and to human activities.

654E58D0DFE70131A32968A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of soil quality on the characteristics of an ecosystem.

654E1950DFE70131A32868A86D17958E.description: Explain the interaction among changes in the environment due to natural hazards (including landslides, wildfires, and floods), changes in populations, and limiting factors (including climate and the availability of food and water, space, and shelter).

654DDB40DFE70131A32768A86D17958E.description: Illustrate energy flow in food chains, food webs, and energy pyramids

654D9740DFE70131A32668A86D17958E.description: Summarize the characteristics of the levels of organization within ecosystems (including populations, communities, habitats, niches, and biomes).

654D4E40DFE70131A32568A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of how organisms interact with and respond to the biotic and abiotic components of their environment. (Earth Science, Life Science)

654CF4F0DFE70131A32468A86D17958E.description: Ecology: The Biotic and Abiotic Environment

654CA8C0DFE70131A32368A86D17958E.description: Explain the effects of disease on the major organs and body systems (including infectious diseases such as colds and flu, AIDS, and athlete's foot and noninfectious diseases such as diabetes, Parkinson's, and skin cancer).

654C5BC0DFE70131A32268A86D17958E.description: Summarize the relationships of the major body systems (including the circulatory, respiratory, digestive, excretory, nervous, muscular, and skeletal systems).

654C1980DFE70131A32168A86D17958E.description: Recall the major organs of the human body and their function within their particular body system.

654BD6E0DFE70131A32068A86D17958E.description: Summarize the levels of structural organization within the human body (including cells, tissues, organs, and systems).

654B8970DFE70131A31F68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the functions and interconnections of the major human body systems, including the breakdown in structure or function that disease causes. (Life Science)

654AF4D0DFE70131A31D68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between inherited traits and those acquired from environmental factors.

654AA870DFE70131A31C68A86D17958E.description: Use Punnett squares to predict inherited monohybrid traits.

654A5690DFE70131A31B68A86D17958E.description: Summarize how genetic information is passed from parent to offspring by using the terms genes, chromosomes, inherited traits, genotype, phenotype, dominant traits, and recessive traits.

654A1660DFE70131A31A68A86D17958E.description: Explain how cellular processes (including respiration, photosynthesis in plants, mitosis, and waste elimination) are essential to the survival of the organism.

6549D260DFE70131A31968A86D17958E.description: Compare the body shapes of bacteria (spiral, coccus, and bacillus) and the body structures that protists (euglena, paramecium, amoeba) use for food gathering and locomotion.

65498370DFE70131A31868A86D17958E.description: Compare the major components of plant and animal cells.

65494200DFE70131A31768A86D17958E.description: Summarize the structures and functions of the major components of plant and animal cells (including the cell wall, the cell membrane, the nucleus, chloroplasts, mitochondria, and vacuoles).

65490170DFE70131A31668A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the structure and function of cells, cellular reproduction, and heredity. (Life Science)

65487FB0DFE70131A31468A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate safety procedures when conducting investigations.

65483CF0DFE70131A31368A86D17958E.description: Critique a conclusion drawn from a scientific investigation.

6547F6B0DFE70131A31268A86D17958E.description: Explain the relationships between independent and dependent variables in a controlled scientific investigation through the use of appropriate graphs, tables, and charts.

6547A1A0DFE70131A31168A86D17958E.description: Explain the importance that repeated trials and a well-chosen sample size have with regard to the validity of a controlled scientific investigation.

65475ED0DFE70131A31068A86D17958E.description: Explain the reasons for testing one independent variable at a time in a controlled scientific investigation.

65471520DFE70131A30F68A86D17958E.description: Generate questions that can be answered through scientific investigation.

6546C840DFE70131A30E68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate tools and instruments (including a microscope) safely and accurately when conducting a controlled scientific investigation.

65468030DFE70131A30D68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of technological design and scientific inquiry, including process skills, mathematical thinking, controlled investigative design and analysis, and problem solving.

document.title: South Carolina Science Academic Standards

6532AFB0DFE70131A30A68A86D17958E.description: Illustrate ways that simple machines exist in common tools and in complex machines.

653271D0DFE70131A30968A86D17958E.description: Explain how the design of simple machines (including levers, pulleys, and inclined planes) helps reduce the amount of force required to do work.

65323480DFE70131A30868A86D17958E.description: Recognize that energy is the ability to do work (force exerted over a distance).

6531F610DFE70131A30768A86D17958E.description: Illustrate the directional transfer of heat energy through convection, radiation, and conduction.

6531B710DFE70131A30668A86D17958E.description: Illustrate energy transformations (including the production of light, sound, heat, and mechanical motion) in electrical circuits.

653175D0DFE70131A30568A86D17958E.description: Explain how magnetism and electricity are interrelated by using descriptions, models, and diagrams of electromagnets, generators, and simple electrical motors.

653124E0DFE70131A30468A86D17958E.description: Explain how energy can be transformed from one form to another (including the two types of mechanical energy, potential and kinetic, as well as chemical and electrical energy) in accordance with the law of conservation of energy.

6530D180DFE70131A30368A86D17958E.description: Identify the sources and properties of heat, solar, chemical, mechanical, and electrical energy.

653070B0DFE70131A30268A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the law of conservation of energy and the properties of energy and work. (Physical Science)

652FEFB0DFE70131A30068A86D17958E.description: Explain the influence of global winds and the jet stream on weather and climatic conditions.

652FAC10DFE70131A2FF68A86D17958E.description: Explain how convection affects weather patterns and climate.

652F6130DFE70131A2FE68A86D17958E.description: Explain how solar energy affects Earth's atmosphere and surface (land and water).

652EE8D0DFE70131A2FD68A86D17958E.description: Predict weather conditions and patterns based on weather data collected from direct observations and measurements, weather maps, satellites, and radar.

652E9A60DFE70131A2FC68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate instruments and tools to collect weather data (including wind speed and direction, air temperature, humidity, and air pressure).

652E5750DFE70131A2FB68A86D17958E.description: Summarize the relationship of the movement of air masses, high and low pressure systems, and frontal boundaries to storms (including thunderstorms, hurricanes, and tornadoes) and other weather conditions.

652E13A0DFE70131A2FA68A86D17958E.description: Classify shapes and types of clouds according to elevation and their associated weather conditions and patterns.

652DCB80DFE70131A2F968A86D17958E.description: Summarize the interrelationships among the dynamic processes of the water cycle (including precipitation, evaporation, transpiration, condensation, surface-water flow, and groundwater flow).

652D7A80DFE70131A2F868A86D17958E.description: Compare the composition and structure of Earth's atmospheric layers (including the gases and differences in temperature and pressure within the layers).

652D3790DFE70131A2F768A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the relationship between Earth's atmospheric properties and processes and its weather and climate. (Earth Science)

652CB1E0DFE70131A2F568A86D17958E.description: Compare learned to inherited behaviors in animals.

652C69C0DFE70131A2F468A86D17958E.description: Summarize how the internal stimuli (including hunger, thirst, and sleep) of animals ensure their survival.

652C19A0DFE70131A2F368A86D17958E.description: Illustrate animal behavioral responses (including hibernation, migration, defense, and courtship) to environmental stimuli.

652BC610DFE70131A2F268A86D17958E.description: Explain how environmental stimuli cause physical responses in animals (including shedding, blinking, shivering, sweating, panting, and food gathering).

652B5E50DFE70131A2F168A86D17958E.description: Compare the response that a warm-blooded (endothermic) animal makes to a fluctuation in environmental temperature with the response that a cold-blooded (ectothermic) animal makes to such a fluctuation.

652B1080DFE70131A2F068A86D17958E.description: Summarize the basic functions of the structures of animals that allow them to defend themselves, to move, and to obtain resources.

652ACBA0DFE70131A2EF68A86D17958E.description: Compare the characteristic structures of invertebrate animals (including sponges, segmented worms, echinoderms, mollusks, and arthropods) and vertebrate animals (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals).

652A8860DFE70131A2EE68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of structures, processes, and responses of animals that allow them to survive and reproduce. (Life Science)

652A4520DFE70131A2ED68A86D17958E.description: Structures, Processes, and Responses of Animals

6529FBC0DFE70131A2EC68A86D17958E.description: Explain how disease-causing fungi can affect plants.

6529ADA0DFE70131A2EB68A86D17958E.description: Explain how plants respond to external stimuli (including dormancy and the forms of tropism known as phototropism, gravitropism, hydrotropism, and thigmotropism).

65295180DFE70131A2EA68A86D17958E.description: Summarize the processes required for plant survival (including photosynthesis, respiration, and transpiration).

6528EAC0DFE70131A2E968A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between the processes of sexual and asexual reproduction of flowering plants.

6528A180DFE70131A2E868A86D17958E.description: Summarize each process in the life cycle of flowering plants (including germination, plant development, fertilization, and seed production).

65285880DFE70131A2E768A86D17958E.description: Summarize the basic functions of the structures of a flowering plant for defense, survival, and reproduction.

652808E0DFE70131A2E668A86D17958E.description: Compare the characteristic structures of various groups of plants (including vascular or nonvascular, seed or spore-producing, flowering or cone-bearing, and monocot or dicot).

6527C3F0DFE70131A2E568A86D17958E.description: Recognize the hierarchical structure of the classification (taxonomy) of organisms (including the seven major levels or categories of living things—namely, kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, and species).

65277990DFE70131A2E468A86D17958E.description: Summarize the characteristics that all organisms share (including the obtainment and use of resources for energy, the response to stimuli, the ability to reproduce, and process of physical growth and development).

65273220DFE70131A2E368A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of structures, processes, and responses of plants that allow them to survive and reproduce. (Life Science)

6526ED30DFE70131A2E268A86D17958E.description: Structures, Processes, and Responses of Plants

65269140DFE70131A2E168A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate safety procedures when conducting investigations.

65263960DFE70131A2E068A86D17958E.description: Use a technological design process to plan and produce a solution to a problem or a product (including identifying a problem, designing a solution or a product, implementing the design, and evaluating the solution or the product).

6525EEF0DFE70131A2DF68A86D17958E.description: Classify organisms, objects, and materials according to their physical characteristics by using a dichotomous key.

6525A8C0DFE70131A2DE68A86D17958E.description: Differentiate between observation and inference during the analysis and interpretation of data.

65256310DFE70131A2DD68A86D17958E.description: Use appropriate tools and instruments (including a spring scale, beam balance, barometer, and sling psychrometer) safely and accurately when conducting a controlled scientific investigation.

65251630DFE70131A2DC68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of technological design and scientific inquiry, including process skills, mathematical thinking, controlled investigative design and analysis, and problem solving.

53E469F0DFE70131883168A86D17958E.description: Analyze and describe characteristics of the media arts that exist across time and among diverse cultural and ethnic groups.

53E3F300DFE70131883068A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate ways that media artwork portrays the people and cultures of the world.

53E397C0DFE70131882F68A86D17958E.description: Describe ways that information from past and present culture has influenced the evolution of the media arts.

53E34A20DFE70131882E68A86D17958E.description: The student will understand the context and history of the development of the media arts from the late nineteenth century to present and will recognize the role of media artwork in world cultures.

53E2A0E0DFE70131882C68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate the effects of the media arts in the global economy.

53E25120DFE70131882B68A86D17958E.description: Analyze and evaluate the financial aspects of media arts productions, including budget responsibility and career opportunities.

53E1F9C0DFE70131882A68A86D17958E.description: Communicate an understanding of the relationship between the media arts and other arts disciplines and other content areas.

53E1A370DFE70131882968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ways that the media arts relate to everyday life and activities in the world at large.

53E146E0DFE70131882868A86D17958E.description: The student will make connections between the media arts and other arts disciplines, other content areas, and the world.

53E0A8D0DFE70131882668A86D17958E.description: Describe the characteristics of particular media art forms and explain ways that they convey meaning and influence their audience.

53E05B80DFE70131882568A86D17958E.description: Analyze the manner in which the language, tone, and point of view used in media texts work to influence the meaning and interpretation of messages.

53E00E70DFE70131882468A86D17958E.description: Evaluate the creative techniques used in a variety of media texts (for example, television, film, radio, Internet).

53DFC5E0DFE70131882368A86D17958E.description: Identify the codes and conventions used in media texts and explain the ways in which they help to create meaning.

53DF7B30DFE70131882268A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate comprehension of the effectiveness of the presentation and treatment of ideas in media texts.

53DED1A0DFE70131882068A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ways in which a variety of media texts address their intended purpose and audience.

53DE8410DFE70131881F68A86D17958E.description: The student will access, analyze, interpret, and create media texts.

53DDEED0DFE70131881D68A86D17958E.description: Apply elements of artistic design specific to individual media.

53DDA460DFE70131881C68A86D17958E.description: Describe processes used in the creation of media artwork and identify the products that are the result of those processes.

53DD5800DFE70131881B68A86D17958E.description: Create media artwork that communicates his or her experiences and reflects an analysis of social or community issues.

53DCFE50DFE70131881A68A86D17958E.description: Communicate effectively using media arts vocabulary.

53DCB4E0DFE70131881968A86D17958E.description: The student will create media artwork that demonstrates an understanding and command of the principles of artistic design.

53DC2300DFE70131881768A86D17958E.description: Create self-led and peer-led instruction and assessment materials for evaluating media artwork.

53DBD7B0DFE70131881668A86D17958E.description: Utilize information literacy skills to make informed decisions using digital tools and resources in the creation of media artwork.

53DB7C90DFE70131881568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate an understanding of and respect for the accepted procedures regarding the responsible care of media arts equipment and materials.

53DB32F0DFE70131881468A86D17958E.description: Use a variety of media technologies, techniques, and processes to communicate ideas.

53DAEB70DFE70131881368A86D17958E.description: Identify the specific skills, knowledge, and abilities necessary for creating media artwork.

53DA98C0DFE70131881268A86D17958E.description: The student will develop and expand his or her knowledge of the processes, techniques, and applications used in the creation of media artwork.

document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards for Health and Safety Education

68C81440DFE70131A88568A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate the ability to select healthy foods.

68C7D3C0DFE70131A88468A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate practices that promote personal health (for example, washing hands, brushing teeth, combing hair) and practices that prevent the spread of disease (for example, covering coughs and sneezes).

68C790D0DFE70131A88368A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ways to be safe as a pedestrian and as a passenger in a car and in a bus.

68C743E0DFE70131A88268A86D17958E.description: Describe fire safety rules for home and school (for example, "if clothing is on fire, stop, drop, and roll," "get out of the burning building and meet in a safe place," "do not play with fire").

68C6F8F0DFE70131A88168A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate the ability to practice health-enhancing behaviors and avoid or reduce health risks.

68C6AA70DFE70131A88068A86D17958E.description: Set a goal to brush his or her teeth twice a day.

68C66D40DFE70131A87F68A86D17958E.description: Set a goal to be active at recess.

68C62FD0DFE70131A87E68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate the ability to use goal-setting skills to enhance health.

68C5F170DFE70131A87D68A86D17958E.description: Identify situations that require action to protect personal safety.

68C5B350DFE70131A87C68A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate the ability to use decision-making skills to enhance health.

68C57280DFE70131A87B68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate ways to say "no" to alcohol and tobacco.

68C52B60DFE70131A87A68A86D17958E.description: Explain ways to identify trustworthy adults to tell when someone is in need of help, feels threatened, or has been harmed.

68C4D460DFE70131A87968A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate how to make an emergency phone call.

68C48A40DFE70131A87868A86D17958E.description: Name healthy ways to express needs, wants, and feelings.

68C42980DFE70131A87768A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate the ability to use interpersonal communication skills to enhance health and avoid or reduce health risks.

68C3DE60DFE70131A87668A86D17958E.description: Discuss why medical checkups and dental checkups are needed for a person to stay healthy.

68C39CF0DFE70131A87568A86D17958E.description: Explain ways to identify trustworthy adults from whom he or she can safely take medicine.

68C35AE0DFE70131A87468A86D17958E.description: Explain ways to identify trustworthy adults who can help him or her deal with personal feelings.

68C30E60DFE70131A87368A86D17958E.description: The student will demonstrate the ability to access valid information and products and services to enhance health.

68C2CF80DFE70131A87268A86D17958E.description: Identify how the family influences personal health practices and behaviors.

68C291C0DFE70131A87168A86D17958E.description: Identify ways that family and friends can help a person stay safe and avoid injury.

68C252F0DFE70131A87068A86D17958E.description: The student will analyze the influence of family, peers, culture, media, technology, and other factors on health behaviors.

68C211A0DFE70131A86F68A86D17958E.description: Explain why the body needs daily physical activity.

68C164B0DFE70131A86D68A86D17958E.description: Explain why the body needs food (including breakfast) and water.

68C108A0DFE70131A86C68A86D17958E.description: Explain why getting enough sleep is important.

68C0C950DFE70131A86B68A86D17958E.description: Explain why it is important to brush the teeth and go to a dentist.

68C08BF0DFE70131A86A68A86D17958E.description: Name behaviors that affect personal health (for example, bathing, washing hands, eating healthy foods).

68C04E20DFE70131A86968A86D17958E.description: Define the terms "health," "health behaviors," "health checkups," and "health risks."

68BFCEB0DFE70131A86768A86D17958E.description: Explain how families are alike and different (for example, have several brothers and/or sisters, have only one child, have one parent working outside the home, have a grandparent living in the home, have a pet). Note: References to homosexuality are prohibited by the Comprehensive Health Act except in the context of instruction concerning sexually transmitted diseases.

68BF8B50DFE70131A86668A86D17958E.description: Name ways children grow and change.

68BF43F0DFE70131A86568A86D17958E.description: Name the five senses and describe what they do.

68BECAE0DFE70131A86368A86D17958E.description: Identify warning symbols on medicines, household cleaners, and yard chemicals.

68BE8F30DFE70131A86268A86D17958E.description: Identify ways that drugs can be helpful or harmful.

68BE4FD0DFE70131A86168A86D17958E.description: Distinguish between medicines and other substances that may look like medicines.

68BDB950DFE70131A85F68A86D17958E.description: Explain what a person should do to deal with a minor injury (for example, cut, scrape, nosebleed).

68BD7470DFE70131A85E68A86D17958E.description: Name ways to stay safe around strangers.

68BD3100DFE70131A85D68A86D17958E.description: Identify appropriate ways to deal with specific emergency situations.

68BCCC10DFE70131A85C68A86D17958E.description: Identify ways to prevent common childhood injuries at home (for example, falling down the stairs, drinking an unknown substance, finding a gun), school (for example, climbing on playground equipment), or in the environment (for example, running across the street, riding a bicycle, swimming, walking in a rainstorm, approaching an unknown animal).

68BC7F60DFE70131A85B68A86D17958E.description: Define the term "feelings" (for example, happy, sad, angry).

68BC30B0DFE70131A85A68A86D17958E.description: The student will comprehend concepts related to health promotion to enhance health.

document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards and Performance Indicators for Science

648BAA19A53847BC8E285F5FC6C272FE.description: Obtain and communicate information about how various instruments are used to extend human senses by transmitting and detecting waves (such as radio, television, cell phones, and wireless computer networks) to exemplify how technological advancements and designs meet human needs.

737DE2BF3D774089AF7DED3CDB813B71.description: Construct explanations for how humans see color as a result of the transmission, absorption, and reflection of light waves by various materials.

680F542F632645429211AA120E29EA63.description: Analyze and interpret data to describe the behavior of mechanical waves as they intersect.

6491EDC11BBE4DE68CAC1E4936E76DD0.description: Analyze and interpret data to describe the behavior of waves (including refraction, reflection, transmission, and absorption) as they interact with various materials.

5F179C5D8B974E2ABFF24D6041556D79.description: Develop and use models to exemplify the basic properties of waves (including frequency, amplitude, wavelength, and speed).

9BD65C2559B3479D90320814FE868FBF.description: Construct explanations of the relationship between matter and energy based on the characteristics of mechanical and light waves.

4A87E238EE504420A3184AA630D04CAE.description: Waves (including sound and seismic waves, waves on water, and light waves) have energy and transfer energy when they interact with matter. Waves are a repeating pattern of motion that transfers energy from place to place without overall displacement of matter. All types of waves have some features in common. When waves interact, they superimpose upon or interfere with each other resulting in changes to the amplitude. Major modern technologies are based on waves and their interactions with matter.

20517FF5BB204D7AA03268277E4EEC4D.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the properties and behaviors of waves.

B6CA9753DB6541AEBE9879C6D4837F61.description: Use mathematical and computational thinking to describe the relationship between the speed and velocity (including positive and negative expression of direction) of an object in determining average speed (v=d/t).

8EC5723536E04D778AC5E8DB97737655.description: Use mathematical and computational thinking to generate graphs that represent the motion of an object's position and speed as a function of time.

C91BE20FE0EB48F39F4D2EAAC036EBA0.description: Analyze and interpret data to describe and predict the effects of forces (including gravitational and friction) on the speed and direction of an object.

E4F547F81AC9481B8FE96363F76686BA.description: Analyze and interpret data to support claims that for every force exerted on an object there is an equal force exerted in the opposite direction (Newton's Third Law of Motion).

E10EAAADA659494CBCF108098BEE25E0.description: Construct explanations for the relationship between the mass of an object and the concept of inertia (Newton's First Law of Motion).

592BF3EAED9D43D4AEED052620BACCDD.description: Develop and use models to compare and predict the resulting effect of balanced and unbalanced forces on an object's motion in terms of magnitude and direction.

7986C2A7050F45A6810FC976D84A8F14.description: Plan and conduct controlled scientific investigations to test how varying the amount of force or mass of an object affects the motion (speed and direction), shape, or orientation of an object.

70E796964AB44BA89CE57CEA4234EA32.description: Motion occurs when there is a change in position of an object with respect to a reference point. The final position of an object is determined by measuring the change in position and direction of the segments along a trip. While the speed of the object may vary during the total time it is moving, the average speed is the result of the total distance divided by the total time taken. Forces acting on an object can be balanced or unbalanced. Varying the amount of force or mass will affect the motion of an object. Inertia is the tendency of objects to resist any change in motion.

15705097AB08400E97140C00F0A76552.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the effects of forces on the motion and stability of an object.

9DCA51AA51674B44899EAFBC4FC9CEC7.description: Obtain and communicate information to support claims that natural and human-made factors can contribute to the extinction of species.

23D347CA7E46461F8FAA8589CBEB4675.description: Construct explanations for how biological adaptations and genetic variations of traits in a population enhance the probability of survival in a particular environment.

809F0783D1794C128050A840A87C6257.description: Adaptation by natural selection acting over generations is one important process by which species change in response to changes in environmental conditions. The resources of biological communities can be used within sustainable limits, but if the ecosystem becomes unbalanced in ways that prevent the sustainable use of resources, then ecosystem degradation and species extinction can occur.

6D2415C2E90E49BE833BC4C6ABFAF58C.description: Construct explanations for why most individual organisms, as well as some entire taxonomic groups of organisms, that lived in the past were never fossilized.

32419DAD0BF34EC295402227A7F5EF66.description: Construct and analyze scientific arguments to support claims that different types of fossils provide evidence of (1) the diversity of life that has been present on Earth, (2) relationships between past and existing life forms, and (3) environmental changes that have occurred during Earth's history.

229197390EAA45D38DC5B28F315C3ABA.description: Construct explanations from evidence for how catastrophic events (including volcanic activities, earthquakes, climatic changes, and the impact of an asteroid/comet) may have affected the conditions on Earth and the diversity of its life forms.

20F90A67C0E64F77BE61311E084F3FDB.description: Analyze and interpret data from index fossil records and the ordering of rock layers to infer the relative age of rocks and fossils.

5757CDE83BDF4D0F8DD9A5B40916FC12.description: Develop and use models to organize Earth's history (including era, period, and epoch) according to the geologic time scale using evidence from rock layers.

42A4B5D676FF4CF9B0C258C4584DBC87.description: The geologic time scale interpreted from rock strata provides a way to organize major historical events in Earth's history. Analysis of rock strata and the fossil record, which documents the existence, diversity, extinction, and change of many life forms throughout history, provide only relative dates, not an absolute scale. Changes in life forms are shaped by Earth's varying geological conditions.

85C4216C9DFC465684D3FA9AD4A6EBE6.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of Earth's geologic history and its diversity of life over time.

309F3DC20E4A409E9590C220F17BE3FA.description: Earth Science: Earth's History and Diversity of Life

138F39F44D314FC3807BF8A807630FDA.description: Obtain and communicate information regarding the physical and chemical properties of minerals, ores, and fossil fuels to describe their importance as Earth resources.

7DD253C276604DF2B5D3204E049DF9FD.description: Humans depend upon many Earth resources – some renewable over human lifetimes and some nonrenewable or irreplaceable. Resources are distributed unevenly around the planet as a result of past geological processes.

A2C0303CD9E148EA9707C28163AAC8E1.description: Define problems that may be caused by a catastrophic event resulting from plate movements and design possible devices or solutions to minimize the effects of that event on Earth's surface and/or human structures.

AA4A65E2BAFF45D79184DF08ABC67DB0.description: Construct explanations of how forces inside Earth result in earthquakes and volcanoes.

6EFA11632B2749D7A8A4ECC583761D19.description: Analyze and interpret data to describe patterns in the location of volcanoes and earthquakes related to tectonic plate boundaries, interactions, and hot spots.

4050E27FC5184E178D0A97B464AFFB0B.description: Natural processes can cause sudden or gradual changes to Earth's systems. Some may adversely affect humans such as volcanic eruptions or earthquakes. Mapping the history of natural hazards in a region, combined with an understanding of related geological forces can help forecast the locations and likelihoods of future events.

E6EAA8D81B4C42C7A5A43AFD1D880360.description: Construct and analyze scientific arguments to support claims that plate tectonics accounts for (1) the distribution of fossils on different continents, (2) the occurrence of earthquakes, and (3) continental and ocean floor features (including mountains, volcanoes, faults and trenches).

D98193779333414BBD625F017F5860FD.description: Construct explanations for how the theory of plate tectonics accounts for (1) the motion of lithospheric plates, (2) the geologic activities at plate boundaries, and (3) the changes in landform areas over geologic time.

43E77F3A9C6142AF85A5ED955676ACB9.description: Obtain and communicate information about the relative position, density, and composition of Earth's layers to describe the crust, mantle, and core.

53F35565D65640DDB19230885DB2D7CB.description: Use the rock cycle model to describe the relationship between the processes and forces that create igneous, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks.

2CD07B626D144BEC89B228160664BE49.description: Develop and use models to explain how the processes of weathering, erosion, and deposition change surface features in the environment.

6A71F8D6593A49108F764B051402A12C.description: All Earth processes are the result of energy flowing and matter cycling within and among Earth's systems. Because Earth's processes are dynamic and interactive in nature, the surface of Earth is constantly changing. Earth's hot interior is a main source of energy that drives the cycling and moving of materials. Plate tectonics is the unifying theory that explains the past and current crustal movements at the Earth's surface. This theory provides a framework for understanding geological history.

A5D7053636214F91950526279B9C1AD3.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the processes that alter the structure of Earth and provide resources for life on the planet.

A64196EB1BAE4F39B7F7B341CF76D6C1.description: Earth Science: Earth Systems and Resources

038F386BCBA147A9B2B99CF4CEAE0949.description: Analyze and interpret data from the surface features of the Sun (including photosphere, corona, sunspots, prominences, and solar flares) to predict how these features may affect Earth.

B34C93D29C714A2B9F84B96CF64E5158.description: Obtain and communicate information to describe how data from technologies (including telescopes, spectroscopes, satellites, space probes) provide information about objects in the solar system and the universe.

6F4F013DE6D74AC785FA4225E00BAB4A.description: Develop and use models to explain how motions within the Sun-Earth-Moon system cause Earth phenomena (including day and year, moon phases, solar and lunar eclipses, and tides).

E9709595B9E34DD396C40D213C253653.description: Develop and use models to explain how seasons, caused by the tilt of Earth's axis as it orbits the Sun, affects the length of the day and the amount of heating on Earth's surface.

EFFE818D3CEF4D70B2262C544DAFC0FF.description: Construct explanations for how gravity affects the motion of objects in the solar system and tides on Earth.

0294177D5958443492EE47F90592EF97.description: Obtain and communicate information to model and compare the characteristics and movements of objects in the solar system (including planets, moons, asteroids, comets, and meteors).

CCEC445995424574A82042034E3E8078.description: Earth's solar system consists of the Sun and other objects that are held in orbit around the Sun by its gravitational pull on them. Motions within the Earth-Moon-Sun system have effects that can be observed on Earth.

C780616D31454E4FBF1C565791894B65.description: Construct and analyze scientific arguments to support claims that the universe began with a period of extreme and rapid expansion using evidence from the composition of stars and gases and the motion of galaxies in the universe.

06E5905FD9124C2C90733A10F5A19436.description: Obtain and communicate information to model the position of the Sun in the universe, the shapes and composition of galaxies, and the measurement unit needed to identify star and galaxy locations.

26AFBC43111D49C0A413F9E7D44E9470.description: Earth's solar system is part of the Milky Way Galaxy, which is one of many galaxies in the universe. The planet Earth is a tiny part of a vast universe that has developed over a span of time beginning with a period of extreme and rapid expansion.

F9B3376AEB544EE8BB7B084603E29DC0.description: The student will demonstrate an understanding of the universe and the predictable patterns caused by Earth's movement in the solar system.

6D710529BC584841A81B477EE520461F.description: Earth Science: Earth's Place in the Universe

086533292A054FA0A3E8E236546ADF9B.description: Construct devices or design solutions using scientific knowledge to solve specific problems or needs: (1) ask questions to identify problems or needs, (2) ask questions about the criteria and constraints of the device or solutions, (3) generate and communicate ideas for possible devices or solutions, (4) build and test devices or solutions, (5) determine if the devices or solutions solved the problem and refine the design if needed, and (6) communicate the results.

E9BEC06C4EE64E7CAE7FC3D013B3A319.description: Technology is any modification to the natural world created to fulfill the wants and needs of humans. The engineering design process involves a series of iterative steps used to solve a problem and often leads to the development of a new or improved technology.

837D4873C13A4D2DB93A92603D3E81B8.description: Obtain and evaluate scientific information to (1) answer questions, (2) explain or describe phenomena, (3) develop models, (4) evaluate hypotheses, explanations, claims, or designs or (5) identify and/or fill gaps in knowledge. Communicate using the conventions and expectations of scientific writing or oral presentations by (1) evaluating grade-appropriate primary or secondary scientific literature, or (2) reporting the results of student experimental investigations.

ED0A0A9364EB4D8291FAF90869DF0485.description: Construct and analyze scientific arguments to support claims, explanations, or designs using evidence from observations, data, or informational texts.

15BA44E641114815B37429350A6C3A08.description: Construct explanations of phenomena using (1) primary or secondary scientific evidence and models, (2) conclusions from scientific investigations, (3) predictions based on observations and measurements, or (4) data communicated in graphs, tables, or diagrams.

2D92B92FA35640B0A4D0F42B9DC02243.description: Use mathematical and computational thinking to (1) use and manipulate appropriate metric units, (2) collect and analyze data, (3) express relationships between variables for models and investigations, or (4) use grade-level appropriate statistics to analyze data.

61C0AA4A03594F2B90DF62210092C158.description: Analyze and interpret data from informational texts, observations, measurements, or investigations using a range of methods (such as tabulation, graphing, or statistical analysis) to (1) reveal patterns and construct meaning or (2) support hypotheses, explanations, claims, or designs.

8E257A92A64048B4A6E78C5A38E24412.description: Plan and conduct controlled scientific investigations to answer questions, test hypotheses, and develop explanations: (1) formulate scientific questions and testable hypotheses, (2) identify materials, procedures, and variables, (3) select and use appropriate tools or instruments to collect qualitative and quantitative data, and (4) record and represent data in an appropriate form. Use appropriate safety procedures.

41CB6AC5C5CB4C70A2E0A68C306A0878.description: Develop, use, and refine models to (1) understand or represent phenomena, processes, and relationships, (2) test devices or solutions, or (3) communicate ideas to others.

72481B1FC1DC441FB43EEA79431FD73F.description: Ask questions to (1) generate hypotheses for scientific investigations, (2) refine models, explanations, or designs, or (3) extend the results of investigations or challenge claims.

CA6FB7010BFF4D61A3CAAAF1997C6ABE.description: The practices of science and engineering support the development of science concepts, develop the habits of mind that are necessary for scientific thinking, and allow students to engage in science in ways that are similar to those used by scientists and engineers.

E33D2D3E84C444AB8E8FA56553A80B19.description: The student will use the science and engineering practices, including the processes and skills of scientific inquiry, to develop understandings of science content.

document.title: Common Core State Standards for English Language Arts & Literacy in History/Social Studies, Science, and Technical Subjects

5B604360DFE70131952B68A86D17958E.description: Acquire and use accurately grade-appropriate general academic and domain-specific words and phrases; gather vocabulary knowledge when considering a word or phrase important to comprehension or expression.

5B5FEDA0DFE70131952A68A86D17958E.description: Distinguish among the connotations (associations) of words with similar denotations (definitions) (e.g., stingy, scrimping, economical, unwasteful, thrifty).

5B5FA100DFE70131952968A86D17958E.description: Use the relationship between particular words (e.g., cause/effect, part/whole, item/category) to better understand each of the words.

5B5F4FF0DFE70131952868A86D17958E.description: Interpret figures of speech (e.g., personification) in context.

5B5EFD80DFE70131952768A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate understanding of figurative language, word relationships, and nuances in word meanings.

5B5EAAF0DFE70131952668A86D17958E.description: Verify the preliminary determination of the meaning of a word or phrase (e.g., by checking the inferred meaning in context or in a dictionary).

5B5E52F0DFE70131952568A86D17958E.description: Consult reference materials (e.g., dictionaries, glossaries, thesauruses), both print and digital, to find the pronunciation of a word or determine or clarify its precise meaning or its part of speech.

5B5DEAA0DFE70131952468A86D17958E.description: Use common, grade-appropriate Greek or Latin affixes and roots as clues to the meaning of a word (e.g., audience, auditory, audible).

5B5D7140DFE70131952368A86D17958E.description: Use context (e.g., the overall meaning of a sentence or paragraph; a word's position or function in a sentence) as a clue to the meaning of a word or phrase.

5B5D1B20DFE70131952268A86D17958E.description: Determine or clarify the meaning of unknown and multiple-meaning words and phrases based on grade 6 reading and content, choosing flexibly from a range of strategies.

5B5C75D0DFE70131952068A86D17958E.description: Maintain consistency in style and tone.

5B5C05E0DFE70131951F68A86D17958E.description: Vary sentence patterns for meaning, reader/listener interest, and style.

5B5B9FC0DFE70131951E68A86D17958E.description: Use knowledge of language and its conventions when writing, speaking, reading, or listening.

5B5A9D40DFE70131951B68A86D17958E.description: Use punctuation (commas, parentheses, dashes) to set off nonrestrictive/parenthetical elements.

5B5A4C90DFE70131951A68A86D17958E.description: Demonstrate command of the conventions of standard English capitalization, punctuation, and spelling when writing.

5B59FE80DFE70131951968A86D17958E.description: Recognize variations from standard English in their own and others' writing and speaking, and identify and use strategies to improve expression in conventional language.

5B59A850DFE70131951868A86D17958E.description: Recognize and correct vague pronouns (i.e., ones with unclear or ambiguous antecedents).

5B595AA0DFE70131951768A86D17958E.description: Recognize and correct inappropriate shifts in pronoun number and person.

5B58A150DFE70131951568A86D17958E.description: Ensure that pronouns are in the proper case (subjective, objective, possessive).

document.title: South Carolina Academic Standards for Health and Safety Education

68FEFF60DFE70131A8F068A86D17958E.description: Encourage others to protect and improve the environment.

68FEAEF0DFE70131A8EF68A86D17958E.description: Encourage friends and family members to make positive health choices regarding ATOD.
