49B72610E80C44BAB3EDE4EA365358CC.description:
Express opinions
about their abilities in
different areas (“I’m a
good friend.” I can run
fast.” “I know all my
letters!”).

C0230A31D7F4488D8A98850AA4CF1BE6.description:
Stick with tasks
even when they are
challenging.

C5316BABD6464A0A9CDCB027105E2447.description: Express the belief that they can do many things.

58B5932498F947108912A86A70D17A70.description: Express positive feelings about themselves by showing and/or telling others about themselves, things they like, or things they have done.

0F7E9D01A12146A2986EB3D23B9D4B6D.description:
Attempt to reach
goals without help
from others (push adult
away, say “Me do it
myself!”).

E5BDDF56A6B74204ADF2FD9F6229E314.description:
Show confidence
in their abilities
through actions and/
or language (try to lift a
heavy object, say, “I’m
strong!”).

FC04A78A6E2240D98BCC2348B86405AB.description:
Explore the environment independently to satisfy their own interests (seek out toy
or favorite materials).

CFEA5462F6B54AA89C10B7DA3168FF13.description: Express positive feelings about themselves by showing and/or themselves, things they like, or things they have done. ESD-2g

97A52EE0550943DCA4B357F550D27C04.description:
Bring others things
they like or show
them things they have
done.

291E8DB84F594A35A9E52145FF70784D.description:
Show confidence in
their ability to make
things happen by
repeating or changing
their actions to reach
a goal (move closer to
reach an object they
want).

38A12CDCEEBB4248AD78726B9138ECBE.description:
Explore the
environment on their
own, but check in
with a familiar, trusted
adult occasionally.

435EF6E65B704504AA49D43B3FAFB290.description:
Explore the
environment with
support from a familiar,
trusted adult.

A19F8FD80F2C422593DBE738EBED6F6C.description:
Show pleasure at
things they have done
(wiggle, coo, laugh).

CF679EDB775044EE922CB3D5335C7624.description:
Show they expect
results from their
actions (repeat loud
noise to gain attention,
hit toy over and over to
produce sound).

98DAB8DD78FF4528B611551017012509.description: Children express positive feelings about themselves and confidence in what they can do.

7153FBF032E64448A29EB70B8963CE70.description:
Choose to spend
more time on preferred
activities, and express
awareness of skills
they are developing.

4E7503F40CC2433090CA16BD84AEB14F.description:
Express awareness
that they are members
of different groups
(e.g., family, preschool
class, ethnic group).

5529DE36008B460CBD56D31682E6175B.description:
Describe themselves
in concrete ways, with
greater detail and
accuracy (“My eyes
are brown.” “I am
tall.”).

8F90D342F6E54B1D995214BD7F37F2DB.description:
Choose activities
they like and name
their favorite activities.

578E1D31274A473488E991EEBEDC1E64.description:
Use own first and
last name.

7ADB86503A0D4C11BBC9E2402D6A5EB5.description:
Express a sense of
belonging to a group
(say “There’s Kirby
from my class,” move
to stand with own
group upon request, “I
am a girl.”).

06A101C57A934B50B849B9100B92D4CC.description:
Describe self
(characteristics
that can be seen,
things they can do,
things they like,
possessions).

D69A43509CAD4369A9511C43DA8E1699.description:
Make choices and
have favorite clothes,
toys, and activities.

043636CAEB1548B8A9EA3FB2031B3D39.description:
Use their own name
or a personal pronoun
to refer to themselves
(I, me, and mine).

F6EB1A84564544F087FAFED4E23A70C3.description:
Show awareness
of some of their own
characteristics and
things they can do
(recognize themselves
in pictures, say, “I help
Daddy!”).

AC4736CB92BF4567B1E54B415B99707C.description:
Express choices
with gestures, signs,
or words (select a toy
they want).

19338F8E60D444978428480D2F4BD475.description:
Recognize
themselves in a mirror
(point to self, make
faces in mirror).

831127A454F34837A054518406B978A1.description:
Show awareness of
specific body parts.

E9AF1FA2AED548818A843FEC93CC897F.description:
Express likes and
dislikes (smile, cry, and
protest).

34F5D60CC3ED44F3B7E21CEC3490676E.description:
Respond to their
name with sounds or
movement.

C7207DADDDB44119BCC3FD07C38B7A62.description:
Show interest in
their image in a mirror
(stare, smile, reach out
to touch).

2390D7DD20644FD0B181AD22AA841072.description:
Show awareness
of their bodies (study
own hands and feet
moving; use hands,
mouth, and eyes in
coordination to explore
their bodies).

4C1E5DB8411F4D1DA3EDA8CB1CBD8713.description: Children demonstrate a positive sense of self-identity and self-awareness.

document.title: South Carolina Early Learning Standards

CF109BA644D449AFA2699A2344FE146D.description:
Identify people who
can help them in the
community (police,
firefighter, nurse).

781965EF5E7647DB8FD2603EF4F118C5.description:
Consistently
recognize and avoid
objects, substances,
and activities within
the environment that
might cause harm.

0D38D714616E4611A74DDE7C41581717.description:
Call a trusted adult when someone gets
injured or is in an unsafe situation.

FB57D55F6B8D41329295AB152CB4A3EC.description:
Usually recognize and avoid objects and situations that might
cause harm.

E7483AE9D310436FB0E89F163C1102B4.description: Know what their bodies can do, and play within their abilities to avoid injury to self or others.

BC07D7960DEF49C3B664DB80E20BBDAA.description:
With guidance, recognize and avoid situations that might
cause harm.

60892703733042ABA9E5599EAE256F83.description:
Increase self-control over their impulses (remind self not to touch something; wait for adult vs. running
ahead).

F8B78BC86BE843C5ABF777B9C64B6DB6.description:
Remember cause and effect experiences and apply their experiences to future situations (avoid touching cold railing, walk slowly down
steep hill where fall happened).

72050002B3D04F1FA937F3F33AE2D373.description:
Respond to simple
warnings that prevent
harm (“Stop!” “Hot!”
“Wait!”).

EE5B958DC0874DADA0E2D0775FD14E60.description:
Show some caution
about unfamiliar and/
or unsafe situations.

4ADA42B0AC5C4CB5B20947F9D9A28095.description:
Watch for adult
reactions to unfamiliar
things or situations
that might be
dangerous.

85B7E03CE2A94D638FDCCBA89EC1996C.description:
Notice and imitate
adults’ reactions
to new people and
situations.

FF66A92F9B7C4C5CB3C9A07E14D48A56.description:
Show trust in familiar
caregivers (calm down
with adult help, make
eye contact with
caregivers).

DC6A594CB42D4FFFB22E84DBCF3BAEFD.description: Children develop awareness of basic safety rules and begin to follow them.

F1004D38E16D47B0B7724AB16C3E3318.description:
Describe the value of
good health practices
(wash hands to get rid
of germs, drink milk to
build strong bones).

02636BD66DB140D6A8FC9135FF6D7449.description:
Perform tasks
to maintain the
indoor and outdoor
learning environment
independently.

A2911C66AD9C46A290C898F384C4BCDF.description:
Use adaptive equipment, ask for help with positioning
and movement, and/or
participate in medical
care routines as
needed.

C0D4DB5665D344209C7C390CC31F4B61.description:
Name people who help children
stay healthy.

B4ADF09D4A2047EEAB41D8778867FDC0.description:
Help with routine care of the
indoor and outdoor learning
environment (recycle, care for
garden).

9169CEA08E7B43C9BBAB5354A54C3C05.description:
Gain independence in hygiene
practices (throw tissues away
and wash hands, flush toilet).

77B52F4BFBEF49459FDFCD206C077BF2.description:
Follow basic hygiene practices
with reminders (brush teeth,
wash hands, use toilet, cough
into elbow).

B0E659F5E2F143009879E844340978F8.description:
Dress and undress themselves
with occasional assistance.

053D174258734FAC9FEEB743FD15D7D3.description:
Use adaptive equipment, ask for help with positioning and movement, and/or participate in
medical care routines as needed.

F09EE58CFA804A15A4E88F74981DA2A1.description:
Begin to take care
of objects (put toys
away, handle materials
carefully, water plants
or garden).

5E5F96CB59A444DEAA85401063FAC8BA.description:
Help with meal and
snack routines.

E78188BC0A3C4E6FBA0A7F37750BF243.description:
Initiate self-care
routines and complete
with guidance (put on
some clothes, undress,
throw away paper
towel, begin to show
an interest in toileting).

1C0118EAB7D640A38EF0A24B4D764C67.description:
Use adaptive
equipment, ask for
help with positioning
and movement, and/or
participate in medical
care routines as
needed.

8841AD77A79A4DEAB0E1D2A365FE92E8.description:
Drink from a cup
(with or without a lid)
and feed themselves
with their fingers or a
spoon.

818B5448E6FC4C8893AD0D6CAB436590.description:
Cooperate and help
with care routines and
cleanup (mouth care,
hand-washing,
diapering, dressing,
bathing).

F842D9E3E92140B3884F4747D2DB865A.description:
Show interest and
assist in routines
(open mouth for milk
or spoon, raise arms
for dressing).

1EDAF7A836204927A7D49F4DB9B82466.description:
Accept care
routines (mouth care,
handwashing,
diapering, dressing,
and bathing).

ADD50A04AA5841EBA712EA698EB9162F.description: Children develop independence in caring for themselves and their environment.

4940BA64E02F400187552C377AA5515F.description:
Consistently use
strategies to calm
themselves when
needed.

374E17E5B9104F2DA65808C3C3571981.description:
Use language to
ask adults or peers
specifically for the kind
of help needed in a
particular situation.

675FE0C0D523492A88BD56884A5D9920.description:
Use different
strategies to calm
themselves when
needed (self-talk,
deep breathing, cozy
corner).

40E14E20998E48F3808FA3967AC87E75.description:
Use words, signs,
or sign language to
ask for the things
they need (food when
hungry, drink when
thirsty, go outdoors
when they need to
be physically active).

CE284AF9F81C4BC28CEB7DAA3E2583C7.description:
Soothe themselves
when needed (find a
quiet area for alone
time, look at book
before nap).

2859B0F8ECB44E99973C087987818951.description:
Use words, signs,
or sign language to
ask for the things
they need (food when
hungry, drink when
thirsty, go outdoors
when they need to
be physically active).

82B207CDD7494784954FE84A21083656.description:
Use objects and
follow routines that
are comforting (get
their blanket and lie
down where they
usually sleep,
pick out favorite book
to be read before
lunch).

8827260397704E68B863BBB89430657C.description:
Use gestures,
words, signs, or
sign language to
communicate what
they need.

AAFEC27BC673498595178EBA2A307735.description:
Begin to soothe
themselves (suck
thumb, find pacifier,
reach for a security
object).

B132A582E72145B1B270D7191B802C1D.description:
Use different sounds
to let caregivers know
they need attention.

5184D581D4E24C4887C6B949D7EEB635.description: Children develop awareness of their needs and the ability to communicate their needs.

B6550ADA6A924A05864931149E28E7D5.description:
Use tools that require
strength and dexterity
of small muscles with
a moderate degree of
control (spray bottle,
hole puncher).

87FB21FE6E6F466999418F7CA1F51D43.description:
Engage in complex
hand-eye coordination
activities with a
moderate degree of
precision and control
(fasten clothing, cut
shapes, put together
small pieces).

AA64063A67114B35916F61857EE2F1E4.description:
Draw and write
smaller figures with
more detail (faces
with features, letters,
or letter-like forms).

68451A5CDF8547968A0196D08B1A2849.description:
Use tools that
require strength,
control, and
dexterity of small
muscles (forks,
crayons, markers,
safety scissors,
adapted tools).

497CB19775054017B8ADA9978474EB0F.description:
Engage in activities
that require hand-eye
coordination (build
with manipulatives,
mold Play-Doh®, work
puzzles with smaller
pieces).

3E37B94B0E9542AC87E33BAD50BCB476.description:
Draw simple shapes
and figures (square for
block, circles).

14C505F3BFD84D15AF9A77B5536898F2.description:
Use tools that require
finger and hand control
(large paintbrush,
measuring cups,
switches, shovel).

DF350E4E472748718EBF19E50BB72079.description:
Use hands and eyes
together with a
moderate degree of
control (complete
puzzles, thread beads
with large holes, use
shape sorters).

6BF603C4826F46D6925B56B94871B80B.description:
Use more complex,
refined hand
movements (stack a
few small blocks,
try to draw, turn pages
one at a time).

4ACE5B9099A04316A87AB74697D2F721.description:
Use simple tools
(spoon for feeding,
hammer with pegs,
crayon for scribbling),
however imperfectly.

A9D075A7D4C844BEB7635BEDF9D62039.description:
Use hands and eyes
together (put together
and take apart toys,
feed themselves
finger foods, fill
containers).

6965BA3D8B5F46138FBF07FFB721BF48.description:
Use hands to
manipulate objects
(stack two or three
large blocks, pick up
or roll a ball).

1C6AE2CA0A684604BD6E69AAC1BA072A.description:
Use a pincer grasp to
pick up an object with
finger and thumb.

1D36733A4F6B4F53A65B5E9B2DEAE145.description:
Transfer objects from
one hand to the other.

289CB8E158D149C8B9B691C31D872FD7.description:
Use both hands to
swipe at, reach for,
grasp, hold, shake,
and release objects.

499922215F3149C6B98D9A05FC071AEA.description:
Children develop small muscle control and hand-eye coordination to manipulate objects
and work with tools.

E94E72CB628741D386C7F2B5A936622C.description:
Show awareness of
own body in relation to other people and
objects while moving through space.

6508E6C817284E98BC8496F3DBF618CE.description:
Move quickly through
the environment and stop (run fast, pedal fast).

E23F21E668D148B0AE184319A842C53B.description:
Perform complex
movements smoothly
(skipping, balancing
on beams, hopping from one place to another).

935BBB31F47544C3AD7B08E79D0D7378.description:
Coordinate movement of upper and
lower body.

43117F0BF38C475DB777D77F8CE53A6C.description: Move in space with good coordination (running, hopping in place, galloping).

9BBE4F9CB32C49DCBE6A46A4278E5E72.description:
Demonstrate large muscle control
by throwing balls
accurately, sliding
down slides, pedaling riding toys, and using
assistive technology effectively.

BEA6DD56B8CA4DB9A996F46F9D77EF92.description:
Refine movements and show generally good coordination
(e.g., throwing and
catching).

E6E0D09D38184F478D451F2C845B019D.description:
Demonstrate strength and balance
by managing uneven surfaces such as hills, ramps, and
steps.

41A9A16A25F641C7A8D67C2006F81F5C.description:
Perform actions smoothly with balance, strength, and coordination (dance,
bend over to pick up a toy, reach up high on a shelf, walk up and
down steps).

0AD31902F1994A549F86E5E15D0D89E8.description:
Use familiar objects
that encourage large
motor movements
(riding toys, crawl tubes, large ball in
basket, slide).

DAFCD2ACE0194311951BF642E1145E8E.description:
Move through the
world with a variety of movements and with increasing
independence
(run, jump, pedal).

FD6FDCFAC99645C6A707CD1BCD8CB6AF.description:
Move arms and legs to complete a
task (kick, jump, step, pedal, push away).

A058F2C3F1CD4369806C2703A911060B.description: Move through the world with more independence (crawl, cruise, walk, run, use therapeutic walker).

8E3FA1BCFE2445B0B95444E22B88CCF3.description:
Move arms and legs together to climb,
push, and pull (push a stroller, use riding toys, crawl up steps).

FE318D9036D0432D8D225FA9D6374F8D.description:
Develop strength, balance, and coordination by repeating movements (pull up and sit down;
bend and straighten,
squat to pick
something up from the floor).

9B0B1F8BEE694EEC832E993BC9DA660F.description:
Move from place to place as their abilities
allow (squirm, roll,
scoot, crawl, cruise, or walk).

F9D04DAF9B414EED9B3B271F865F0DBC.description:
Move in and out of various positions by
rolling, pushing up,
and pulling to stand.

ECFEBA7A35264EF096AE4355F5704647.description:
Develop upright
posture when sitting
and standing.

70F94A3E10074BC796AD66FA402CE34F.description: Gain control of arm and leg movements.

F0E041B28C7242BAA4C2E9699A62C726.description:
Children develop the large muscle control and abilities needed to move through and
explore their environment.

1CBD0D2170A64DC0960C5A10D7B25D43.description:
Independently start
and participate in
sleep routines most of
the time.

9045CECA7B9E45048B071151ECA4BA10.description:
Communicate ways
sleep keeps us healthy
and makes us feel
good.

D40BE958194549878C35FA40279EBABE.description:
With increasing
independence, start
and participate in
sleep routines.

C36CDAC22A8141C88060CB52305C6025.description:
Recognize and
communicate signs of
being tired.

E6A240BC2BED4CFDA76C2B445BA9D952.description:
Learning to fall
asleep on their own.

DE257374DC454C11948255CBA6376C3E.description:
With guidance,
participate in sleep
routines (wash hands
after lunch, get blanket,
lie down on bed or
mat).

67B08EF0259048408BED2017DDF5878F.description:
Use language about
sleep (say, “Time for
bed,” after clearing
lunch things; give sign
for sleep).

C17E605483AC42E6B10801BE7CD1E53E.description:
Use simple sounds,
gestures, or words to
show they are tired
(say, “Night, night.”).

B297A30E415B4B89AABCF5CEFFE96EE6.description:
Cooperate with
sleep routines
(choose a book,
get preferred sleep
toy).

897CE9568D654BB8A937A4F6F5EBC958.description:
Develop a personal
sleep routine or
pattern.

400E1D45DAF849FE8439536DA26AEE6F.description:
Settle down and fall
asleep after a routine
that includes a familiar
series of events.

09A2632D285E492A9B8885BB333F18C0.description:
Sleep for longer
periods at a time
(more at night, and
less during the day).

566C19C816AA4C9C852CB09880E98987.description:
Transition
independently
from active to quiet
activities most of the
time.

8C734355746B4B30A8B8FBFAD6534C2B.description:
Participate in
structured and
unstructured motor
activities that build
strength, speed,
flexibility, and
coordination (red light,
green light; chase; free
play).

3E065C0FD7DB4F1F9EC174CA4E5518D2.description:
Communicate ways
physical activity keeps
us healthy and makes
us feel good.

4086886E496F478DA9AAE3BE46F5DC5F.description:
Develop strength and
stamina by spending
extended periods of
time engaged in active
physical play indoors
and out.

A8F84FEE887F461CB17F467DD5360E28.description:
Transition from
active to quiet
activities with limited
guidance and support.

1FE86124375C46D2864825D83BA60322.description:
Participate in simple
games and other
structured motor
activities that enhance
physical fitness (songs
with movement,
throwing and
catching).

EDE7D713BE7E43448E8F2A9B30FFCD66.description:
Choose a variety
of structured and
unstructured physical
activities indoors and
outdoors.

2637C6316D734FEBBCC12F493A859C65.description:
Develop strength and stamina by spending moderate periods of
time engaged in active
physical play indoors
and out.

A9339A103A034DADAD7C6DD7907403B7.description:
With guidance and
support, transition from
active to quiet
activities.

955DB3BDA1744C4AA962C1B2F75BE9D7.description:
Show satisfaction
with new active skills
and strengths (ask
others to watch them,
say, “I’m big and
strong!”).

5F1CA6887E8E45A6BD1BB8C6B41C1D10.description:
Develop strength and stamina by spending moderate periods of time engaged in active
physical play indoors
and out.

ED2FAFFD878C4DD39ACABBF39487CAC9.description:
Develop strength
and stamina as they
use large muscles
and participate in
physical activity for
longer periods of
time.

912EEE5D261641FF87A9B747359A0BDA.description:
Engage in regular
and sustained
movement (push toys
around play yard, go
up and down slide
over and over).

77BC68F822414A69A3BEA93775ADDEA2.description:
Anticipate and ask
for outdoor play (point
at door and say,
“Out!”, resist coming
indoors).

DA35C6E75B18498AA57D4C126BD9147D.description:
Show they enjoy
active play and seek
to be physically active
(choose to play often
on climber, laugh and
squeal while moving).

ED34F74E4E0B41689DEE5BA35E4E1A71.description:
Develop strength by
continuing movements
over short
periods of time.

0A0989FA5F9049DE96C987513B7D4938.description:
Move their bodies to
explore the indoor and
outdoor environment.

4A77DD4C46634A319D3CA8905B831DA0.description:
Engage in physically
active movements
(spending time on their
tummy, repeating
actions, kicking,
waving arms, rolling
over).

C8FACBBADC014A6099F92AEC6E0C914D.description: Children engage in and sustain various forms of physical play indoors and out.

6540138310BE4CAC9BD793783353C283.description:
Name foods and
beverages that help to
build healthy bodies.

F4E33856248340AF8EC0559B2F165E08.description:
Talk about variety
and amount of foods
needed to be healthy
(can identify what is
missing from their
meal).

BEAC34C9B61F495AAA8FD4F2873538DE.description:
Given a selection of
familiar foods, identify
which foods are
nutritious and which
are not.

7E4C9892D3554DA99B16ABB60502CBA8.description:
Communicate that
some foods are
good for them (fruits,
vegetables, milk) and
some are not healthy
(potato chips, soda).

F8A89E3E05504890B1410AF07E240009.description:
Notice and talk about
food preferences,
textures, temperatures,
and tastes (crunchy
crackers, warm
soup, sweet apples).

5F34C010656D4B508F9C6C006AD50216.description:
Eat foods depending
on their appetite and
personal preference
(make food choices
at a meal, leave
unwanted food on
plate, ask for seconds
of favorite food).

4A75AC07890647A8B43A88C65CCF3F37.description:
Feed themselves
using utensils and
hands.

0DA5279FD218424795EC09876A93F836.description:
Eat a variety of
small pieces of ageappropriate table
foods.

9F2E973F7FE843C69863D4A037300A59.description:
Eat enough to meet
nutritional needs,
even when the
amount or type of
food varies over time
(eat a lot at one meal
and little at the next,
show interest in many
foods but no interest
in others).

7A8D603E74D140C385F7D856BABE4B1E.description:
Ask for or accept
food when hungry.

6A3ADE15C8AC40AEA9927E2236243EDD.description:
Feed themselves
with some assistance
(may use hands,
spoons, or cups with
or without lids).

367DB4B2880940B98C3DDE0DEC3AD008.description:
Eat different kinds of
food such as liquids,
pureed or soft foods,
and finely chopped
food.

E3468601718547838FA47F0DA8917FF3.description:
Respond to different
textures of food in their
mouth (wait for the next
bite, spit out food, turn
head away).

B54BC17ED2354446B154387E821F1BD6.description:
Indicate foods they like
and do not like.

928862136F11463F85B2005DA6EB34B5.description:
Show hunger or
fullness using actions,
sounds, or words (cry
or search for food, turn
away when full).

74EAF835359C43AEBAC30D0A56049DFC.description:
Help with feeding
themselves (eat finger
foods, hold bottle).

document.title: South Carolina Early Learning Standards

AA53FFA7E145422EB515C2B4F4B20477.description: Use some conventional letters in their writing.

45045BF4B186484AAC10A2555E64BB83.description:
Imitate adult writing
conventions that they have
observed (write groups of
letter-like forms separated
by spaces, try to write on
a line, press Enter key on
computer after typing a series
of “words”).

2666AA9DEC04454C8094D40C4D9FDD22.description:
Use a variety of writing tools
and materials with increasing
precision.

AA942DB97988474AA5D10871412AFD4A.description:
Play with writing letters and make
letter-like forms.

6778BF43B96F400C9B50E3D518618FAF.description:
Make marks they call “writing”
that look different from drawings (vertical series of marks for a
“grocery list,” horizontal line of
marks for a “story”).

860D0BB622BF422E9612CEAD60059334.description:
Use a variety of writing tools and
materials with purpose and control
(pencils, chalk, markers, crayons, paintbrushes, finger paint,
computers).

D58F978214A149A98D203BC16A51C2FC.description:
Transition from
holding a crayon or
marker in their fist to holding it between
thumb and forefinger.

9E9A96CDDE9F4869BD34990013EA94C0.description:
Scribble and/or
imitate an adult’s marks with markers, crayons,
paints, etc.

907E34674550430AA1B044D51AB4588D.description:
Explore a variety of
tools that can be used
for writing.

286692937C1640549EDD5ED9BD9630D7.description:
Dot or scribble
with crayons, may
progress to
vertical lines.

BAB454CB134E4671952BEBAF89D50732.description:
Hold marker or
crayon with their
fist.

0F66C27B30264B638A2C5617B27E0A59.description: Children use writing skills and conventions.

09C4C5A351A14F5E9B36C12B03EAE372.description:
Try to connect the sounds in
a spoken word with letters in
the written word (write “M” and
say, “This is Mommy.”).

DC58C4615B2C41B184EF659644BA52B1.description:
Use known letters and approximations of letters to write
their own name and some
familiar words.

9A12DDBF1D364EFFA9F725FF720F86D4.description:
Show they know that written
words are made up of particular
letters (point to the first letter
of their own name, find the first
letter of their own name in a list of
letters).

226CFBA720F3439F9514E28F846B670F.description:
Distinguish letters from different
kinds of drawings/graphics.

92BAECAFA27E48FC98D4D1559EEA7C27.description:
Begin to use letters and
approximations of letters to write
their name.

EDA612815C034221BE079DEA655B7A66.description: Children use knowledge of letters in their attempts to write.

87021B0A94D5442683656BC6850BA62A.description:
Engage in discussions regarding
different purposes (enjoyment,
information) and forms of writing
(narrative, informational, and
opinion).

76A1F779351C4139AC79BB700BAFAA98.description:
Independently engage in writing
behaviors for various purposes
(e.g., write symbols or letters for
names, use materials at writing
center, write lists with symbols/
letters in pretend play, write
messages that include letters or
symbols).

E87F40777EBB4376888051EE4716C272.description:
Communicate their thoughts for
an adult to write.

D0288162DFC94DCCBBA3234459930DFF.description:
Incorporate representations of
signs, logos, or other commonly
used symbols into their drawing
or writing to communicate the
messages that they convey.

C536C5BA9F704ECE93B82BF643218C69.description:
Represent thoughts and ideas in
drawings and by writing letters or
letter-like forms.

04F07FF521A547FBA674682532159217.description:
Engage in writing
behaviors that imitate
real-life situations
(e.g., make marks to
take food order during
pretend restaurant play).

14235C5D134F4FC4B3C64F8FFEBA8F06.description:
With prompting and
support, communicate
their thoughts for an
adult to write.

3471F633882E4A13B4F894DE1DD41480.description:
Represent thoughts
and ideas through
marks, scribbles,
drawings, and paintings
(draw a picture of
something they did
during the day, indicate
what they want for lunch
with a mark under the
picture of the food they
want).

434D446D5EE14CAC93DB5C28F08C659C.description:
Pretend to write in
ways that mimic adult
writing (e.g., scribble
on paper while sitting
with caregiver who is
writing, hold phone to
ear and make marks
with pencil).

B65B091E5D5E47E58E20FECCF34F16B9.description:
Make marks,
scribble, and paint
(e.g., cover easel
paper with big
crayon or paint marks,
make marks with
marker or crayon).

0373773CF314479A95C8C44DCD368A76.description:
Children use writing and other symbols to record information and communicate for a
variety of purposes.

32440D6902E941769192A0EE6653975E.description:
Associate sounds with
the letters at the beginning
of some words, such as
awareness that two words
begin with the same letter
and the same sound.

4D84E8E9968947D7B15633354FAF9534.description:
Make some sound-to-letter
matches, using letter name
knowledge (notice the letter
B with picture of ball and
say, “Ball”; say, “A-a-apple.”).

9BEBC269628A438A995F3252780DD5B6.description:
Recognize and name
many letters of the alphabet,
especially those in their own
name and in the names of
others who are important to
them.

F76AE9F45D6F43C38AD3063C5DFF2504.description:
Show they know that letters
function to represent sounds
in spoken words.

E8D1D856F5444877A3733C6AA941D19A.description: Demonstrate an interest in learning the alphabet.

8C5C5849C38D45C5A3A623610340FE11.description:
Recognize and name
some letters of the
alphabet, especially
those in their own
name.

50F2B99BA01A425494A8BDCD0824F190.description:
Recognize letters
of the alphabet as a
special category of
print, different from
pictures, shapes, and
numerals.

4C4AD8E75C4141EC842DFF9F0E22FEB1.description: Demonstrate an interest in learning the alphabet.

91AE638B9F9D46C4BB0D0321A3DFC598.description:
Demonstrate an
interest in letters by
asking about and/or
naming some of them.

D1E006B65874472D93339DF3E2EE0697.description: Children begin to develop knowledge of the alphabet and the alphabetic principle.

F8C5721ED16D48DDA9C0BD5532191A9F.description:
Associate sounds with
specific words, such as
awareness that different
words begin with the same
sound.

38123E0FE1294D68B5E16C9B8094D3B9.description:
Play with the sounds of
language, identify a variety
of rhymes, create some
rhymes, and recognize the
first sounds in some words.

C7376DBB2FC74943BC2CA377F08065AA.description:
Repeat a variety of
rhythmic patterns in poems
and songs using words,
clapping, marching, and/
or instruments to repeat the
rhythm or beat syllables.

F2A461C589F344BA8D1DF2D8BDF27C5C.description:
Enjoy rhymes and wordplay
with songs, poems, and
books and sometimes add
their own variations.

1B84F0684BCE463D8F3C080F0A6AC83B.description:
Distinguish between similar
sounding words (e.g. tree
and three).

9966C8B667C641C3BBA459009A009E76.description:
Play with the
sounds of language
and begin to identify
rhymes (make up
silly-sounding words,
repeat rhyming
words).

9D08FC17888B4926B56DE51BA549CE70.description:
Repeat rhythmic
patterns in poems and
songs using words,
clapping, marching,
and/or using
instruments.

E54193980B734298BFFEE11CF7BA3A6F.description:
Participate in
experiences with
songs, poems, and
books that have
rhyme and wordplay,
and learn words well
enough to complete
refrains and fill in
missing words and
sounds.

75CA3AF5BE404581894ACB857B476CAD.description:
Participate in
experiences using
rhythmic patterns
in poems and songs
using words, clapping,
marching, and/or using
instruments.

2E48E5F66EC6416CB5D04E748B970E12.description:
Notice sounds that
are the same and
different.

7F7EB282D264413A9D99098FD3B1394F.description:
Focus on and enjoy
playing with repetitive
sounds, words,
rhymes, and gestures.

EC0AFBC13C8747568CF4D278B6D9118C.description:
Imitate and
take turns with
caregivers making
different sounds.

72C64EC43C0C4D48A96EF492EEA6098F.description:
Discuss storybooks by responding
to questions about the beginning,
middle, and end of the story.

704609CBCDBD454C83CF2311F60552CA.description:
Discuss storybooks by responding
to questions about what is
happening and predicting what will
happen next.

FB58940193F34EB1920ACABEF01A5AB7.description:
Ask more focused and detailed
questions about a story or the
information in a book.

A97C280DA030472BA5E0511E9AA17094.description:
Relate personal experiences to
an increasing variety of events
described in familiar and new
books.

EBE0AE7F2A5F4286A3C830097745DB69.description:
Use knowledge of the world to
make sense of more challenging
texts.

CD25093DEA7D426FA9D6EE5A81DA5829.description:
Use informational texts and
other media to learn about the
world, and infer from illustrations,
ask questions and talk about the
information.

20F511A571614F59BF932AE227BAF63D.description:
Imitate the special language in
storybooks and story dialogue with
accuracy and detail.

D21F0C99AA50406F80C2B6CB216DCB2F.description:
With prompting and support,
discuss storybooks by responding
to questions about what is
happening and predicting what will
happen next.

07D299D26FE54597B34E4518BD0DEB0F.description:
Ask questions about a story or
the information in a book.

40601233CD4242CFA0E1E4508391E875.description:
Relate personal experiences to
events described in familiar books,
with prompting and support.

B1C433890A0C481AB39ECDFCF466FE79.description:
Use their knowledge of the world
(what things are, how things work)
to make sense of stories and
informational texts.

B1F80EFCA201435B8079D09C11282A03.description:
With prompting and support,
use books and other media that
communicate information to learn
about the world by looking at
pictures, asking questions, and
talking about the information.

6A015A29B27748ACADC19DA0F53D574B.description:
Imitate the special language in
storybooks and story dialogue with
some accuracy and detail.

D71BE46DC24B46E9BFFC6538B3077656.description:
Imitate the special
language in storybooks
and story dialogue
(repetitive language
patterns, sound effects,
and words from familiar
stories).

2AEFDA9713D84F549727E9A468CB1D87.description:
Begin to relate personal
experiences to events
described in familiar
books.

CD1AB192DFA046D39D6BAD2A86CC334B.description:
Pretend to read familiar
books from memory;
repeat familiar phrases
while looking at a book.

28C214ED32EB4D43AAC5CE7279111961.description:
Chime in on a repeated
line in a book while being
read to by an adult.

F16C708630554764B242E376B55C10A4.description:
Make appropriate
sounds when looking at
pictures (say, “Quack,
quack” when looking
at a duck, “Vrrrrooom”
when looking at a car).

4A4621202249434D8AB6E540E182BB59.description:
Allow entire short
book to be “read” with
willingness to look at
most pages.

62FB5FB74D2B439481664BE1B53E1804.description:
Listen to and repeat
parts of simple and
repetitive books, stories,
songs, and finger plays.

E9F6CA963747488AAB0FF75AE1E0881D.description: Children comprehend and use information presented in books and other print media.

5A55CE63EF1541BCB46A0650627272D8.description:
Identify their name and the names
of some friends when they see them
in print.

8DDF384F036040559F7A9D565F1A1A35.description:
Demonstrate an understanding
of some basic print conventions
(the concept of what a letter is, the
concept of words, directionality of
print).

45BB927549194EC9AFD0DFC5A3385A70.description:
With prompting and support, run
their finger under or over print as
they pretend to read text.

4C8B5C8458964A00B2B6DFBE3C86DEA8.description:
Recognize print and symbols used
to organize classroom activities
and show understanding of their
meaning (put toys in box with
correct symbol and name; check
sign-up sheet for popular activity;
check schedule to learn next
activity).

C8BB1CFF49354FD6B6E723F5547AB3ED.description:
Recognize print in different forms
for a variety of functions (writing a
message to friend, pointing to print
and saying, “Those words tell the
story,” or reading familiar signs in
the environment).

F4CF8D28B4FF4D7BB8D660730E72C9B4.description:
Hold a book upright while turning
pages one by one from front to
back.

5D4EB02488664DB4A5DAB6A5C37D0A79.description:
Demonstrate an
understanding that
print and symbols can
tell people what to do
(to organize classroom
activities—where to store
things, when they will
have a turn).

CBF6C65FFD1146048E241E5D6A29F693.description:
With prompting and
support, recognize print
occurs in different forms
and is used for a variety
of functions (sign naming
block structure, “message”
on card for family
member).

D939EE0B566D4B7EB500BF2312E6534D.description:
Hold a book upright
while turning pages one
by one front to back, but
not always in order.

771A03CF2DD647D99560A8C2906EABEC.description:
Demonstrate an
understanding of
realistic symbols such as
photographs, and later,
abstract symbols such as
signs and environmental
print (know which pictures
stand for which activities
on a daily schedule; say,
“That means light” when
looking at a symbol of a
light bulb located over the
light switch).

45A140419791480EB188F674EE3E2B54.description:
Demonstrate
understanding of the
need for and the uses of
print (pretend to read a
“grocery list” during play;
say, “I want chicken” when
looking at a menu).

041A7E71EF8E46E18946579524403C16.description:
Hold a book upright, turn
some pages front to back
(but not always in the right
order), close book, and
say, “done” or “the end.”

CC0858CD2F094C708429B8CD4F4A2FE4.description:
Identify some
environmental print and
logos (favorite cereal
box, a sign for a familiar
store).

6FE94CE26E844A36A760AD85AC9087F2.description:
Turn pages (but not
always in the right
order); point to and
label pictures in books;
sometimes treat
pictures as real (licking
a picture of ice cream,
rubbing “fur” of a cat in
a book).

03E6F94670E94736BAD8A190E706026A.description:
Look at pictures
while cuddling
with caregiver.

4000649F85AF48118CDC900B54C33EFF.description:
Explore books
and paper by tasting,
mouthing, crumpling,
banging, and
patting.

57BAEDA9372949D6B92A59C0BE41577F.description: Children develop book knowledge and print awareness.

7FA58E2D5CCD4EA5AC2E8C86E01A90D0.description:
Listen to and
discuss increasingly
complex storybooks,
information books, and
poetry.

0B3E810055834B01BD21741C2B321955.description:
Use and share books
and print in their play.

0D00905E98DF464FB8178CFF393FBF8D.description:
Engage in
reading behaviors
independently with
increased focus for
longer periods of time.

F8356A976F014BE5A74131E864EE3E13.description:
Listen to and discuss
storybooks, simple
information books,
and poetry.

CFA0DA8AC6A147158DFA798A73C18BA2.description:
Show an interest
in books, other print,
and reading related
activities.

81C8C32FD48A45E9816F338101FD5354.description:
Engage in reading
behaviors
independently
(choose books, turn
pages but not always
in order, tell the story).

1C85D43EBCC94DC498A880A15A7C6211.description:
Listen for short
periods of time to
storybooks,
informational books,
stories, poetry, songs,
and finger plays.

4090CC11AAB64A18A7E778E03B7B8B51.description:
Engage in reading
behaviors
independently
(choose books, turn
 pages but not always
in order, tell the story).

E8E47E6F99CB47219E6DD6753D2BD9A4.description:
Carry books around,
“name” them, and
select books for
adults to read out
loud.

7C689069AB6642CDBE9CAB626B8B59D0.description:
Listen to simple
and repetitive books,
stories, and songs for
a brief time.

7FB6A06889744ED8A4691456D36E0923.description:
Show interest in
books (e.g., tactile
and picture books).

2563DB5938EA44A8BBAB16598A834485.description:
Engage in
reading behaviors
independently
(choose books, turn
pages but not always
in order, tell the
story).

A685136641F142AE852C279CB59B549F.description:
Listen to simple and
repetitive books,
stories, and songs.

5E5C376529EC4698A0856342AC0A0F8D.description:
Look at pictures of
faces and simple
objects.

38A574D75E394EE0A5166654655BADB1.description:
Pat and chew on
tactile books.

22DF495FA68E4926AB6DD521844DD8F5.description: Children develop interest in books and motivation to read.

7C1B007885814937BE31937789C300C2.description:
Distinguish between
real and made up
words.

55BAA2403E4B449AA112E3CF0BDDD57A.description:
Infer the meaning of
different kinds of new
words from the context
in which they are used
(for example, hear
“sandals” and “boots”
used to describe two
pairs of shoes, and
infer that the unfamiliar
shoes must be sandals
because they know that
the other pair of shoes
are boots).

48ACB00665554866834FD265D3DBD9EF.description:
Use a growing
vocabulary that
includes many kinds of
words to express ideas
clearly.

F3E670AD98BC4305942564D9AE8A039E.description:
Repeat familiar
songs, chants, or
rhymes.

5B0C1692DC6941FC92C6518A7151711D.description:
Use many kinds
of cues in the
environment to figure
out what words mean.

572C040B954541269932CBE21FB3BD40.description:
Make up names
for things using
words they know
(e.g., dog doctor for
veterinarian).

BB8FA6397AF34966BC7C15BFA48FFCFB.description:
Use more than one
word for the same
object and use words
for parts of objects
(e.g., dog, beagle,
Rover; arm, leg).

DDC8CF81C26B46EEA55C26C129F7323D.description:
Repeat familiar
songs, chants, or
rhymes.

08ECE823BBA34F24964A2D11F82B8DF0.description:
Use proper nouns
for people and things.

EDF7C39DC85547FA9C8C6313A098586B.description:
Show they
understand many new
vocabulary words and
a variety of concepts
(big and little, in and
out).

4CA865FD2C5C4B679F6F601972A87AE6.description:
Participate in or
repeat familiar songs,
chants, or rhymes.

229141C8AF3F46E3BF7FFBDF91CB14B2.description:
Use new words each
day and have a word
for almost all familiar
people, objects,
actions, and conditions
(hot, rainy, sleepy).

297EB2C946194732BCD266191A957160.description:
Use several words
to make requests
(e.g., “done,” “wannit,”
“please”) as well as to
label people and
objects.

8E6FA8D6DFE148B4BCC17B1F68A8FC5E.description:
Respond to simple
words and phrases
that they hear often.

18B71F77BCBA4005A783F3613B461324.description:
Imitate parts of
familiar songs,
chants, or rhymes.

EEBC83E9FECA40159CBCDA13F7C4F970.description:
Show steady
increase in words
used (e.g., name
family members and
familiar objects).

51D97883179D4AC9A9FC80DE87150783.description:
Recognize spoken
or signed words for
common items.

1B4D925F2DFD4A618F9E29769571BD94.description:
Make specific
sounds, facial
expressions, and/or
gestures for certain
people and objects.

334564544DAC49E78F3B8360EB6E7BA1.description: Children respond to and use a growing vocabulary.

D8CC4F493562407E9BD31A47FC7AD5E2.description:
Speak in full
sentences that are
grammatically correct
most of the time.

386C3313AB5D47E08CA98CDAD298C978.description:
Make grammatical
errors that follow
language rules (say,
“mouses” instead of
“mice”).

46B00E0790CE4838A9F99A193F5A825D.description:
Communicate in
longer sentences
and use more
conventional
grammar in their
home language
(plurals, tenses,
prepositions).

4544B4EFEFF540E8841862CAD3301FCA.description:
Communicate in short
sentences that follow
the word order of their
home language.

5993F7FD097046C786C75783BAB0A600.description:
Use a few words to
communicate (make
requests and ask
questions).

C3E3B5DBEBFE431381C968B6518A7369.description:
“Jabber” and put
together vocalizations
in a way that sounds
similar to the rhythm
and flow of their home
language.

4B862CDEA2C14822B266CDA0627A49EB.description:
“Jabber” and pretend
to talk using many
sounds or signs
from the languages
used around them to
communicate.

4BBA5DD4700D40E49259C3DDE9A38572.description:
Make different
sounds for different
purposes (whimper
when wet, cry loudly
when hungry).

D41CB622437C4D89AC2F93046F4DEF13.description: Children use most grammatical constructions of their home language well.

6853DDB1609B4560A43E8438C097A354.description:
Describe experiences
and create and/or
retell longer narratives.

8C1090AC61A54051970A27CE8B9D6B18.description:
Describe
experiences and
create or retell short
narratives.

55B69184963544EDB8D3A04EEBA323A5.description:
Talk to themselves
and others about what they are “working on,” what they are doing, routines, and events
of the day.

68AEF76924A74AFDB301FBDEB2295B5C.description:
Use dramatic play to
act out familiar scenes
and events and imitate
familiar people.

66348E5450A84A5EA88709F5BDF1F70D.description:
Talk to themselves
and others about what they are “working on,” what they are doing, routines, and events of
the day.

57FED074A34842EBAF35C9C8DA726D62.description:
Act out familiar
scenes and events,
and imitate familiar
people.

1D048FA8AB874BE7BEBD9E7AAB47BB95.description: Children describe familiar people, places, things, and events.

9FB6DE0C9211473186FB22B097D9946B.description:
Express ideas in more
than one way.

444EE00188A742CC819D009BA3ACB6B0.description:
State point of view, likes
and dislikes.

CAC888635908425F8B9BBA7C1082B11C.description:
Speak clearly enough
to be understood by most
people.

B4A679DD5CB141469FAF0C995E646035.description:
Adapt their
communication to meet
social expectations
(speak quietly in library,
speak politely to older
relative).

5058991155F94A8E912795CFA51ABF3D.description:
Use language and
nonverbal cues to
communicate thoughts,
beliefs, feelings, and
intentions.

9DBC4C54A8644BC3B905477B3A14CA2D.description:
Speak clearly enough to be understood by familiar
adults and children.

B9DA57EE36FE4BF899ECBD99330DBA85.description:
Communicate messages with expression, tone, and inflection appropriate
to the situation.

9B5880B26BA746549C1A8BF8BA6E8330.description:
Use speech that is understood most of the
time by familiar listeners.

CD7ADEB617B945C782C337EEB9349B5A.description: Communicate messages with expression, tone, and inflection.

0D1BC699901446149AB22A3267FB066A.description:
Use non-verbal
gestures to express
ideas and feelings.

4C9998C922E8452C8143ED90563BFDCF.description:
Expect others to
understand them and
show frustration, often
through their
behavior, if not
understood.

5BD46F6181E941F486368BED95F15509.description:
Communicate
through facial
expressions, sounds,
and body movements.

7FF3668136794C3E8EFADC806F8147B1.description:
“Babble” and pretend
to talk using many
sounds or signs from
the languages used
around them.

CB3D520D61A7482F9EEEF370E17F7116.description:
Make different
sounds for different
purposes (whimper
when wet, cry loudly
when hungry).

329F9DF94EEB473F8FBA66E6FB929D11.description:
Repeat actions to
communicate (lift arms
to be picked up, point
at desired toys).

3998F87DE60E4A39B3A1D5BE1DFF0C6E.description: Children communicate thoughts, feelings, and ideas clearly.

9C2FAF326D884463A255457CE4F02DF7.description:
Ask specific
questions to learn
more about their
world, understand
tasks, and solve
problems.

5D5F6689E709452A90012BBAE66658D4.description:
Answer more
complex questions
with an explanation
(“I didn’t like camping
out because it rained.”
“Emily is my friend
because she’s nice to
me”).

23CD041A28A44F5EB9FDA87E459916AC.description:
Use sentences
or questions to ask for things (people, actions, objects, pets) or gain information.

B43B0BDEDA1A432DA449372DCB6B720D.description: Answer longer questions using more detail.

E5647885F56D4EBEAAC740A8369663F8.description:
Use simple sentences or questions to ask for things (e.g., people, actions, objects, pets) or gain
information.

4C8847045559496E85916D2126479EA2.description: Answer simple questions (“What is she doing?” “What happened to the bear in the story?”).

36E495CC7E7C4D23BFF5643CBAB5BCF9.description:
Respond to simple
statements and
questions about
pictures, play,
people, and things
that are happening.

2E64B0629CFC4DF2A7887451A1BDDB66.description:
Children ask and answer questions in order to seek help, get information, or clarify
something that is not understood.

D77E1D4EE1BE4E62A4318210AAC04929.description:
Show an appreciation
for and can use humor
appropriately.

EE2B9CD905C04AF18B4A955973001C5B.description:
Participate in a group
discussion, making comments
and asking questions related
to the topic.

B39A8EF7CC984C7E93DC9700B8EE2ED8.description:
Initiate and participate
in conversations related
to interests of their own
or the persons they are
communicating with.

13C6C7ABB20D458DAA0593FCAE145F3D.description:
Initiate and carry on
conversations that involve
multiple back and forth
communications or turns
between the persons involved
in the conversation.

2A195447260D4984BAC884191F5C019D.description:
Express an understanding
that people communicate
in many ways (gestures,
facial expressions, multiple
spoken languages, sign
language, and augmentative
communication).

90631862381A4096A0205C6EFA58FF0E.description:
With prompting and
support, make
comments and ask
questions related
to the topic of
discussion.

77E63F255735486B9964257E1B8B43BA.description:
Initiate and carry on
conversations, and
ask questions about
things that interest
them.

7946930E69A3400CB64A9806636643BE.description:
Demonstrate an
understanding that
people communicate
in many ways
(gestures, facial
expressions, multiple
spoken languages,
sign language,
augmentative
communication).

CE6EB5B7FD3548DD929A400148483E86.description:
Ask questions or use
verbal or nonverbal
cues to initiate
communication with
another child or adult.

9018661AD70F4DB9BD8E56BC49160B64.description:
Engage in short
dialogues of a few
turns.

4F2643678E7D4DCD8ECACB5587CEC50A.description:
Use movement or
behavior to initiate
interaction with
another person.

A69F82BC0BE2425CA564D8F6BF830C3D.description:
Respond to and
initiate dialogue with
another person.

850182278D744E5A8B003256A788B627.description:
Establish joint
attention by looking
at an object, at their
caregiver, and back at
the object.

7E3FFC4D981849E1A3599BEEC56D99A2.description:
Engage in turn-taking
during social and
vocal play with adults
and other children
(babbling, imitating
facial expressions,
repeating sounds from
languages they hear).

DA8FDD967F73448DBDD1A851AD9A4461.description:
Pay brief attention to
the same object the
caregiver is looking at.

86BC82518DDE4FD48741DC7BF1F71B36.description:
Respond differently
to facial expressions
and tones of voice.

6D82641600254F5CA590E476E3E8EE1D.description: Children participate in conversations with peers and adults.

13494A37D1434CB3B501BBC0959273B6.description:
Respond to requests
for information or
action.

BAFD308C1F6642C094761258870C2559.description:
Show understanding
of increasingly
complex sentences.

DADEC46146A14426B87FE51ADFC4C4A1.description:
Follow simple
multistep directions
with visual cues, if
needed.

8842F0BD013A472694F215563419E6FE.description:
With prompting and
support, respond to
requests for
information or action.

385B46F554134951AC8B2B62A9960432.description:
Show understanding
of increasingly
complex sentences.

D0F8A27224E346C8B16D2AE05F11A25D.description:
Follow two-step
directions with visual
cues if needed (“Pick
up the paper and put it
in the trash.” “Get your
cup and put it on the
table.”).

1898B8B5EACB49919C62AF08DFFBF06E.description:
Respond
appropriately to
gestures, facial
expressions, tone of
voice, and some words
that show emotions.

64183CED30644E2DBA33DFFC9F547859.description:
Respond when others
talk to them, using a
larger variety of words
or signs.

A85207F1A0E2478695895F4CCAE41EA2.description:
Follow simple
directions and/or
visual cues (“Put
your pillow on the
mat.” “Please sit by
me.”).

9C3BEE7EEF16408881AB4BF0B376C6BF.description:
Respond
appropriately to
gestures, facial
expressions, tone
of voice, and some
words that show
emotions.

E28BB5CA05D44FE5B063032470819F04.description:
Respond to others
by using words or
signs.

76C416C0F67F4A39BF1E3A19046EF53C.description:
Respond to simple
requests (“Come
here.”or “Do you want
more?”).

5C2D1B93F91343F7AD367A8654786AD0.description:
Respond to different
tones in speech
directed at them.

135BD6AA508641D3B06C6EBB84939465.description:
Show interest in
voices, and focus on
speech directed at
them.

6364AA5A65E24A939CFE59C45E449302.description:
Engage in individual
and reciprocal sound
exploration and play
(make “raspberries”
or other sounds with
someone).

document.title: South Carolina Early Learning Standards

748634ABBAC74DD1BE4801CB63C1D409.description:
Identify and describe strategies
used to complete increasingly difficult
puzzles (for example, when completing
a floor puzzle, working on the edges
first).

DADBCF94460E4A13B085916D0691D11C.description:
Begin to explain how a mathematical
problem was solved (“I saw that there
was always a blue flower after a red
flower so I knew to put a blue one
next.” “I counted four friends who didn’t
have crackers so I got four more.”).

C57E4EF2DBB5478A83C2CA9311A378F7.description:
Use drawing, writing, and
concrete materials to represent and
communicate a variety of mathematical
ideas (draw shapes to represent
pattern; stack different-colored blocks
to represent classmates’ answers to a
survey question).

757928D011AF461E8FC3A9C9C6E90D8B.description:
Seek answers to questions during
play and daily activities using an
increasing variety of mathematical
strategies (figure out how to balance
a block structure; to build a bridge; to
create a pattern with Legos®).

9B1B9F9868574C9DB6BBF7F2ED9A4F6F.description:
Develop and
consistently use
intentional strategies
when working with
knobbed puzzles and
similar materials.

CA5473CBD53F48318944F2A3CD6CE291.description:
Use drawing and
concrete materials
to represent and
communicate
mathematical ideas (draw
many circles to show
“lots of people,” put craft
sticks in a pile to show the
number of children who
want crackers for snack).

E687E3288032435C93513000F5A9239E.description:
Seek answers to
questions by using
mathematical thinking (i.e.
reasoning and problem
solving) during play and
daily activities (determine
who is taller by standing
next to classmate; find
two smaller blocks to
replace larger block).

6C76D119705D4A91A1CAA0D33D03C8C2.description: Children use mathematical thinking to solve problems in their everyday environment.

92B01251AE3E40888F9F30D1F0A189F5.description:
Recognize routines with time passing
throughout the day (identifying circle
time, snack time, outside play, etc.).

E7F62AB67EC34C5BA7B0E74859A719B8.description:
Describe the weather as hot or cold.
(Continue to engage in explorations
with temperature).

78D7FA4C3B7B48C0963EDBC5D4BF56B3.description:
Use simple measurement tools with
guidance and support to informally
measure objects (a ruler, measuring
cup, scale).

2128FCF5E53047BF9CDFB6DF54F17257.description:
Put a few objects in order by size,
length or weight (arrange a group of 3
blocks in order from the shortest to the
longest).

7A90FABD0EB44845860F2FE70E700F22.description:
Directly compare more than two
objects by size, length, or weight (“That
rock is heavier than these others; I
can’t lift it.” Look at three strings that
are different lengths and select the
longest string).

B2F80B78DB5141D6B4227091FC93B91C.description:
Use descriptive language for size,
length, or weight (short, tall, long,
heavy, big).

D67338715C764AE2A49FDC81B6D5C32F.description:
Recognize routines with time
passing throughout the day
(identifying circle time, snack
time, outside play, etc.).

631F23C895E34D8895EA141101994E88.description: Describe the weather as hot or cold. (Engage in explorations with temperature).

FFD5603D32CD4394BEFA65DA5A6BA424.description: Use simple measurement tools with guidance and support to informally measure objects (a ruler, measuring cup, scale).

3DAFCAC93C2F44F0BE4409A4DF2A9E0F.description: Compare the size or weight of two objects and identify which one is longer/taller/ heavier than the other (“That rock is heavier than this one. I can lift it.” “The snake is longer than the worm”).

B4330C415D314CC8BAAFF0392DF36FBB.description: Use descriptive language for size, length, or weight (short, tall, long, heavy, big).

8B4E7578730F4CDD87DF6DBEF99DC022.description: Engage in continued explorations with temperature.

F8FE1D44744C480BB0862616434F7CED.description:
Use size and amount words to label and compare objects, people, and collections
(big truck, a lot of crackers, little baby).

8854E27CA702472EA556334402E062BB.description:
Engage in
beginning
explorations with
temperature (quickly
touching cold and
warm items).

5F36D7A55C8546ED9A5EBF0E41F3180A.description:
Participate in
activities that
compare the size
and weight of
objects.

F29152A86CF749E4A53341FDFD33A85F.description:
Examine
objects of
different sizes by
exploring (touch,
pick up, and
move objects).

5D7C576E35D84BD7BEFC189CB13EF881.description:
Children demonstrate a beginning understanding of measurement (the idea of repeating the use of an object to
measure) and a beginning understanding of data analysis through comparing and interpreting data during play and other activities.

B5870D7071214FCAB2351F3F991C1701.description: Foundations of Measurement and Data Analysis

C1429AA410E74FD8ACED614D8596E100.description:
Name basic 2 and 3-dimensional
shapes (square, prism, circle,
sphere, triangle, pyramid,
hexagon), and describe their
characteristics using informal
descriptive and geometric
attributes (“That’s a triangle; it’s
pointy.” “It’s a circle because it’s
round.”).

6D1FAE0AA0FE478DAE324B720D80B5C8.description:
Identify basic 2- and
3-dimensional shapes (square,
circle, triangle) in the environment.

091DAD8B19704039BB7A4C358BF43986.description:
Use 2- and 3-dimensional shapes
to represent real world objects
(say, “We are building a castle
and we need a round block for
the tunnel.” “I glued a circle and
a square on my picture to make a
house.”).

FD7DE80ACD554DE8B424B01D775F1B81.description:
Consistently use a variety of
words for positions in space (in,
on, over, under, etc.), and follow
directions using these words.

A67EE9CE832D4EB4ACBB68920E2E865E.description:
Stack or line up blocks
that are the same
shape.

288B9E4582E64A82A8E06E809520A5B8.description:
Name or match a few
2- and 3-dimensional
shapes (circle, sphere,
square, triangle, cone)
and describe their
differences.

91596C0488694629A967242ABFE20B70.description:
Respond to and begin
to use words describing
positions (in, on, over,
under, etc.).

B316A042B7324707A63A6EF4E6447845.description:
Stack or line up blocks
that are the same shape.

F80861716F954B309A4459118BF412C2.description:
Name or match a few
2- and 3-dimensional
shapes (circle, square,
cylinder).

3DC1FD73FBAA47EA996D2A413DE77D2A.description:
Respond to and
begin to use words
describing positions (in,
on, over, under, etc.).

FD3A3A4923C240F4A65011DD01737D5B.description:
Put basic shapes
into a shape sorter
using trial and error.

662206C2F3474B01ADC8077425A4BF5C.description:
Explore space with
their bodies (fit self
into large box, crawl
under table, climb
over low walls).

3B03C40D33FF42239649C87A23EB3687.description:
Attempt to put
objects into other
objects (such as
putting pieces into
holes or other
spaces).

7865EE9C0A8949AA9AF5BFFEC3FC9A13.description:
Examine different
shapes by
exploring (banging
blocks on the floor,
rolling balls).

50F4BE43B5714357BF35052B487CBBA7.description:
Children begin to identify, describe, classify, and understand shape, size, direction, and
movement during play and other activities.

3FCFCA7904E94DE196762FE95113EFC0.description: Foundations for Geometry and Spatial Understanding

21EE704828764E8A80C27B4D4400A358.description:
Show beginning abilities to
create simple repeating patterns.

4F1957B540054A9DBEBDC00374DA432B.description:
Describe, duplicate and extend
simple repeating patterns (twopart patterns) using concrete
objects (look at a pattern of
beads and tell what bead comes
next in the pattern).

142B8B607722462E9743D94B81BFDD0C.description:
Sort a group of objects (0-10)
using one attribute (color, size,
shape, quantity) with increasing
accuracy (sort blocks by shape
and place like-shaped blocks on
the shelf; sort beads by color or
another attribute).

AA45E35E06754BCE8ED86B1BD3ECA3CB.description:
Recognize simple
repeating patterns
(AB type patterns) and
attempt to repeat or
extend them during play
(repeat a movement
pattern during a song,
extend a line of blocks
in alternating colors).

8823F071AC3C413B8B5C2E374DB53F8D.description:
Identify familiar objects
as the same or different.

8FE0AF8E361A4A9A936C278A8B05BC0B.description:
Sort familiar objects into categories (cars with cars, plates separated from cups;
rectangle blocks on one
shelf and square blocks
on another).

40208AEC5CBC4D35AE73B20F7F526A9D.description:
Can follow along
and imitate patterns of
sounds and movement
(for example, repeating
a chorus in a song
or clapping a simple
rhythm).

DCC7EF99898E44B590584339AFC37F0A.description:
Sort familiar objects into categories (cars with cars, plates separated from cups;
rectangle blocks on
one shelf and square
blocks on another).

57B29FB15DFE44D59311FC427F2D10F7.description:
Can follow along
and imitate patterns
of sounds and
movement (for
example, repeating
a chorus in a song
or clapping a simple
rhythm).

13FF8AB93C86429B8166A1B86527DFF7.description:
Show awareness of
different categories
during play (put balls
in a box and dolls
in a bed; give one
friend all the cars
and another friend
all of the trucks when
playing in the block
area).

922C041348154084BA7942C0DA2FE732.description:
Children demonstrate a beginning understanding of algebraic thinking by sorting,
describing, extending, and creating simple patterns during play and other activities.

90BF5D071F1D44F78432C4EF3ADBED1B.description:
Show different ways a set
of up to five objects can be
decomposed (broken apart) or
composed (put together) (e.g.,
5 objects can be broken into 2
and 3 objects and 2 and 3 can
be combined to make 5 objects).

EEB0C6BF71874F629FC8E6AADAA37A02.description:
Use observation and counting with increasing accuracy to
answer questions such as “How
many do we need?” and “How
many more do we need?” during
play and other daily activities
(count new children to see how
many more plates are needed
for snack; return extra drinks to
cooler at picnic to arrive at the
correct number).

85F71F250AD7434B858D1B4720BBC804.description:
Show they understand
that putting objects
together in a set will
make a bigger set, and
removing objects from a
set will make a smaller
set.

65E559F86EDD483392280C3B88C6F377.description:
Use observation and
counting (not always
correctly) to find out
how many things are
needed during play and
other daily activities
(figure out how many
spoons are needed
for snack, find enough
dolls so each person
has one when playing in
the dramatic play area).

F8952FB99BA64D3D8AA589A7A5F0F86F.description:
Use observation and
emerging counting
skills (1, 2, 3) during
play and other daily
activities.

3764F26206DC43B5A8053B2E9AD0A6FB.description:
Children demonstrate a beginning understanding of numbers and operations during play
and other activities.

18CCC44C748C4E4CBE0035213C86D61F.description:
Show understanding of first, next, and last during play
and daily activities (answer questions about who is first
and last to slide down the slide; say, “The engine is first,
and the caboose is last” when making a train).

512CA01B186140589445CE2B93243D65.description:
Tell what number comes next or what number came
before another number when counting 1-5.

E155C99EEE23425B9F377CE9C293FCE3.description:
State the number of objects in a small collection (1-5)
without counting (when a friend holds up two fingers, look at
her hand and say, “Two fingers” without counting).

80C3F45114364A43A4F0FBFC8A827659.description: Given a number 0-5, count out that many objects.

DB21909B1A4B4BBFACAD548EFEC155D8.description:
Recognize that objects can be counted as part of
different groups (forks can be counted alone, or as part of
a set of utensils).

543F924D82594344B3CA461DF8086739.description:
Match numerals 1-10 to sets of objects, with guidance
and support.

6A13228DCABC464CA15BBD5CC6EE87E7.description:
Recognize numerals up to 10 and attempt to write them or
number-like forms during play and daily activities.

2A4F4BF468C84819A10EA19C7ADA7BF8.description:
Count up to 10 objects arranged in a line using oneto-one correspondence with increasing accuracy, and
answer the question “How many are there?”

AFA7AC89B6B34B6C82ECCC5F6E9D7EFF.description:
Count up to 10 objects in a variety of ways (for example,
left to right, right to left, in stacks, etc.).

4394C0387BCA4175915E266B06810E3F.description: Rote count to 20 with increasing accuracy.

D705C8F0E0B14AC081F03214FDADC6FA.description:
Show an understanding of magnitude by recognizing
larger sets when compared to smaller sets and describe
how they are different.

B391E786CE654992A15F2CA08BC8EC35.description:
Compare the amount of items in small sets of objects
(up to 5 objects) by matching or counting and use
language such as “more than” and “less than” to describe
the sets of objects.

57833764FF444F3094263F95D5E3276B.description:
Write numerals or numberlike forms up to 5 during play
and daily activities.

AED81F8E6CA745C8A24C0DF5AE684A33.description:
Match numerals 1-5 to sets
of objects, with guidance and
support.

F4437F59DB5048FEA3442758A91CB624.description:
Recognize numerals up
to 5 during play and daily
activities.

C499326999E2480C924CB65792434D9D.description:
Count up to 5 objects
arranged in a line using
one-to-one correspondence
with increasing accuracy and
answer the question, “How
many are there?”

B6A7B34D14234B838D8B1319270E3532.description:
Rote count to 10 with
increasing accuracy.

7538207DEE284D20815AA2FD8D9354F5.description:
Visually compare two
groups of objects that are
obviously equal or unequal
in quantity and communicate
that they are the same or
different, and, if appropriate,
which one has more and/
or which one has less. (If
child is offered two plates
of crackers can select the
preferred amount and can
explain that he wanted more
or less).

562045E8260F467E8765ABF53026A3F3.description:
Make a small group (1-3) with the
same number of items as another
group of items (take 3 balls from
a basket after the teacher shows
the group that she has 3 balls and
asks each person to take the same
number of balls)

B739592C96EC4944BFFE482DF37FC4D5.description:
Place items in one-to-one
correspondence during play and daily
routines (one spoon at each plate;
one doll in each toy car).

EAFFB4DB0795496AA6E91E8B190064A6.description:
Attempt to chant or recite numbers,
but not necessarily in the correct
order (for example, counting objects
on a page during a read aloud).

A1C8863AAC7C4D9C8587606B5DD0F8FC.description:
Recognize when presented with
two obviously unequal sets of objects
that one set has more than the other
and/or that one set has less than
the other. (Can point to which set of
crayons has more or less depending
on what is asked).

836C95B63FF945E7BC47226A77C6B060.description:
Use words or actions that show
understanding of the concepts of
“more,” “all,” and/or “none” (ask for
more food, stop asking for more
blocks when told they have “all” of
the blocks, become upset when told
there is no more Play-Doh®).

AED12925CA8941F88A0EE1E4B89123E7.description:
Recognize
when presented
with two
obviously
unequal sets of
objects that one
set has more
or less than the
other (Can point
to which set of
crayons has
more).

05B5710E31B24FCE9B8D8113C556E798.description:
Use words or
actions that show
understanding of
the concepts of
“more,” “less,”
and “all” (ask for
more food, stop
asking for more
blocks when told
they have “all”
of the blocks).

EF8AB4C5708C44C895F9EAF33EA2B8DD.description:
Explore quantity
(for example,
filling and
dumping
containers).

30651570D5244D4AB219E01C276B9239.description:
Show interest
(look at or
reach for)
in obvious
differences in
quantity (look
at a tower with
7 blocks longer
than a tower
with 3 blocks,
reach for a
basket with
three balls
rather than a
basket with one
ball).

C9432D2D38BA46C29D81F68D58157BEA.description:
Indicate they
want “more”
with signs,
sounds, or
looks.

4F3FE6D5C3B1431EAF853C1B1FB9C4DC.description: Children demonstrate a beginning understanding of numbers and quantity during play and other activities.

document.title: South Carolina Early Learning Standards

387C08E677964532A4D2C284C22B17F8.description:
